author: sigros02
body:
`tailscale serve --tcp=<port>` is documented as raw TCP forwarding but in practice terminates TLS at the tailnet edge using the node's MagicDNS certificate, forcing clients into `.ts.net` FQDNs or cert-verify opt-outs. That contradicts the sidecar contract's "plain HTTP over the already-encrypted tailnet" guarantee and made Roster carry a TLS-verify workaround. Switching to `--http=<port>` exposes the backend as real HTTP on the tailnet — WireGuard still encrypts every hop and the bearer token still authorizes, so the security posture is unchanged.

User-facing URL (`http://<tsHostname>:<port>`), port, and contract are unchanged. Documents updated: the co-owned sidecar contract (§2 transport bullet, §10 sub-decision #1), ARCHITECTURE.md (sidecar property table, network-flow diagram, new 2026-05-15 decision entry), HANDOFF.md (Risk 12), CLAUDE.md, and docs/secrets-guide.md.

Closes #6

author: effortlesssteven
body:
### Motivation

- Reduce the size and complexity of the long `src/cli.rs` file by extracting separate responsibilities into single-purpose modules so the top-level CLI remains a small parser/dispatcher. 
- Centralize JSON emission, terminal styling, and project/template command logic to improve SRP boundaries and make testing and review easier. 
- Fix a small correctness/compile annoyance by adding equality derives to the `DriftPair` type used in lock drift comparisons. 
- Improve deterministic ordering of redaction patterns to satisfy lints and ensure stable behavior.

### Description

- Split CLI internals into four new modules under `src/cli/`: `json.rs` (canonical JCS emitters), `style.rs` (TTY/color helpers), `project.rs` (workspace/project commands, status/history helpers), and `template.rs` (template commands and validation). The top-level `src/cli.rs` remains the argument parser and dispatcher and now imports these helpers. 
- Moved `emit_*` JSON helper functions out of `src/cli.rs` into `src/cli/json.rs` and updated call sites to use the centralized emitters. 
- Moved terminal styling helpers (color detection and styled output) into `src/cli/style.rs` and updated call sites to import `styled_check`, `styled_info`, `styled_success`, and `styled_warning`. 
- Moved project/workspace command implementations (status aggregation, history, spec-status derivation, pending fixup counting, TUI invocation) into `src/cli/project.rs` and exposed a minimal set of helpers used by `cli.rs`. 
- Moved template command handling into `src/cli/template.rs`. 
- Added `#[derive(PartialEq, Eq)]` to `DriftPair` so `FlowLockDrift` can derive equality without error. 
- Replaced an explicit closure `sort_by(|(id1, _), (id2, _)| id1.cmp(id2))` with `sort_by_key(|(id, _)| *id)` in `crates/xchecker-redaction/src/lib.rs` to satisfy clippy and ensure deterministic ordering. 
- Minor formatting/whitespace cleanups where code was moved.

### Testing

- Ran unit and integration test suite: `cargo test --workspace --lib --bins` — all tests passed. 
- Ran formatting check: `cargo fmt -- --check` — passed. 
- Ran linter: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — currently fails on an existing `unnecessary_sort_by` clippy finding in `crates/xchecker-receipt/src/writer.rs` (pre-existing unrelated location); the PR fixes clippy findings introduced by the refactor but the repository still contains that outstanding lint.

body:
## Summary

- Adds a build-generated validation-status dashboard at `docs/website/status/validation.md` aggregating every ADR + reference doc's `validation:` block (ADR 0056). Surfaces status summary, evidence-kind cross-tab, V0/V8 extractor findings, and per-contract listing grouped ADRs vs reference docs.
- Emits via `@sophie/astro`'s `pagefind-postbuild.ts` hook **next to** `writePedagogyIndexJson` (PR #47), consuming the same in-memory `indexAccumulator.asPedagogyIndex()` snapshot — one extraction pass, two outputs, no JSON disk round-trip.
- Suppressed when `SOPHIE_DOCS_INCLUDE_VALIDATION=0`, symmetric with PR #50's admonition gate. Also no-ops when `docs/website/status/` is absent (consumer repos without the sophie docs tree, e.g. the smoke fixture's build root).
- Registers `status/validation.md` in `myst.yml` with `tags: [private]` in frontmatter (PR 6 will add the `excludeTagged: [private]` MyST config to hide it from public builds).

## Design notes (locked by the canonical plan)

- **In-memory snapshot consumption** vs the rejected "re-read pedagogy-index.json" alternative — keeps PR 5 conceptually paired with PR #47 (`6821b11`); avoids the disk round-trip.
- **Pure function + thin wrapper**: `generateValidationIndex(index)` returns the Markdown body and is exhaustively unit-tested; `writeValidationIndexMarkdown(index, sophieRoot)` handles env-flag check + I/O.
- **`process.cwd()` as `sophieRoot`** matches the existing `repoRoot` resolution in `TextbookLayout.astro`'s `extractContractValidations` call (PR 3 of ADR 0056), so the two sites resolve identically.
- **Generated-source vs hand-authored convention**: existing `status/*.md` files are hand-authored. `status/validation.md` introduces a "build-generated source" convention (file is checked in so MyST sees it; overwritten on every build). Header banner + frontmatter description flag this clearly.

## I2 extension decision (PR #50 reviewer's "every ADR carries a validation-* class")

**Deferred to PR 6.** PR 6 already requires a full docs build for the curated initial-pass verification on ~20-25 ADRs; that assertion belongs with the curated-pass change. Adding it to PR 5 would mix concerns (index-page generation vs admonition coverage). PR 5's testing is the generator unit tests (13 cases) + smoke build verification + end-to-end spot-check (78 contracts extracted, MyST renders the page to HTML).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` — clean (lockfile in sync).
- [x] `pnpm turbo run typecheck` — 11/11 successful, 0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 hints.
- [x] `pnpm turbo run test:unit` — 9/9 packages green; +13 tests in `@sophie/astro` (9 generator + 4 writer).
- [x] `pnpm turbo run build --filter=@sophie/astro --filter=smoke` — smoke build green; writer correctly no-ops on `cwd=examples/smoke/` (no `docs/website/status/` there).
- [x] End-to-end spot-check (script ran with `cwd=sophie-root`): 78 contract entries + 0 V0/V8 findings extracted; `docs/website/status/validation.md` overwritten with realistic content.
- [x] `cd docs/website && SOPHIE_DOCS_INCLUDE_VALIDATION=1 npx mystmd build --html` — page rendered to `_build/html/validation/index.html` and `_build/site/content/validation.json` (frontmatter `tags: ["private"]` round-trips through MyST as expected).

- [x] `pnpm exec biome check packages/ docs/website/myst.yml docs/website/status/validation.md` — 0 errors, 0 warnings across 321 files checked.

author: valenlanzillotta
body:
## Descripcion

Agrega la pantalla "FIUBA Plan" al drawer de alumno. Carga el bundle de FIUBA-Plan localmente y le inyecta automáticamente los horarios del cuatrimestre actual obtenidos del SIU Guaraní, sin que el alumno tenga que copiar y pegar nada.

## Como funciona

Al abrir la pantalla, LUDO hace un request al backend para obtener las comisiones del cuatrimestre actual desde Guaraní. Las comisiones se transforman al formato interno de FIUBA-Plan (`guaraniToHorariosSIU`) y se inyectan en cuanto tanto los datos como el iframe/WebView están listos.

El handshake entre LUDO y FIUBA-Plan funciona así:
- FIUBA-Plan envía `LUDO_PLAN_READY` cuando su React monta
- LUDO responde con `LUDO_PLAN_INIT` llevando el payload de horarios
- En mobile, como alternativa al postMessage, los datos se inyectan directamente con `injectJavaScript` y `window.__LUDO_PLAN_DATA__`

En mobile se inyecta además `window.__LUDO_EMBEDDED__ = true` antes de que cargue la página (via `injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded`) para que FIUBA-Plan detecte el contexto LUDO de forma confiable.

Si el fetch a Guaraní falla (VPN no disponible, timeout, etc.), se muestra un banner de error y FIUBA-Plan queda accesible para cargar horarios manualmente como fallback. El backend tiene configurado un timeout de 30s en las llamadas al SIU para evitar requests colgadas.

## Cambios

- `src/scenes/fiuba_plan/index.tsx`: pantalla mobile con WebView, inyección de datos vía `injectJavaScript`, flag `__LUDO_EMBEDDED__`, banner de error
- `src/scenes/fiuba_plan/index.web.tsx`: versión web con iframe, handshake `LUDO_PLAN_READY` / `LUDO_PLAN_INIT`, banner de error
- `src/scenes/fiuba_plan/guaraniTransformer.ts`: transforma comisiones del SIU al formato de FIUBA-Plan; normaliza días con/sin acento, agrupa por materia, extrae periodo del cuatrimestre
- `src/repositories/guarani.ts` + `src/repositories/index.ts`: repositorio para el endpoint de oferta de comisiones
- `src/scenes/root_drawer/config/menu_config.ts`: agrega "FIUBA Plan" al submenu Académico del alumno (mobile y web)
- `src/scenes/root_drawer/index.web.tsx`: registra `FiubaPlanScreen` en el drawer web
- `App.tsx`: registra `FiubaPlan` como Stack.Screen
- `public/fiuba-plan/`: bundle estático de FIUBA-Plan para servir en web (mismo patrón que FIUBA-Map)
- `package.json`: agrega `react-native-webview`

## Tests

Tests unitarios del transformer en `__tests__/guaraniTransformer.test.ts`. Cubren: días con y sin acento en mayúsculas y minúsculas, comisiones sin horarios, agrupación por materia, formateo de docentes con campos faltantes, fallbacks de campos del API, lectura del periodo lectivo desde la respuesta del SIU.

## Cómo probar

Requiere estar conectado a la VPN del SIU.

- Web: npm run web
- Android: npm run android

Los bundles de FIUBA-Map y FIUBA-Plan están incluidos en el repo, por lo que no hace falta tener esos repos clonados para correr la app.

> `npm run android:sync` — solo necesario si querés reconstruir los bundles después de hacer cambios en `../FIUBA-Map` o `../FIUBA-Plan`. 
> Requiere tener ambos repos clonados localmente.

Al entrar a la pantalla FIUBA Plan, los horarios de todas las comisiones disponibles en el periodo actual se cargan automáticamente desde el SIU. Si la VPN no está disponible, se muestra un banner de error y podés cargar los horarios manualmente usando el parser del SIU (flujo original de FIUBA-Plan).

closes https://github.com/LUDO3-FIUBA/.github/issues/9

author: longhuynh4825
body:
The current implementation of `download_mail_attachments` in `ImapHook` silently overwrites files if they already exist in the target directory. This can lead to data loss when multiple emails have attachments with the same filename.

This PR adds a configurable `overwrite` parameter (defaulting to `True` for backward compatibility) to `download_mail_attachments`. When set to `False`, the hook will automatically rename files by appending a numeric suffix (e.g., `report (1).csv`) if a collision is detected.

Summary:
- Added `overwrite` parameter to `download_mail_attachments`.
- Implemented `_resolve_non_conflicting_path` helper to handle filename collisions.
- Added comprehensive unit tests for both overwrite and collision-avoidance scenarios.
- Updated the IMAP provider changelog.

author: danmestas
body:
## Summary

- `orch-spawn --verify`'s banner-match path calls `tmux capture-pane | grep -qF "$BANNER"`. When pane width wraps the banner mid-substring (observed at width=42 with `Claude Code v0 (test banner)` wrapping as `Claude Cod\ne v0...`), `grep -F` misses and verify falls through to timeout though the agent is actually up.
- Fix: add `-J` to capture-pane in both production (`bin/orch-spawn`) and the regression test (`test/test-orch-spawn-verify.sh`). `tmux capture-pane -J` joins wrapped lines, restoring substring continuity.

## Repro before fix

```sh
$ bash test/test-orch-spawn-verify.sh
...
FAIL  banner-match: capture-pane | grep -qF 'Claude Code' matches
        expected: found
        got:      missing
Results: 9 passed, 1 failed
```

Reproduced identically on `main` before this branch — pre-existing, not introduced here.

## After fix

```
Results: 10 passed, 0 failed
```

## Why this matters in production

Same `tmux capture-pane | grep -qF` pattern lives in `bin/orch-spawn:351` as the verify-readiness signal. Narrow panes (split into a 3-column tmux layout, dense status bars, etc.) trigger the wrap. Workers verify-time-out → caller emits "agent failed to start" → operator thinks the spawn died when it didn't.

## Test plan

- [x] `test-orch-spawn-verify.sh` 10/10 locally
- [x] shellcheck clean on both touched files
- [ ] Confirm CI green

author: morganmcg1
body:
## Hypothesis

PhysicsAttention is the core of Transolver. It projects N mesh nodes into `slice_num` learnable physics tokens via soft membership assignment, then runs O(slice_num²) self-attention in that reduced space. With **slice_num=64**, the model has 64 physics "slots" to jointly represent:
- wake region (downstream)
- boundary layer (each foil)
- pressure side / suction side (each foil)
- inter-foil gap (the geometric coupling region)
- far-field
- ...across two distinct foil geometries at varying gaps and stagger angles.

That's a lot to compress into 64 tokens. Doubling to **slice_num=128** increases the attention space by 4× (128²/64² = 4) while leaving depth (n_layers=5), hidden dim (128), and all training settings unchanged.

This is the **architecture-capacity axis along the token count dimension**. It is orthogonal to fern's depth-sweep (which varies n_layers at slice_num=64) — capacity-via-tokens vs capacity-via-depth are different scaling axes. Both could win, both could lose, or one could win and the other lose.

## Instructions

1. **First check whether `--slice_num` is already a CLI argument** in `train.py`:
   ```bash
   grep -n slice_num target/train.py target/transolver.py 2>/dev/null
   ```
   - If it's in Config as a flag, just use it directly.
   - If it's hardcoded (e.g. `slice_num=64` in the model constructor), add it to Config:
     ```python
     slice_num: int = 64  # Transolver physics tokens; baseline 64
     ```
     then thread `cfg.slice_num` into the `Transolver(...)` constructor call. Both the live model AND `copy.deepcopy(model)` for EMA will pick this up automatically — no manual EMA changes needed.

2. **Stay on the merged EMA+clip+Huber+decay=0.99 baseline** — do NOT touch `grad_clip`, `huber_delta`, `ema_decay`, `n_layers`, or `n_hidden`.

3. **Run 1 primary arm + 1 conditional arm**:
   - Arm A (primary): `--slice_num 128`
   - Arm B (only if Arm A wins, time permitting): `--slice_num 256`

4. **Log diagnostics**:
   - `train/wall_time_per_epoch` — confirms epochs-per-budget didn't drop too much
   - `train/peak_gpu_mb` from `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` — VRAM should still be well under 96GB

### Reproduce command (each arm)

```bash
cd target/ && python train.py \
  --grad_clip 5.0 \
  --huber_delta 1.0 \
  --ema_decay 0.99 \
  --slice_num <128|256> \
  --wandb_group slice-num-sweep \
  --wandb_name slice-num-<value> \
  --agent willowpai2i48h2-tanjiro
```

Submit ONE terminal SENPAI-RESULT covering Arm A (and Arm B if run) with the best `val_avg/mae_surf_p` AND `test_avg/mae_surf_p` (3-split mean).

## Current baseline (PR #3474 — alphonse fast EMA decay=0.99)

- `val_avg/mae_surf_p` = **90.6131** (run `fzrq04xr`)
- `test_avg/mae_surf_p` (3 valid splits; cruise=NaN) = **88.8252**
- Per-split val: 106.135 | 99.466 | 70.358 | 86.494
- Reproduce: `python train.py --grad_clip 5.0 --huber_delta 1.0 --ema_decay 0.99 --agent <student>`
- Model config (do NOT change anything except slice_num): `n_hidden=128, n_layers=5, n_head=4, slice_num=64, mlp_ratio=2`

## Expected outcome

If capacity is binding along the token-count axis, expected `val_avg/mae_surf_p` ∈ [85, 90]. The boundary-layer + wake + inter-foil regions may benefit most from more tokens.

If `slice_num=128` is marginal (val_avg ∈ [90, 92]), the architecture may still win at full 50-epoch budget but isn't worth the wall-clock cost within 14 epochs. Report this clearly.

If `slice_num=128` clearly regresses (val_avg > 93), the answer is no — 14 epochs isn't enough to train the larger token space. Try `slice_num=256` only if 128 is at least competitive.

## Risk notes

- **VRAM**: At slice_num=128 with batch=4 and 242K nodes max, the attention matrix [128, 128] is tiny (~64KB per head), but the membership projection [N, 128] grows linearly with N (~120MB at 242K nodes). Total still well within 96GB. Verify `peak_gpu_mb` < 80000 on the largest split. If OOM unexpectedly, drop batch_size to 2 (and report this).
- **Wall-clock**: each forward pass touches slice_num² attention. 128² is 4× 64², but slice_num attention is a tiny fraction of total compute (the N×N membership is dominant). Expect ~5-10% slower per epoch, so ~12-13 epochs in the 30-min budget instead of 14. The trade-off: more capacity vs slightly fewer optimizer steps. Track both.
- **EMA**: shadow model picks up the new slice_num via `copy.deepcopy(model)` — no manual EMA-init change needed.
- **Evaluation**: test-time eval uses EMA shadow — confirm no hardcoded `slice_num=64` in evaluate_split or in checkpoint loading.

## Sanity check before launching

Run `--debug` (3 epochs) at `--slice_num 128` to confirm:
1. Model fits in VRAM
2. EMA shadow has matching architecture
3. Forward + backward pass works on the largest val split (camber_cruise, 242K nodes)
4. Loss decreases over the 3 debug epochs

Then kick off the real arm.

## Summary

Adds a new **Fluency** game mode to MindSprint — a rapid-fire arithmetic drill where players answer as many questions as possible within a countdown timer.

## Changes

### New files
- `src/app/pages/game-mode/fluency/fluency.engine.ts` — Self-contained engine using Angular signals. Generates arithmetic questions (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) scaled by difficulty, runs a 100 ms countdown tick, tracks score, streak, accuracy, and emits game-over state.
- `src/app/pages/game-mode/fluency/fluency.component.ts` — Standalone Angular component `<app-fluency-mode>` with on-screen keypad, keyboard input support, and a `(nextChallenge)` output event.
- `src/app/pages/game-mode/fluency/fluency.html` — Template with a colour-coded timer bar, large question display with enter/exit animations, per-question correct/incorrect feedback, game-over summary (score, correct count, accuracy %), and a "Next Challenge" button.
- `src/app/pages/game-mode/fluency/fluency.css` — CSS with timer urgency colours (green → amber → pulsing red), feedback state transitions, keypad styling, and `prefers-reduced-motion` support.

### Modified files
- `src/app/services/game.service.ts` — Added `FluencyPayload` interface (`difficulty`, `timeLimitSeconds`, `operations`, etc.).
- `src/app/pages/game-mode/game-mode.ts`:
  - Added `'fluency'` to `SuperGameMode` union type (replaces legacy `'fluency-speed'` placeholder).
  - Added `fluencyEngine` instance and import of `FluencyModeComponent`/`FluencyEngine`.
  - Added `getFluencyPayload()` extractor (reads `difficulty` + `timeLimitSeconds` from challenge, falls back to `challenge.timeLimitSeconds`).
  - Engine is configured and started inside `loadChallenge()` on challenge response; stopped in `stopModeEngines()` and `ngOnDestroy`.
  - Updated `toApiMode()`, `isSuperMode()`, `superModeInfo()`, `shouldShowGenericNextChallenge()` for the new mode.
  - Updated mode selector list — `fluency-speed` (legacy alias) replaced by `fluency`.
- `src/app/pages/game-mode/game-mode.html`:
  - Added `<app-fluency-mode>` block bound to `fluencyEngine` with `(nextChallenge)="loadChallenge()"`.
  - Removed `fluency-speed` from the abacus-flash `@if` condition.

## Integration points
- **Adaptive difficulty** — initial `difficulty` is sourced from the backend challenge payload (same adaptive system as other modes).
- **Streak system** — engine tracks its own streak; the super-mode badge (⚡ Fluency Champion) is awarded on the next correct `submitChallenge` call.
- **XP rewards** — awarded via `submitChallenge()` triggered by the parent template's existing reward flow.
- **Next challenge flow** — component emits `nextChallenge` → parent calls `loadChallenge()`, consistent with ai-puzzle pattern.

author: mikestahp
body:
💡 **What:** Added an `emptyDescriptorSets` cache map to `Vulkanite.java` and replaced the per-frame `allocateSet()` calls in `RenderPassExecutor` with `getEmptySet()`.

🎯 **Why:** In `RenderPassExecutor.execute()`, the rendering loop was allocating and freeing new empty descriptor sets from the descriptor pools *every frame* to fill gaps in the layout array. This caused unnecessary memory allocations, descriptor pool fragmentation, and general overhead.

📊 **Impact:** Reduces per-frame object allocations and Vulkan descriptor set allocations (`vkAllocateDescriptorSets`) significantly when processing layouts with gaps. 

🔬 **Measurement:** Compile with `./gradlew build -x test`. Run a profiler (like VisualVM or a built-in rendering metric) and observe reduced memory churn and lower overhead in the `vulkanite_encode_rt_passes` rendering phase.

author: natsukium
body:
## Summary

- Extract the Plan role (read-only) and Apply role (read/write) definitions from `infra/global/oidc/main.tf` into dedicated `iam-plan.tf` and `iam-apply.tf` files.
- `main.tf` retains the `terraform { backend ... }` block, the AWS provider, the GitHub OIDC IdP resource, the shared `locals` (`oidc_provider_arn`, `aud_condition`), and the two role ARN outputs.

## Why

The OIDC stack is the one place in this repo where a single Terraform state holds two intentionally distinct permission boundaries: a Plan role used by PR plans (read-only on `tfstate`) and an Apply role used by main pushes (read/write on `tfstate`). When both roles live in the same file, a reviewer auditing a change to one inevitably scrolls past the other, which weakens the per-role audit boundary that exists for exactly this kind of review.

By splitting per role, a diff that touches Plan permissions (or expands its `sub` allowlist, etc.) shows up in `iam-plan.tf` only, and the Apply role is untouched in the PR — and vice versa. This is exactly the granularity that justified the split in the very first place.

The other stacks (`global/state/`, `global/domains/`, `services/github/`, `services/hydra/`, `services/nix-builder/`) remain single-file because none of them contain comparable internal permission boundaries that would benefit from per-file separation. Splitting them for the sake of splitting would be cosmetic, not semantic.

## State

Resource addresses (`aws_iam_role.plan`, `aws_iam_role.apply`, `aws_iam_policy.tfstate_{read,write}`, `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.{plan,apply}_tfstate`) are unchanged, so this is a pure file reorganization. Verified locally:

\`\`\`
$ cd infra/global/oidc && terraform plan
No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.
\`\`\`

## Test plan

- [ ] `terraform fmt -recursive -check infra/` passes
- [ ] Local `terraform plan` in `infra/global/oidc/` reports no changes
- [ ] CI workflow: `terraform` job is skipped (no path filter matches `infra/global/oidc/**`)
- [ ] After merge, no apply step is required — file moves don't touch state

author: erickgrau
body:
<!-- This PR closes no GitHub issue: issues are disabled on this repo. -->

## Why

**Use case:** Follow-up to the "Adjacent issues" note on PR #1 (Claude Design ZIP import silent-failure fix). That PR fixed the client; this fixes the daemon defect it surfaced.

**Pain:** `POST /api/import/claude-design` mounted `importUpload.single('file')` as bare middleware with no error handler. A `MulterError` raised by that middleware — an oversize zip past the 100 MB `fileSize` limit, an unexpected field name, etc. — is thrown *before* the route handler runs, so the handler's own `try/catch` never sees it. The error fell through to Express' default error handler, which replies with an **HTML 500 page** instead of the JSON error envelope every other daemon route returns. A client parsing the response as JSON gets a parse failure rather than an actionable reason.

The sibling project-upload route already does this correctly: `handleProjectUpload` wraps `projectUpload.array(...)` and funnels errors through `sendMulterError`. The import route was simply never given the equivalent wrapper.

## What users will see

No visible UI change. A failed Claude Design ZIP import caused by a multer-level rejection (file too large, malformed multipart) now produces a structured error the web client can render in its import-error Toast (added in PR #1) — e.g. "file too large" with a 413 — instead of a generic failure. Successful imports are unchanged.

## Surface area

- [ ] **UI**
- [ ] **Keyboard shortcut**
- [ ] **CLI / env var**
- [x] **API / contract** — `POST /api/import/claude-design` now returns the standard `{ error: { message, code } }` envelope for multer-level failures (oversize/malformed uploads) instead of an HTML 500. No request-shape or success-response change.
- [ ] **Extension point**
- [ ] **i18n keys**
- [ ] **New top-level dependency**
- [ ] **Default behavior change**
- [ ] **None**

## Bug fix verification

- Test path: `apps/daemon/tests/claude-design-import-route.test.ts`
- Did the test go red on `main` and green on this branch? **yes** — red on `main` (`expected 500 to be 400`; HTML body), green on this branch (structured JSON 400, `error.code === 'BAD_REQUEST'`, `error.message` "unexpected file field").
- The spec posts a file under an unexpected field name — a cheap, deterministic `LIMIT_UNEXPECTED_FILE` trigger — rather than uploading a >100 MB file to exercise `LIMIT_FILE_SIZE`. `sendMulterError` maps every `MulterError` code, so one representative code proves the wiring; `LIMIT_FILE_SIZE` → 413 is covered by that same shared mapper.

## Validation

- `pnpm guard` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @open-design/daemon typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm --filter @open-design/daemon` vitest on `claude-design-import-route`, `claude-design-import`, `folder-import-route` — 20/20 pass
- Pre-existing baseline failure in `project-watchers.test.ts` (real-chokidar watch-event timing) is unrelated — fails on `main` before this change; untouched here.

author: andrew-bierman
body:
### Motivation
- The repository lint baseline (`biome`) is set to allow up to 2 parameters, but the team wants to tighten style to prefer a single typed object parameter for first-party code. 
- Introduce a stricter, repo-specific check to enforce a one-parameter rule while avoiding noise from callbacks and third-party code. 
- Provide an explicit opt-out when multiple parameters are genuinely required to make incremental migration feasible.

### Description
- Added a new custom check script `packages/checks/src/check-max-params.ts` which scans `apps/` and `packages/` TypeScript files and reports any function-like node with more than one parameter.  
- The checker ignores common test/build/generated paths, excludes `node_modules`/dist/build, and treats callbacks passed directly into call expressions as non-violations to reduce false positives.  
- Introduced an escape hatch annotation `@allow-multi-param` that can be placed on a leading comment to exempt specific functions.  
- Wired the new script into npm scripts: added `check:max-params` to `packages/checks/package.json` and a root-level `check:max-params` and appended it to the `lint:custom` pipeline in the root `package.json` while leaving Biome's `useMaxParams` at `max: 2` as the baseline.

### Testing
- Ran `bunx biome format --write packages/checks/src/check-max-params.ts` which formatted the new file successfully.  
- Ran `biome check --no-errors-on-unmatched` against the changed files as part of the pre-commit hook which succeeded after formatting.  
- Ran `bun run --cwd packages/checks check:max-params` which intentionally failed because it reported existing multi-parameter functions in first-party code (this is expected and indicates the check is detecting current violations).

  - `<version>-llm-opencode` — opencode CLI bundled (was `-llm`, renamed)
  - `<version>-llm` — backward-compatible alias for `-llm-opencode` (no deployment changes required)
  - `<version>-llm-ollama` — ollama binary only (v0.9.0); daemon runs externally at `OLLAMA_HOST`
  - `<version>-llm-aider` — aider-chat v0.82.2 via pipx at `/usr/local/bin/aider`

- **Dockerfile**: extracted shared `llm-base` stage (debian:12-slim + tini PID 1 + nonroot uid 65532 + ca-certs + git) consumed by all three LLM targets. Eliminates the duplicated apt+user setup that was in the old `runtime-adapters-llm` stage.

- **Helm**: `llm.enabled` (bool) → `llm.target` (enum: `""` / `"opencode"` / `"ollama"` / `"aider"`). Migration: `llm.enabled: true` → `llm.target: opencode` + `image.tag: <ver>-llm-opencode`. `OLLAMA_HOST` env var injected for ollama target. `secrets.aiderEnv` Secret rendered for aider target. `auth.json` and opencode ConfigMap mounts scoped strictly to `llm.target="opencode"`.

- **CI**: `build-llm-image` → `build-images` matrix (3 targets × 2 platforms = 6 parallel legs, `fail-fast: false`). Pushes to ghcr.io on `main`; PR runs are build-only (no push). GHA cache scoped per target+platform.

## Helm migration path (llm.enabled → llm.target)

```yaml
# Before
llm:
  enabled: true
image:
  tag: "0.1.0-llm"

# After (opencode — functionally identical, old -llm tag still works)
llm:
  target: opencode
image:
  tag: "0.1.0-llm-opencode"   # or keep "0.1.0-llm" (alias image)

# Ollama
llm:
  target: ollama
  ollamaHost: "http://ollama.ollama.svc.cluster.local:11434"
image:
  tag: "0.1.0-llm-ollama"

# Aider
llm:
  target: aider
secrets:
  aiderEnv:
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: "sk-ant-..."
image:
  tag: "0.1.0-llm-aider"
```

## Test plan

- [x] `docker buildx build --target=runtime-adapters --load .` — passes (cached, distroless)
- [x] `docker buildx build --target=runtime-adapters-llm-opencode --load .` — passes
- [x] `docker buildx build --target=runtime-adapters-llm-ollama --load .` — passes; ollama 0.9.0 binary verified (`ollama --version`)
- [x] `docker buildx build --target=runtime-adapters-llm-aider --load .` — passes; aider 0.82.2 verified (`aider --version`)
- [ ] CI matrix (6 legs) — verify green in this PR
- [ ] Helm `helm template` with each `llm.target` value renders expected resources

author: leaanthony
body:
Fixes #5459.

For v3.0.0 GA, **GTK4 + WebKitGTK 6.0 becomes the default Linux build stack.** GTK3 + WebKit2GTK 4.1 becomes a legacy opt-in via `-tags gtk3` for one v3 cycle and is scheduled for removal in v3.1. Rationale recorded in `IMPLEMENTATION.md` Decision 1.1.

## Summary of changes

| Area | What changed |
|------|---|
| **Build constraints** | 12 files in `v3/` renamed from `*_linux_gtk4.go` → `*_linux.go` (default), constraint `gtk4` → `!gtk3`. 10 files renamed from `*_linux.go` → `*_linux_gtk3.go` (legacy), constraint `!gtk4` → `gtk3`. The `gtk4` build tag is retired in favor of `gtk3` as the toggle. |
| **cgo C/H files** | `linux_cgo_gtk4.c`/`.h` → `linux_cgo.c`/`.h`. Build directives, `#include` directive, and header guards updated to match the new filename — these would have silently mismatched the cgo pair and produced link errors if missed. |
| **Doctor** | Legacy `internal/doctor/packagemanager/*.go` (7 files): inverted required/optional polarity. `pkg/doctor-ng/packagemanager/*.go` already had the correct polarity — left alone. |
| **CI** | `build-and-test-v3.yml`, `cross-compile-test-v3.yml`, `build-cross-image.yml`: both stacks installed; step labels renamed `GTK4 default` / `GTK3 legacy`; `BUILD_TAGS=gtk4` → `=gtk3`; `-tags gtk4` → `-tags gtk3`; library-presence test checks GTK4 SOs first. |
| **Taskfile** | `v3/Taskfile.yaml` rename `test:example:linux:gtk4` → `:gtk3`, `sanity:gtk4` → `:gtk3`, hints flipped. User-template Taskfiles unchanged (already pass `EXTRA_TAGS` generically). |
| **nfpm template** | `updatable_build_assets/linux/nfpm/nfpm.yaml.tmpl`: default runtime deps → `libgtk-4-1` / `libwebkitgtk-6.0-4`; RPM and Arch overrides updated; legacy deps shown commented out for users who build with `-tags gtk3`. All 7 example `nfpm.yaml` files bumped to match. |
| **Docs** | English canonical only (Crowdin sync handles i18n): `linux.mdx` "GTK4 Support (Experimental)" → "Legacy GTK3 Support"; `building.mdx`, `cli.mdx`, `dialogs.mdx`, `window.mdx`, both `installation.mdx`s, both `contributing/*.mdx`s updated. Anchor renames: `#gtk4-support-experimental` → `#legacy-gtk3-support`, `#linux-gtk4-limitations` → `#linux-dialog-behavior`. No orphaned inbound links. |
| **Tracking docs** | `IMPLEMENTATION.md` gets Decision 1.1 (2026-05-16); original Decision 1 preserved and marked SUPERSEDED. `AGENTS.md` policy section updated. |
| **Cleanup** | Removed `v3/test/manual/dialog/bin/file-*-gtk4*` and `message-*-gtk4*` test binaries committed during the original #4958 GTK4 dev work. |

## Reviewer hot-spots — please look here first

1. **The `-skip "TestService"` CI skip moved tracks.** Originally it was on the `-tags gtk4` opt-in step (display issues in CI). Since GTK4 is now default, the skip moves to the default-test step; the `-tags gtk3` legacy step now runs the full suite. See `.github/workflows/build-and-test-v3.yml` lines ~170-179.
2. **The "GTK4 EXPERIMENTAL" stdout banner is removed.** The `fmt.Println` block in `application_linux.go` `init()` printing the experimental box on every app startup is deleted — GTK4 is no longer experimental.
3. **Beyond-plan deletion of `message-*-gtk4*` binaries.** The original plan only mentioned `file-*-gtk4*`; I also removed the symmetric `message-*-gtk4*` binaries.
4. **`icon lookup not implemented for GTK4`** error rephrased to point users at `-tags gtk3` as the workaround, since this is now reachable on the default path.

## Verification status

| | Status |
|---|---|
| `go vet ./...` on darwin | ✅ Clean against this change. (Pre-existing JSON-tag / MarshalJSON issues in `internal/generator/testcases` are unrelated.) |
| Cross-vet `CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux` | Predictably fails — the package mixes cgo and non-cgo Linux files; same on master. |
| **Linux cgo build on a real host** | ❌ **Not done — required gate before merge.** Test on `lin-node1` (or any Linux box with `libgtk-4-dev libwebkitgtk-6.0-dev libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` installed). At minimum: `cd v3 && go build ./...` (default GTK4) and `cd v3 && go build -tags gtk3 ./...` (legacy). |
| nfpm runtime package names exist on target distros | ⚠️ Picked `libgtk-4-1` and `libwebkitgtk-6.0-4` for Debian/Ubuntu based on standard naming; please `apt-cache show libwebkitgtk-6.0-4` on `lin-node1` to confirm before the resulting `.deb` ships. If the actual package name differs, the generated package won't install. |

## Downstream packager migration paragraph (for `v3.0.0-beta.1` release notes)

> **Linux: default toolchain is now GTK4 + WebKitGTK 6.0.** Packagers for Flatpak, AUR, nixpkgs, Debian, Fedora, and other distributions should: **(1) drop `-tags gtk4` from any existing build invocations** — it is now a no-op. **(2) Replace build-time system dependencies** `libgtk-3-dev` / `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` with `libgtk-4-dev` / `libwebkitgtk-6.0-dev` (Debian/Ubuntu naming; equivalents: `gtk4-devel`/`webkitgtk6.0-devel` on Fedora; `gtk4`/`webkitgtk-6.0` on Arch). **(3) If you target a stable distribution that ships only GTK3** — Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Debian 12, Fedora 39 or older, RHEL 9.x — **add `-tags gtk3`** to your build command. The legacy path is supported through the v3.0.x line and scheduled for removal in v3.1; plan to migrate to GTK4 in coordination with your distribution's GTK4 / WebKitGTK 6.0 availability. The `wails3 doctor` and `wails3 doctor-ng` commands now report GTK4 as required and GTK3 as `(legacy)` optional; the `wails3 tool capabilities` JSON output is unchanged. No source code changes are required in Wails applications themselves.

## Out of scope

- Removal of the GTK3 code path entirely — that's v3.1 work.
- Smart-default auto-fallback in `wails3 build` (e.g. detect GTK3-only host and auto-inject `-tags gtk3`) — explicitly chosen against for consistency; users on a GTK3-only host get the bare `pkg-config webkitgtk-6.0` failure with a clear error pointing at `-tags gtk3`.
- Renaming the `gtk4-benchmark/` directory (kept by request — it's a dev tool that compares both stacks).
- i18n docs trees (`ja/`, `ru/`, `zh-cn/`, `pt/`, `zh-tw/`, `de/`, `ko/`, `fr/`) — will sync via Crowdin.
- v2 maintenance.

## Test plan
- [ ] On `lin-node1` (or equivalent): `cd v3 && go build ./...` succeeds (default GTK4) with `libgtk-4-dev libwebkitgtk-6.0-dev` installed
- [ ] On `lin-node1`: `cd v3 && go build -tags gtk3 ./...` succeeds with `libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` installed
- [ ] `wails3 doctor` reports GTK4/WebKitGTK 6.0 as required, GTK3/WebKit2GTK 4.1 as `(legacy)` optional
- [ ] `wails3 doctor-ng` polarity matches (unchanged file — sanity check)
- [ ] Build one example with `wails3 build` (default) and one with `wails3 build -tags gtk3`, run both
- [ ] Verify `apt-cache show libwebkitgtk-6.0-4` returns a real package on Ubuntu 24.04 / Debian 13 (otherwise adjust nfpm template runtime dep names)
- [ ] CI green for the v3 workflows on this PR

author: bloknayrb
body:
## Summary

Implements **ADR-031** (see #697): replace direct \`doc.transact(...)\` with five free-function helpers in \`src/shared/origins.ts\` — \`withMcp\`, \`withFileSync\`, \`withInternal\`, \`withReload\`, \`withBrowser\`. Every Y.Doc write — server-side and browser-side — now goes through one of the helpers. Raw \`*.transact(\` outside the helpers file is flagged by \`.claude/hooks/check-raw-transact.sh\`.

Skip-set matrix (channel / durable-sync / tombstone observers) is enforced via predicates \`shouldSkipChannel\` / \`shouldSkipDurableSync\` / \`shouldSkipTombstone\` instead of inline origin equality. The migration also widens skip sets to match the ADR contract: channel observers now skip \`internal\` and \`reload\` in addition to \`mcp\` and \`file-sync\`; the durable-sync observer skips \`internal\` in addition to \`file-sync\`.

Closes the silent-bug class where untagged setup writes (session restore, file population, tutorial seeding, server-internal metadata broadcasts, cleanup-after-failure paths, force-reload) compiled fine and avoided observer echo only by coincidence.

## Commit sequence (review in order)

1. **\`feat(origins): introduce 5 origin-tagged transaction wrappers\`** — \`src/shared/origins.ts\` foundation: constants, helpers, skip-set predicates, \`transactForTest\`. Unit tests at \`tests/shared/origins.test.ts\`. \`src/server/events/origins.ts\` becomes a thin re-export for migration-window compatibility (PR 9 cleanup deletes it).
2. **\`refactor(origins): widen observer skip-sets via shared/origins predicates\`** — every channel observer (annotations / awareness / ctrl-chat / ctrl-meta / replies) and the durable-sync observer migrates from inline \`txn.origin === MCP_ORIGIN || txn.origin === FILE_SYNC_ORIGIN\` checks to predicates. The merge transact in \`loadAndMerge\` becomes \`withFileSync\`. **Behaviour today is unchanged** — \`internal\` / \`reload\` origins don't exist until callsites migrate in subsequent commits.
3. **\`refactor(origins): migrate small-fanin callsites\`** — positions (\`refreshAllRanges\` → \`withMcp\`), session manager chat-prune (→ \`withInternal\`), \`injectCommentsAsAnnotations\` (→ \`withInternal\`), tutorial seeding (→ \`withInternal\`).
4. **\`refactor(origins): migrate mcp/ callsites\`** — annotations, awareness, channel-routes, document, document-service. \`addReplyToAnnotation\`'s \`origin?: string\` parameter is replaced with \`wrap: (doc, fn) => void\` defaulting to \`withBrowser\`; MCP caller passes \`withMcp\`. \`document-service.ts\` metadata broadcasts migrate from "MCP_ORIGIN as a skip-set hack" to the structurally correct \`withInternal\`.
5. **\`refactor(origins): migrate file-opener + browser highlight-toggle\`** — 10 callsites in file-opener (\`withMcp\` / \`withInternal\` / \`withFileSync\` / \`withReload\` per audit), \`reloadFromDisk\` (both transacts) → \`withReload\`. Client highlight-toggle → \`withBrowser\`. Test assertions updated to match the new origin sequence.
6. **\`chore(hooks): add check-raw-transact.sh PostToolUse hook\`** — informational stderr warning when a new raw \`*.transact(\` is introduced in \`src/\` outside the helpers file.
7. **\`chore(agents): teach reviewers the ADR-031 five-origin model\`** — \`annotation-model-reviewer.md\` and \`crdt-reviewer.md\` prompts updated.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm test\` — **2125 tests pass** (4 skipped). Full vitest suite across server + client.
- [x] \`npm run typecheck\` — clean. No errors / warnings.
- [x] Origin helper unit tests (\`tests/shared/origins.test.ts\`) — 10/10 pass.
- [x] Per-file regression: \`tests/server/annotations/sync.test.ts\`, \`tests/server/event-queue.test.ts\`, \`tests/server/reload-from-disk-persistence.test.ts\`, \`tests/server/file-opener-transact-batching.test.ts\`, \`tests/server/file-opener-cleanup-on-failure.test.ts\`, \`tests/server/docx-comments.test.ts\`, \`tests/server/annotation-replies.test.ts\` — all green.
- [x] \`grep -nE \"(transact\(.*MCP_ORIGIN|transact\(.*FILE_SYNC_ORIGIN)\" src/\` — only doc-comment hits remain (cleaned up in PR 9).
- [ ] **Manual smoke** — open a \`.md\` file, accept/dismiss a Claude comment, write a chat message, modify a file on disk to trigger reload — verify channel events fire only for browser-origin writes.

## Sequencing notes

- Depends on #697 (ADR-031 docs) for the contract reference. Land #697 first; this PR's review-context resolves against the merged ADR.
- Audit material (39 \`doc.transact()\` callsites categorized) drove the per-file migration choices. The amendments to ADR-031 in #697 (enumerated \`withInternal\` worked examples) come from that audit.

## What this PR does NOT do

- Does not delete \`src/server/events/origins.ts\` — kept as a thin re-export for the migration window. **PR 9** (shim cleanup) deletes it after PR 6 lands.
- Does not add the Biome AST rule for dynamic-dispatch bypass detection. The grep-based hook catches the common case.
- Does not migrate \`MCP_ORIGIN\` / \`FILE_SYNC_ORIGIN\` mentions in doc comments — PR 9 sweeps those.

Refs ADR-031 (in #697).

## Summary
Rails' \`to_gid\` is an alias of \`to_global_id\` — both return a GlobalID instance. Trails inherited a divergence from GID-1 where \`toGid()\` returned the URI string while \`toGlobalId()\` returned the instance. Unify to match Rails.

author: morganmcg1
body:
## Hypothesis

The input feature vector for each mesh node includes `log(Re)` as a **single scalar** (one float in the 24-channel input feature dim). A single scalar gives the model only ONE real-valued number to distinguish between Re=50K and Re=500K — the model must learn the mapping from this scalar to flow behavior entirely through depth and the input MLP.

**Sinusoidal positional embeddings** (as in vanilla Transformers, NeRF, Fourier Feature Networks) decompose the scalar into d frequencies:

```
embed[2k]   = sin(re_norm * 10000^(-2k/d))
embed[2k+1] = cos(re_norm * 10000^(-2k/d))
```

for k = 0 … d/2−1. Different frequency bands sensitize different attention heads to coarse (low-freq) vs fine (high-freq) Re-regime variations. This is exactly the same mechanism NeRF uses to overcome spectral bias on smooth functions.

**Why this should target `val_re_rand` specifically**: that split (currently 86.494) is the weakest OOD improvement from PR #3474 (just −0.2%). All other splits improved 0.2 to 9.7%. The cleanest mechanistic explanation: the model can't tell Re=200K from Re=400K well enough from a single log-scaled scalar in a 24-d feature vector — the signal is washed out.

This is **orthogonal** to everything in flight: it's a feature-representation change, not architecture (fern), optimization (alphonse), or loss (thorfinn, others).

## Instructions

1. **First, find where `log(Re)` enters the feature pipeline**:
   ```bash
   grep -n -i "re\|reynolds\|log_re" target/dataset.py target/loader.py target/train.py 2>/dev/null | head -20
   ```
   You're looking for the dataset's `__getitem__` (or wherever per-sample feature tensors are built). The channel containing `log(Re)` is one specific index in the 24-d input feature `x[..., :24]`.
   
   **Read-only files**: `data/scoring.py` and `data/loader.py` are READ-ONLY. The Re feature is likely already in the feature tensor as a single scalar — you'll inject the embedding either in (a) a custom Dataset wrapper around the existing loader, or (b) inside the training loop after fetching the batch, before passing to the model. **Option (b) is cleaner** — modify the batch in-place inside `train.py`'s training/validation loops.

2. **Add CLI flag**:
   ```python
   re_embed_dim: int = 1  # 1 = scalar (no change); 8 = 8-d sinusoidal embedding
   ```

3. **Implement the sinusoidal encoder** (place in train.py near the top):

   ```python
   def sinusoidal_re_embed(log_re, d=8, max_log=14.0):
       """
       log_re: [B, N] or [N] tensor (the existing log_re scalar feature)
       Returns: [..., d] tensor of sin/cos embeddings
       """
       re_norm = log_re / max_log  # normalize roughly to [0, 1]
       freqs = torch.pow(10000.0, -2.0 * torch.arange(d // 2, device=log_re.device) / d)
       args = re_norm.unsqueeze(-1) * freqs  # [..., d//2]
       return torch.cat([args.sin(), args.cos()], dim=-1)  # [..., d]
   ```

4. **Replace the Re scalar with the embedding inside the batch fetch loop**:

   ```python
   # After batch = next(iter(loader)); before model forward:
   x = batch['x']  # [B, N, 24]
   if cfg.re_embed_dim > 1:
       # The Re feature is at index <RE_IDX> — verify with grep above
       log_re = x[..., <RE_IDX>]  # [B, N]
       re_embed = sinusoidal_re_embed(log_re, d=cfg.re_embed_dim)  # [B, N, 8]
       # Concatenate: drop scalar log_re, append embedding
       x_other = torch.cat([x[..., :<RE_IDX>], x[..., <RE_IDX>+1:]], dim=-1)  # [B, N, 23]
       x = torch.cat([x_other, re_embed], dim=-1)  # [B, N, 23 + d]
   ```

5. **Update `fun_dim` passed to Transolver**: the input dim grows from 24 to (24 - 1 + d) = 31 when d=8. This must match the model's `fun_dim` or `input_dim` constructor arg.

   ```python
   input_dim = 24 - 1 + cfg.re_embed_dim if cfg.re_embed_dim > 1 else 24
   model = Transolver(..., fun_dim=input_dim, ...)
   ```

6. **Stay on the merged EMA+clip+Huber+decay=0.99 baseline** — do NOT touch `grad_clip`, `huber_delta`, `ema_decay`, or any architecture parameters.

7. **Run 1 arm**:
   - Arm A: `--re_embed_dim 8`

### Reproduce command

```bash
cd target/ && python train.py \
  --grad_clip 5.0 \
  --huber_delta 1.0 \
  --ema_decay 0.99 \
  --re_embed_dim 8 \
  --wandb_group re-sinusoidal-embed \
  --wandb_name re-sinusoidal-d8 \
  --agent willowpai2i48h2-frieren
```

Submit ONE terminal SENPAI-RESULT with the best `val_avg/mae_surf_p` AND `test_avg/mae_surf_p`, **PLUS report the per-split `val_re_rand`** — this is the split the hypothesis specifically targets.

## Current baseline (PR #3474 — alphonse fast EMA decay=0.99)

- `val_avg/mae_surf_p` = **90.6131** (run `fzrq04xr`)
- `test_avg/mae_surf_p` (3 valid splits; cruise=NaN) = **88.8252**
- Per-split val: 106.135 | 99.466 | 70.358 | **86.494 (val_re_rand — target this)**
- Reproduce: `python train.py --grad_clip 5.0 --huber_delta 1.0 --ema_decay 0.99 --agent <student>`

## Expected outcome

If the spectral-bias hypothesis is correct, expected `val_re_rand` < 84. `val_avg` should improve to ≤ 89 driven by val_re_rand alone.

If `val_re_rand` drops below 84 but `val_avg` is flat (because other splits regress slightly), this is **still a likely win** for the test_3split metric — the Re-rand split is a sentinel for OOD generalization that matters most for the paper.

If `val_re_rand` is flat at 86, the spectral-bias hypothesis is wrong on this dataset — the bottleneck is elsewhere. Close, no further variant.

## Risk notes

- **`max_log=14.0` is a guess** — verify the dataset's actual log(Re) range first:
  ```python
  # one-time sanity check before launching:
  loader = DataLoader(...); batch = next(iter(loader)); log_re = batch['x'][..., RE_IDX]
  print(log_re.min(), log_re.max(), log_re.mean())
  ```
  Pick `max_log` slightly above the observed max. If `max_log` is wrong, the high-frequency components of the embedding will alias or saturate.
- **Find the correct Re index**: grep the codebase. Common index conventions: x[..., 13] for log_Re, x[..., 12] for Re_raw, etc. **Print the feature column and confirm before launching** — wrong index would silently train on the wrong feature with no error.
- **`fun_dim` mismatch**: if any model constructor or evaluation function hardcodes `fun_dim=24`, you'll get a shape error. **Fast fail at first batch, not a silent bug** — this is good. Just fix and re-run.
- **EMA shadow**: `copy.deepcopy(model)` picks up the new fun_dim automatically.
- **Evaluation**: confirm `evaluate_split` and `test_eval` use the same batch-modification block, or the model will see scalar log_Re at eval time and crash.

## Sanity check before launching

Run `--debug` (3 epochs) at `--re_embed_dim 8`:
1. Print shapes: `x.shape` after batch modification should be `[B, N, 31]`
2. Print `re_embed.min(), .max()` — should be in [-1, 1] (sin/cos range)
3. Confirm loss decreases over 3 epochs
4. Confirm val pass runs (i.e. evaluate_split also applies the embedding)

Then kick off the real arm.

## Summary

- Port the `_MiliInternal.geometry` (`GeometricMeshInfo`: `compute_centroid`, `nearest_node`, `nearest_element`, `nodes_within_radius`, `elems_of_nodes`) and serial `AdjacencyMapping` (`mesh_entities_*`, `neighbor_elements`, `neighbor_nodes`, …) surfaces into the Rust core (new `mili_rs::adjacency`, `Superclass::node_connections`). Pure mesh/coordinate topology over the already parity-correct connectivity + `nodpos` query surface — no derived engine / projection / reductions.
- `milox.geometric_mesh_info` and the new `milox.adjacency` are thin upstream-API-compatible adapters; the serial `if not self.serial` dispatch collapses to identity. **Placement decision recorded in `m4.md`**: thin adapter delegating to core, per the architecture invariant (parity-sensitive value/topology lives in the Rust core).
- New `crates/mili-rs/tests/parity_adjacency.rs` — bit-exact vs the upstream `_MiliInternal.geometry` / `adjacency.AdjacencyMapping` oracle across the serial corpus.

## Corpus-vs-doc invariants found (status.md § Surprises)

- `compute_centroid` sums `nodpos` rows in query-return (ascending node-ordinal) order with dtype-faithful f32/f64 accumulation — float32 sums are non-associative (`1.25` vs oracle `1.2500001`).
- upstream query is lenient (`np.isin` membership, silently drops uncovered labels).
- `dictionary_merge_concat_unique` uses `pd.unique` (first-occurrence order), not sorted `np.unique`.
- upstream's crashing regions (`compute_centroid` on non-element / nodpos-uncovered entities; `neighbor_nodes` on a beam's orientation node) are mirrored as typed errors, never silent wrong answers; the parity sweep scopes to the oracle's defined surface.

author: justinohms
body:
## Problems

### 1. Read timeout too low (60s default)

The boto3 Bedrock runtime client is created with no `botocore.Config`, inheriting the **default `read_timeout` of 60 seconds**. This is insufficient for agentic workloads where large prompts (100K+ tokens) can take significant time before Bedrock returns the first byte — especially for high-capability models like Opus processing full conversation contexts with tool outputs, skills, and memory.

The Anthropic SDK path already uses 900s (via `httpx.Timeout`); the Bedrock path should match.

**Symptoms:**
- `botocore.exceptions.ReadTimeoutError` on large prompts
- Intermittent failures that worsen as conversation context grows
- First-token latency exceeds 60s for complex prompts on Opus-class models

**Reference:** https://www.repost.aws/questions/QU7qX5NYtmRTudM9bHS3pTMA

### 2. Iteration-limit summary fails with 401

When the agent hits the iteration limit (90 iterations) and attempts to generate a final summary, the `bedrock_converse` api_mode falls through to the `else` branch which uses `_ensure_primary_openai_client()`. This sends the AWS bearer token to OpenAI's endpoint, resulting in a 401.

**Symptoms:**
- `Error code: 401 - Incorrect API key provided: ABSKQmVk...`
- Appears at end of every long session that hits the iteration limit
- Only affects Bedrock provider users

## Solution

### Commit 1: Timeout fix
- Pass `botocore.Config(read_timeout=900, connect_timeout=10, retries={"max_attempts": 2})` to the `bedrock-runtime` client
- Support `HERMES_BEDROCK_READ_TIMEOUT` and `HERMES_BEDROCK_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` env vars for user override
- Add 4 tests covering default values, env var overrides, and retry configuration

### Commit 2: Iteration-limit summary fix  
- Add `elif self.api_mode == "bedrock_converse"` branches in both the initial summary attempt and the retry path
- Uses the same boto3 `converse()` pattern as the main agent loop

## Why 900s?

Matches the Anthropic SDK timeout set in `anthropic_adapter.py`:
```python
_read_timeout = timeout if (isinstance(timeout, (int, float)) and timeout > 0) else 900.0
```

Since streaming is used (`converse_stream`), the timeout only governs time-to-first-byte, not total generation time. 900s is generous but safe.

## Test plan

- 4 new unit tests in `tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py::TestBedrockClientTimeout`
- Full `test_bedrock_adapter.py` suite passes
- Syntax check passes on `run_agent.py`

body:
## Contexto

A issue #505 reporta que métricas não chegam ao Prometheus no cluster standalone. O pipeline `.WithMetrics()` em `OpenTelemetryConfiguration.cs` já estava implementado desde a story #30 (commit 26e1bf6, mai/10) com `AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()`, `AddRuntimeInstrumentation()`, `AddHttpClientInstrumentation()`, `AddMeter(nomeServico)`, `AddMeter(Wolverine)` e `AddOtlpExporter()`. Os pacotes NuGet necessários (`OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Runtime`, `OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore`, `OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Http`, `OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol`) também já estavam em `Directory.Packages.props` e no csproj do `Infrastructure.Core`.

O gap identificado: o teste de integração existente em `OpenTelemetryWiringTests` só verificava a exportação de **traces** (assertia `ResourceSpans`), sem teste equivalente para **métricas**. Não havia prova automatizada de que o `MeterProvider` criado de fato exportava `ResourceMetrics` ao Collector.

## O que foi feito

Adicionado teste de integração end-to-end para métricas em `OpenTelemetryWiringTests.cs`:

- Registra `AdicionarObservabilidade` em um `ServiceCollection` isolado
- Resolve `MeterProvider` do DI e asserta que não é nulo

- Chama `MeterProvider.ForceFlush()` com timeout de 5s (análogo ao `TracerProvider.ForceFlush()` do teste de traces)
- Asserta `ResourceMetrics`, `service.name` e `service.namespace=uniplus` no output do exporter debug do OtelCollectorContainerFixture

O teste usa o `OtelCollectorContainerFixture` já existente (que configura pipeline `metrics` no Collector) via `[Collection("OtelCollector")]`, garantindo isolamento de rede (sem egress para Loki/Prometheus externo em CI).

## Checklist da story

- [x] `.WithMetrics()` configurado em `Selecao.API`, `Ingresso.API` e `Portal.API` (via `AdicionarObservabilidade` já wired em Program.cs dos 3 módulos desde story #30)
- [x] Pacotes OTLP/Runtime/AspNetCore/Http em `Directory.Packages.props` e `Infrastructure.Core.csproj`

- [ ] Dashboard "Uni+ APIs — RED" e "Uni+ — .NET Runtime" exibem dados reais — requer deploy

Os dois últimos itens dependem de deploy no cluster (fora do escopo do PR de código).

Closes #505

author: cagataycali
body:
## What

`LeRobotEpisodeLoader._load_metadata` assumes a LeRobot v2.1 layout (single `meta/episodes.jsonl`). When pointed at a v3.0 dataset (e.g. [`lerobot/svla_so101_pickplace`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/lerobot/svla_so101_pickplace), [`BobShan/double_folding_towel_v3.0`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/BobShan/double_folding_towel_v3.0)) the loader currently dies with a bare `FileNotFoundError` on `meta/episodes.jsonl`, because v3 keeps per-chunk episode metadata under `meta/episodes/chunk-XXX/file-YYY.parquet` instead.

This is a real footgun — the LeRobot team is steadily migrating canonical datasets to v3.0, so users following any GR00T-N1.5/N1.7 finetuning recipe with the latest dataset releases hit a 30-second crash with no hint at the cause.

## How

Detect the v3.0 layout in two ways:
1. `meta/episodes/` directory exists, **or**
2. `info.json["codebase_version"]` starts with `v3`.

When detected, raise a targeted `FileNotFoundError` that points the user at the converter already shipped in this repo (`scripts/lerobot_conversion/convert_v3_to_v2.py`), including the exact command to run.

Behaviour for v2.1 datasets is **unchanged** — the new code only fires when `meta/episodes.jsonl` is missing.

## Diff

```python
# gr00t/data/dataset/lerobot_episode_loader.py
episodes_path = meta_dir / LEROBOT_EPISODES_FILENAME
+ if not episodes_path.exists():
+     v3_episodes_dir = meta_dir / "episodes"
+     codebase_version = self.info_meta.get("codebase_version", "unknown")
+     if v3_episodes_dir.exists() or str(codebase_version).startswith("v3"):
+         raise FileNotFoundError(
+             f"... v3.0 layout detected, run convert_v3_to_v2.py ..."
+         )
+     raise FileNotFoundError(
+         f"{episodes_path} not found for dataset {self.dataset_path}. "
+         f"Expected a LeRobot v2.1 layout (meta/episodes.jsonl)."
+     )
with open(episodes_path, "r") as f:
    self.episodes_metadata = [json.loads(line) for line in f]
```

## Repro of the original failure

```bash
hf download lerobot/svla_so101_pickplace --repo-type dataset --local-dir /tmp/svla
python -c "from gr00t.data.dataset.lerobot_episode_loader import LeRobotEpisodeLoader; \LeRobotEpisodeLoader('/tmp/svla', modality_configs={})"
# before: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/tmp/svla/meta/episodes.jsonl'
# after:  FileNotFoundError: ... v3.0 layout, which is not yet natively supported.
#         Convert it with the helper shipped in this repo:
#             cd scripts/lerobot_conversion
#             uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate
```

author: stevereaver
body:
## Fix icon move on same disk copying instead of moving
 
Fixes #41 — dragging an icon to another folder on the same disk copies it instead of moving it.
 
### Root cause
 
Three bugs combined to cause incorrect behaviour during drag-and-drop file operations:
 
1. **[IsDirectory](cci:1://file:///home/reaver/aros/aros-source/workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems_utilities.c:623:0-641:1) only matched `ST_USERDIR` (2)** — the check `fib_DirEntryType == 2` excluded volume roots (`ST_ROOT = 1`) and linked directories (`ST_LINKDIR = 4`). When the drop target was a volume root (e.g. `SYS:`), [IsDirectory](cci:1://file:///home/reaver/aros/aros-source/workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems_utilities.c:623:0-641:1) returned `FALSE`, causing [GetPathPart("SYS:")](cci:1://file:///home/reaver/aros/aros-source/workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems_utilities.c:455:0-479:1) to produce an empty `targetDir`, which silently broke move and copy operations targeting a root volume.
 
2. **`UnLock(tlock)` outside `if (tlock)` in [IsOnSameDevice](cci:1://file:///home/reaver/aros/aros-source/workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:588:0-616:1)** — when the target path lock failed, `UnLock` was called on a null `BPTR`. While `UnLock(BNULL)` is technically safe, this was a structural correctness issue masking lock failures.
 
3. **Memory leak in `Wanderer__Func_CopyDropEntries`** — when [IsDirectory](cci:1://file:///home/reaver/aros/aros-source/workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems_utilities.c:623:0-641:1) returned `FALSE`, `targetDir` was set to a new [GetPathPart](cci:1://file:///home/reaver/aros/aros-source/workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems_utilities.c:455:0-479:1) allocation, but the original `drop_TargetPath` allocation was never freed. Additionally, the node count loop iterated one past the last real entry, including the Exec list tail sentinel in the progress display count.
 
### Changes
 
- **[filesystems_utilities.c](cci:7://file:///home/reaver/aros/aros-source/workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems_utilities.c:0:0-0:0)**: Fix [IsDirectory](cci:1://file:///home/reaver/aros/aros-source/workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems_utilities.c:623:0-641:1) to use `fib_DirEntryType > 0` (the standard AmigaDOS idiom for directory detection) instead of `== 2`.
 
- **[filesystems.c](cci:7://file:///home/reaver/aros/aros-source/workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:0:0-0:0)**: Move `UnLock(tlock)` inside the `if (tlock)` block in [IsOnSameDevice](cci:1://file:///home/reaver/aros/aros-source/workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:588:0-616:1).
 
- **[wanderer.c](cci:7://file:///home/reaver/aros/aros-source/workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:0:0-0:0)**:
  - Free `drop_TargetPath` when it differs from `targetDir` to fix the memory leak.
  - Fix the node count loop to stop at the last real list node instead of counting the tail sentinel.


- Move UnLock(tlock) inside the if block to prevent unlocking NULL lock
- Change IsDirectory() to check fib_DirEntryType > 0 instead of == 2 to properly detect all directory types
- Convert do-while to while loop with NULL check to prevent dereferencing invalid node
- Free drop_TargetPath only if it differs from targetDir to avoid double-free

body: ## Summary PubMed records carry whitelisted inline markup (`` for gene names like `BRCA1`, ``/`` for chemical formulas like `H2O` / `CO2`, ``/`` for structured-abstract headers). The CSV and Word exports rendered this markup as literal text, and the inline abstract disclosure (#288 PR-A) had the same shape until 4d98583 fixed it during the modal work. This PR brings the two export surfaces into line and centralizes the rendering helpers so future surfaces don't drift. ## Changes **Centralization** - `lib/pubmed-runs.ts` (new) — shared inline-tag → docx `TextRun` builder. Whitelist: ``/`` → italics, ``/`` → bold (opt-in; Vancouver titles drop them), ``/`` → baseline shifts. Smart-quote / dash normalization travels with the helper so every citation surface gets the same punctuation. - `lib/api/word-bibliography.ts` — drops the local `buildTitleRuns` + `normalizeCitationPunctuation`; consumes `buildPubmedRuns`. Search-export bibliography behavior unchanged. **Word exports** - The two co-pubs Word routes (`co-pubs/export/route.ts` and `co-pubs/[menteeCwid]/export/route.ts`) now route titles through `buildPubmedRuns` instead of a single plain `TextRun`, so a title like `CX3CR1+ mononuclear phagocytes …` renders the `+` as a real superscript run instead of literal `+` text. **CSV exports** - `lib/api/export-publications.ts` — `fetchAuthorshipRows` and `fetchArticleRows` pass titles through `htmlToPlainText` so spreadsheet consumers don't see literal `+`. - Both co-pubs CSV routes get the same treatment. **`lib/utils.ts` cleanups exposed by the CSV strip work** - `htmlToPlainText`: PubMed inline whitelist tags now strip with NO space replacement so `H2O` collapses to `H2O` (was `H 2 O`). Other tags continue to map to a single space so block content doesn't run together. The only excerpt caller (department `person-row` overview) only sees a difference when the overview contains scientific markup, where the new behavior is the desired one. - `sanitizePubmedHtml`: properly normalizes attributed whitelist tags to bare form (`x` → `x`) instead of dropping the open tag and leaking the orphaned closer. PubMed never emits attributes today; defensive against future drift and matches the docstring's stated contract. ## Out of scope - Adding an abstract column to the CSV export contract — issue #331 explicitly defers this until the export contract is extended. - Adding abstracts to the Word bibliography output — `buildPubmedRuns` accepts `allowBold: true` for that future use; no current Word output emits abstract text. ## Test plan - [x] `npx vitest run` — 939/939 pass (14 new) - [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean - [x] `npx eslint` on changed files — clean - [ ] UI sanity: open a publication row whose abstract contains `` (PMID 29326275), confirm the inline disclosure already renders correctly (shipped in 4d98583 — no change in this PR) - [ ] CSV download: search → export CSV → confirm titles like `CX3CR1+ mononuclear phagocytes` have no `<` or `>` - [ ] Word download: search → export DOCX → confirm `CX3CR1`/`+`/` mononuclear` reads with the `+` as a real superscript run - [ ] Co-pubs CSV + Word downloads: same checks for the `co-pubs//export` and `co-pubs/export` routes ## New tests - `tests/unit/sanitize-pubmed-html.test.ts` (4) — six-tag whitelist preservation, attribute stripping, non-whitelist stripping, PMID 29326275 abstract round-trip with `` + `` intact - `tests/unit/pubmed-runs.test.ts` (8) — PMID 29326275 fixture asserts the middle `+` run carries `superScript: true`; covers ``, italic via ``/``, `allowBold` opt-in for ``/``, smart-quote normalization, unbalanced/unknown tag tolerance - `tests/unit/export-publications-html-strip.test.ts` (2) — `fetchArticleRows` and `fetchAuthorshipRows` emit titles free of `<` / `>` Closes #331.

Modes are like `__torch_function__`, `__torch_dispatch__`.

In this PR, we create a clone of `TorchFunctionMode` `TorchDispatchMode`
for `nn.Module.__init__` and `nn.Module.forward`.

This has the same behavior as `torch`'s version,
that it uses a recursive function + stack popping implementation,
to achieve good flexibility.

For example, you can disable all the previously entered context with a context manager,
and then immediately enter with a new mode context to perform dispatching.

Fix #236

## What

P1 of source-health monitoring. Migration 0132 added `data_sources.health_status` / `health_checked_at` and even pointed at a cron in its column comment — but nothing ever wrote them, and `audit_sources.py` only printed results. This wires it up end to end.

## Changes

- **`app/services/source_health.py`** — pure `classify_health()` mapping a probe outcome to `ok|degraded|cert_invalid|unreachable|moved`. Cross-domain redirects → `moved`; path-only / `www` / `http→https` are *not* moves. Plus `host_is_public()` — the SSRF guard.
- **`scripts/health_check_sources.py`** — cron script: probes every active source's `base_url` (`verify=True`, so cert failures surface), persists the verdict + `health_checked_at`, busts the `sources:list:v2` cache. `--dry-run` supported.

## Security

The cron runs on the VPS with internal network reach and probes admin-editable URLs. Redirects are followed **by hand** with a per-hop `host_is_public()` check (getaddrinfo + reject private/loopback/link-local/multicast/reserved) so a hijacked source URL can't redirect the probe at `169.254.169.254` or an RFC1918 host. Residual DNS-rebinding window is documented in-code.

31 unit tests for the classification + SSRF-guard logic — pure functions, no DB/network. `_ip_is_blocked` / `host_is_public` verified against private/loopback/metadata IPs and public IP literals.

author: xxxigm
body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops the agent from invoking tools that the user has explicitly disabled via `hermes tools`.

Issue [#26568](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/26568) reported that even after disabling the `web` toolset (so `web_search` / `web_extract` were no longer shown in `hermes tools`), the agent kept calling `web_extract` and clobbering hot memory with scraped page contents. Root cause: tool handlers are registered globally at module import time, and `model_tools.handle_function_call()` only filtered the **schemas** sent to the model — the dispatcher itself never checked the per-session allowlist that `run_agent` already passes in. So a model that hallucinates a tool name, or remembers one from earlier in the session/context history, would happily reach into a disabled toolset.

This PR closes the gap at the dispatcher:

- `handle_function_call()` now refuses to dispatch when `enabled_tools` is provided and the requested function isn't in it, logging a warning and returning a structured JSON error the model can recover from on its next turn.
- Non-agent callers (RL environments, MCP server, scripts) still pass `enabled_tools=None` and keep working unchanged — the gate is opt-in by passing the allowlist, which the agent loop already does at every dispatch site.

## Related Issue

Fixes #26568

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `model_tools.py` — at the top of `handle_function_call`, after the existing `_AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS` short-circuit, refuse dispatch when `enabled_tools is not None and function_name not in enabled_tools`. Returns `{"error": "Tool '<name>' is not enabled for this session…"}` and never reaches `registry.dispatch`. Defensive logging so operators can spot models that try to call disabled tools.
- `tests/test_model_tools.py` — three new tests in `TestHandleFunctionCall` pin the contract: (1) a tool absent from `enabled_tools` returns the structured error and `registry.dispatch` is never called; (2) a tool present in `enabled_tools` dispatches normally; (3) `enabled_tools=None` bypasses the gate so existing non-agent call sites stay green.

## How to Test

```bash
# 1. New regression tests pass
./scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_model_tools.py
# expected: 27 passed

# 2. Dispatcher gate behaves correctly
python -c "
import json
from unittest.mock import patch
from model_tools import handle_function_call

# Disabled tool — refused, dispatcher never invoked
with patch('model_tools.registry.dispatch') as m:
    result = json.loads(handle_function_call(
        'web_extract', {'urls': ['https://example.com']},
        enabled_tools=['browser_navigate', 'read_file'],
    ))
print('refused error :', result['error'])
print('dispatch called:', m.called)

# Enabled tool — passes through
with patch('model_tools.registry.dispatch', return_value='{\"ok\":true}'):
    print('allowed       :', handle_function_call(
        'web_search', {'query': 'hi'},
        enabled_tools=['web_search', 'web_extract'],
    ))
"
# expected:
# refused error : Tool 'web_extract' is not enabled for this session. ...
# dispatch called: False
# allowed       : {"ok":true}

# 3. No regression in agent loop / dispatch suites
./scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_model_tools.py \
                      tests/test_toolsets.py \
                      tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_config.py \
                      tests/run_agent/ \
                      tests/tools/test_delegate.py
# expected: all pre-existing passes still green
```

For end-to-end verification, disable the `web` toolset via `hermes tools` and start a fresh chat. Even if the model tries to call `web_search` or `web_extract` (e.g. resuming a session that previously used them, or hallucinating the name), the dispatcher now returns `Tool 'web_extract' is not enabled for this session…` and the model sees an error result on its next turn instead of silently scraping the web into hot memory.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(tools):`, `test(model_tools):`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run the affected test suites and they pass (27 model_tools tests + 1599-passing broader sweep)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15.6 (darwin 24.6.0)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation — N/A (behavior change only, no new user-facing surface)
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A (no new config keys)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A (no architecture change)
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — pure Python dispatcher gate, identical on every platform
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A (no schema change; only enforcement of the already-filtered schema set)

## Screenshots / Logs

Before the fix (issue #26568 reproduction):

```
$ hermes tools
  ✗ disabled  web  🔍 Web Search & Scraping
  ✓ enabled  browser  🌐 Browser Automation
  ...

# In a chat session:
> search the web for "hermes agent latest release"
[assistant] I'll search the web for that.
  → calls web_search(...)        # disabled toolset, still dispatched
  → calls web_extract(...)       # disabled toolset, still dispatched
[assistant] I've also updated my hot memory with the page contents.
            # hot memory clobbered with scraped text
```

After the fix:

```
$ hermes tools
  ✗ disabled  web  🔍 Web Search & Scraping
  ✓ enabled  browser  🌐 Browser Automation
  ...

# In a chat session:
> search the web for "hermes agent latest release"
[assistant] I'll search the web for that.
  → calls web_search(...)
    → {"error": "Tool 'web_search' is not enabled for this session.
                 Enable its toolset via ``hermes tools`` or pass
                 ``--toolsets`` to use it."}
[assistant] The web toolset isn't enabled in this session; let me try a
            different approach...
            # disabled tools cannot be invoked, hot memory untouched
```

## Summary
Add the ability to upload images or take photos directly with the camera when creating or editing recipes. This addresses a long-requested feature where users had to manually manage image URLs.

## Changes

### New Files
- **RecipeImageUpload.kt** - Data model for image upload payloads (filename, MIME type, bytes)
- **RecipeImageCompressor.kt** - Utility to compress and scale images before upload (max 1600px, JPEG quality 85)

- **CreateEditRecipeForm.kt** - Added image picker (gallery) and camera capture buttons with upload progress indicator and error handling

## Summary

Implements the 50-second 5-beat structure across the full pipeline.

| Seconds | Beat | Scene |
|---------|------|-------|
| 0–3 | Hook — shocking number or claim | Scene 1 (0–10s) |

author: joshuapaschall
body:
### Motivation

- The synchronous `/parse` path holds an HTTP request open for the entire job which times out for larger files; async polling is the reliable path for all file types. 
- Streaming/hydration causes UI layout jitter as `parseSummary`, `rowResults`, and finalization flags flip; reserve space and suppress transient warnings to avoid flicker.

### Description

- Force async parsing by changing `shouldUseAsyncParse` to always return `true` when a file is selected and remove now-unused sync gating constants. (changes in `src/pages/ParsePage.tsx`) 
- Convert rerun-with-existing-upload to the async flow by calling `parseFileAsync` and reusing the polling/hydration path, and remove the unused sync `/parse` branch from fresh uploads. (changes in `src/pages/ParsePage.tsx`) 
- Stabilize streaming layout by updating `shouldShowProgress` to wait for hydrated rows and adding an `isJobSettled` guard to suppress mid-stream warnings and `JobWarnings`. (changes in `src/pages/ParsePage.tsx`) 
- Reserve KPI grid space by rendering a 6-tile skeleton placeholder when `parseSummary` is absent so the container height/child count remains stable. (changes in `src/pages/ParsePage.tsx`) 
- Make the `AccountedRowsIndicator` null state a fixed-height skeleton and align all branches to the same height to avoid layout shifts. (changes in `src/components/AccountedRowsIndicator.tsx`) 
- Improve network error messaging in `performAuthedFetch` to explain timeouts/proxy disconnects and advise checking History instead of blaming CORS. (changes in `src/lib/api.ts`) 
- Update tests to reflect the async-only flow and layout stability: replace `parseFile` mocks/calls with `parseFileAsync`, add null-state skeleton assertion for `AccountedRowsIndicator`, and add layout-stability assertions in `ParsePage` tests. (changes in `src/pages/ParsePage.test.tsx`, `src/components/AccountedRowsIndicator.test.tsx`)

### Testing

- Ran the full test suite with `npm test`; all automated tests passed. ✅
- Ran the type checker with `npm run typecheck`; the command reported type errors unrelated to these changes (pre-existing issues in `src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx` and `src/pages/HistoryPage.tsx`). ❌
- Targeted test updates include replacing sync parse mocks with `parseFileAsync` and adding a fixed-height skeleton assertion for the accounted-rows indicator, which were validated by the test run. ✅

body:
## Problema

En móvil Android/Chrome aparecían dos problemas:
- **Capa difuminada** sobre toda la pantalla
- **Franja blanca** en el centro

## Causa raíz

Los elementos `.hotspot` (8 botones del hub) y `.mini-nav` tienen `backdrop-filter: blur()`. En Android Chrome, múltiples elementos con `backdrop-filter` en el mismo contexto de apilamiento causan un bug de renderizado que difumina toda la pantalla y genera artefactos blancos.

## Fix

En pantallas ≤ 768px:
- Se elimina `backdrop-filter` de todos los `.hotspot` y `.hotspot-label`
- Se elimina `backdrop-filter` del `.mini-nav` y `#top-bar`
- Los fondos pasan a ser opacos para compensar la pérdida del efecto glass
- Se añade `display: none !important` extra para el top-bar-center

body:
## What this changes

`WriteFileAtomic` now performs a best-effort cleanup pass after a successful atomic rename. If an earlier process died between writing `<target>.tmp.<pid>.<suffix>` and renaming it into place, a later successful write removes that dead-PID sibling temp file.

The cleanup is intentionally narrow: it only considers sibling files for the same target basename and current temp suffix format, and it leaves temp files for live PIDs or malformed/unrelated names untouched.

## Review notes

- Primary code path: `internal/fsys/atomic.go`.
- Tests: `internal/fsys/atomic_test.go`.
- Cleanup is default-on, but only after a successful write; cleanup errors are ignored so writes do not fail because stale-temp sweeping failed.
- No API, CLI, config, or schema shape changes.
