body:
First PR of the masterclass-level improvement engagement. Two commits:

## 1. \`docs(audit): Phase 1 audit + Phase 2 plan + anti-cheat research\`

Pure planning artifacts under \`audit/\` — 10 dimension-specific audit reports + ranked SUMMARY (10 Critical / 34 High / 35 Medium / 35 Low), Phase 2 grouped plan with per-item scope/files/risk/verification, and 5 parallel anti-cheat investigations synthesised into a master action×AC matrix. Bottom line: zero documented bans from Process-Lasso-class tools in 15+ years; the universal invariant is *never request \`PROCESS_VM_READ\`/\`PROCESS_VM_WRITE\` on a protected game*, which our access pattern already satisfies. Real risks remain on Valorant (VAN: Competitive Restrictions, recoverable) and ESEA (vendor-named conflict).

## 2. \`fix(engine,service): item 1.1 — denylist gate at every kernel-write entry-point\`

Closes audit findings **C-01, C-02, C-03, H-17, M-04**. The narrow safety bar: refuse to touch processes/services on the bundled denylist (csrss/lsass/wininit/dwm/audiodg/MsMpEng/Vanguard/EAC/BattlEye/RpcSs/Dhcp/Dnscache/audio/GPU drivers). Outside the denylist, aggression stays the product — BITS/WSearch/ClickToRunSvc/OneDrive/telemetry remain fair game by design.

**Two new free functions** in \`engine/src/lib.rs\`:
- \`check_process_modifiable(safe_list, exe, action)\` — consults \`SafeList::check_process\`; on Denied returns an error carrying the JSON rationale string.
- \`resolve_exe_for_pid_or_err(pid, action)\` — PID → bare exe filename via \`framesage_sys::process::exe_for_pid\`; surfaces clean \"process exited\" errors.

**Wired into every per-PID IPC handler**: \`set_process_priority\`, \`suspend_process\`, \`resume_process\`, \`set_process_affinity\`, \`terminate_process\`, \`trim_working_set\`.

**Rule-driven path defense-in-depth**: \`apply_profile()\` gains \`safe_list: &'static SafeList\` and consults the gate before any \`framesage_sys::apply::apply()\` call. Catches a malicious policy.json with \`ExeName(\"csrss.exe\") -> game-x3d\` before \`SetProcessAffinityMask(1)\` reaches the critical process.

**SetPolicy server-side validation**: new \`validate_policy_against_safe_list()\` in \`service/runtime.rs\` walks every \`Profile.game_mode.{stop_services, suspend_processes}\` and intersects against the bundled SafeList. Reports ALL denials in one \`Response::Error\` so the user fixes them in a single save+reject cycle. Closes audit's **CRITICAL-2** (admin-amplification via \`SetPolicy\` with \`stop_services: [\"WinDefend\"]\`).

## Tests

12 new tests, all passing:

**engine** (6 tests):
- \`check_process_modifiable_refuses_kernel_critical\` — csrss/lsass/wininit/services/smss/winlogon
- \`check_process_modifiable_refuses_shell_audio_gpu\` — dwm/explorer/audiodg/fontdrvhost/nvcontainer/atiesrxx/sihost
- \`check_process_modifiable_refuses_av_and_anticheat\` — MsMpEng/NisSrv/SecurityHealthService
- \`check_process_modifiable_allows_aggression_targets\` — OneDrive/Dropbox/GameBar/OEM/notepad/chrome/Valorant/BF6/Fortnite (all MUST pass)
- \`check_process_modifiable_is_case_insensitive\` — CSRSS.EXE / csrss.exe / CsRsS.ExE
- \`check_process_modifiable_surfaces_rationale\` — error message MUST contain JSON rationale (\"blue-screen\" / \"BSOD\")

**service** (6 tests):
- \`validate_accepts_aggressive_but_safe_defaults\` — full sledgehammer (10 services, 7 processes) MUST pass
- \`validate_refuses_denylisted_services\` — WinDefend/vgc/EasyAntiCheat/BEService/RpcSs/Dhcp/Dnscache/AudioSrv
- \`validate_refuses_denylisted_processes\` — csrss/lsass/wininit/dwm/audiodg/MsMpEng/explorer/nvcontainer
- \`validate_reports_all_denials_at_once\` — 5 bad entries → 5 denials, not 1
- \`validate_accepts_profile_without_game_mode\` — eco/perf profiles
- \`validate_accepts_shipped_default_policy\` — locks invariant that our own defaults pass validation

## Test plan

- [x] cargo build / clippy / fmt all clean
- [x] cargo test --workspace: 31 + 19 + 24 + 6 + 11 + 4 + 37 + 13 + 3 = 148 tests passing
- [x] cargo build --release --workspace clean
- [ ] Manual: deploy via FINISH-DEPLOY.bat, attempt \`framesage terminate csrss\` from CLI → expect rejection with rationale visible in tray status banner
- [ ] Manual: attempt \`SetPolicy\` with a profile containing \`stop_services: [\"WinDefend\"]\` → expect rejection listing the denial reason

## What's next

Group 1 items 1.2 through 1.9 still pending. After all of Group 1: review stop with self-footprint baseline numbers.

body:
## Summary

Adds a friendly multi-song TXT layout to the bulk-import flow on the **Upload lyrics** tab so users can ship the same `title / text / genre` triples they had to use CSV for previously.

Format (auto-detected):

```
Название: Ночной город
Жанр: рок
Текст:
Я иду по улице ночной
Город спит, но не со мной


Название: Морская
Жанр: шансон
Море, море, мир бездонный
```

- Songs are separated by **two blank lines** (3+ newlines).
- Per-block headers `Название:` / `Жанр:` / `Текст:` are all optional; English aliases `Title:` / `Genre:` / `Lyrics:` also work (case-insensitive).
- Everything after a `Текст:` line (or after the last recognised header) is the song body.
- If **no** block in the file looks structured, the importer falls back to the previous behaviour — blank-line-separated blocks become `Песня #1`, `#2`, …; a single block becomes one song.

Also:

- Inline accordion **«Как должен выглядеть TXT / CSV»** under the import controls with a copy-pasteable example.
- README walkthrough updated with the same example.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Autodetection false positives.** A block flips into "structured" mode if **any** of its first three non-empty lines matches the header regex. If a real song happens to start a line with `Жанр: …` or `Title: …`, that line will be silently consumed as metadata instead of being part of the lyrics. Worth eyeballing the regex (`_TXT_HEADER_RE` in `src/datasets/manager.py`) and deciding whether the trade-off is right, or whether we should require an explicit `Название:` to enter structured mode.
- [ ] **Cyrillic + `re.IGNORECASE`.** The header regex matches Cyrillic field names (`название`, `жанр`, `текст`) with `re.IGNORECASE`. This works on Python ≥ 3.6 with default Unicode str patterns, but please sanity-check on the Colab runtime (3.10/3.11/3.12) with a TXT that uses uppercase Cyrillic headers (`НАЗВАНИЕ:`).
- [ ] **End-to-end test in Colab**: pull this branch, open the Upload tab, expand the accordion, copy the example TXT, save as `songs.txt`, import → confirm 2 songs land with the correct titles, genres and multiline bodies. Then try a TXT **without** any headers (just two-blank-line separated blocks) and confirm the fallback still produces `Песня #1`, `#2`.

### Notes

- Splitter changed from `split("\n\n\n")` (exactly 3 newlines) to `re.split(r"\n{3,}", …)` (3+ newlines). This is more lenient about extra trailing blank lines between songs; equivalent for the documented format.
- The single-song fallback now feeds normalised (`\r\n` → `\n`) text into `import_texts` instead of the raw string. Minor.
- New module-level helpers (`_blocks_have_headers`, `_parse_txt_block`) ended up above the `log = get_logger(__name__)` line in `src/datasets/manager.py` — functionally inert (they don't use the logger) but the module-attribute ordering is slightly jumbled if that bothers you.
- No new dependencies; no CI on the repo, so syntax was validated with `ast.parse` and the parser was smoke-tested on a hand-crafted multi-block string (1 structured / 1 English-headers / 1 no-headers block).

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0d87c6c8aee74f69a8dd206fc6bdc13a

body:
# release(v0.57.0): EU AI Act Wave 2 — Article 14 + R25-EU11 claim-limits + VERITAS Q16.1/Q16.3/Q16.5 + PCT + README/EUR-Lex guards + consolidated switch UX [CR-010]

> **GraQle moves from "EU AI Act-aware in the docs" to "EU AI Act-aligned in the code."** One PR closes 9 of 10 ADR-MARKETING-003 marketing-vs-built gaps (CG-MKT-01..10 except 09 which is the process itself), bringing the honesty score from 78/100 to ~98/100.
> **Pattern:** Identical to v0.56.0 release PR #140 — single squashed commit on a release branch off `master`. Cherry-picked content-only from `private/master @ 39ccf4c9`; zero deletions of public-only files; 5 private-only files explicitly excluded.

---

## What's in this release (one paragraph each)

### **Article 14 human-review gate** (CG-MKT-01)
Auto-apply paths (`graq edit/apply/auto`) refuse to apply changes when generation confidence is below threshold AND `--human-review-required` is set OR `GRAQLE_EU_AI_ACT_MODE=on`. Refusal envelope carries the regulatory anchor (`article_14_clauses: ["14(4)(c)", "14(4)(d)"]`), the actual confidence + threshold, and `threshold_status: "placeholder"` (explicit marker that the default 0.75 is pending the R25-EU-CALIB-01 calibration spike).

### **R25-EU11 claim-limits v1.0** (CG-MKT-10)
17 canonical values across 6 categories (temporal, model-dependency, data-scope, decision-scope, trust-boundary, compliance-scope) plus `x-` operator-extension namespace. Every governance record now declares "what does this record NOT claim?" via a typed vocabulary. L08 SHACL constraint + L19 audit-trail rejection are fail-closed (default-deny). Backfill protocol with `["legacy_pre_R25_EU11"]` sentinel. Public attribution to **Ricky Jones (TrinityOS)** LinkedIn 2026-05-13 formulation.

### **VERITAS Q16.1 baseline-doc generator** (CG-MKT-02)
`graq compliance baseline-doc generate` produces a dated, content-addressed baseline document (SHA-256 of canonicalised JSON) covering EU AI Act Article 11 (technical documentation) + ISO 42001 Cl. 6.2 (planning). Optional `--signoff` countersignature, optional PDF emitter (graceful RuntimeError when `reportlab` not installed). VERITAS Pillar 16 Part 1 mapping per **Andrii Matiash** LinkedIn 2026-05-12.

### **VERITAS Q16.3 periodic-assessment** (CG-MKT-03)
`graq compliance periodic-assessment run --period-start ... --period-end ... --cadence monthly|quarterly|annual` computes 5 quality metrics over the trace corpus + auto-flags 3 remediation severities on threshold breach. Idempotent for same `(period, cadence, baseline_id)`. Each assessment references the most recent baseline_id — Cl. 9.1 evidence chains back to Cl. 6.2 evidence.

### **VERITAS Q16.5 OBSERVATION-ONLY drift watcher** (CG-MKT-04)
`graq compliance feedback record/ingest` + `WelfordAccumulator` + `compute_drift_indicator()`. **CRITICAL — Patent-novelty boundary per Q-PATENT 2026-05-22**: the drift indicator is an *observation*, never a *trigger*. The mandatory AST audit test `test_q165_no_active_recalibration_path.py` fails CI if any future contributor wires drift to a calibration call. Keeps R25-EU04 patent-clean under existing EP26167849.4 Claim 4.

### **README snapshot-lock + EUR-Lex drift guard** (CG-MKT-05/06)
Two CI-pinnable invariants. The README snapshot-lock test fails CI if forbidden marketing words (compliant/certified/guaranteed/end-to-end solution) appear as bare claims in the README or `docs/compliance/eu-ai-act/*.md` — with sophisticated exemption logic (negative-lookbehind for compound technical adjectives like `privacy-compliant`, line-level skip for italic/backtick/anti-claim mentions). The EUR-Lex drift guard runs weekly (`.github/workflows/eur-lex-weekly.yml`, Mondays 06:00 UTC), re-fetches every `eur-lex.europa.eu` URL in compliance docs, compares content-hashes to a committed baseline, and opens a GitHub issue on drift.

### **PCT (Proof-Claims Token) Use B + `x-ai-eu` extension** (CG-MKT-07/08)
`graqle.pct.issuer.issue_pct()` mints a JWS (RS256 + kid header) carrying allowed_purposes / permitted_regions / extension claims. `graqle.pct.validator.validate_pct()` returns ALLOW/BLOCK with structured `failure_reasons` after a 6-check pipeline (size cap → JWS structure → signature → schema → temporal → action/jurisdiction). Vendored OPSF schema pinned to commit SHA `f04bbc4862af836a2696e635275ead4bc835d9d1`. Defense-in-depth: 64KB token-size cap (env-configurable via `GRAQLE_PCT_MAX_TOKEN_BYTES`), log-injection-safe `kid` sanitiser. `XAiEuExtension` is GraQle's first-public-draft of the `x-ai-eu` namespace (10 fields covering Articles 6/9/12/13/14/50, articles_covered, GPAI flag, Annex III category, compliance dossier ID).

### **Consolidated switch UX (new in v0.57.0)**
`graq compliance switch [status|on|off]` is the single UX entry-point for the EU AI Act mode toggle. `switch status` returns a consolidated envelope showing every EU-AI-Act-aware subsystem (Article 50 disclosure, Article 14 gate, claim-limits, baseline-doc, periodic-assessment, feedback-trend, EUR-Lex guard). `switch on/off` prints shell-eval snippets for posix/powershell/cmd. Does NOT mutate the user's environment — the trust boundary is the user's shell, not GraQle state.

---

## Files

**68 files: 35 NEW + 33 MODIFIED. Zero deletions of public-only content.**

### New files (35)
| Category | Files |
|----------|-------|
| **PCT package** | `graqle/pct/{issuer.py, validator.py, extensions/x_ai_eu.py, schema/pct_v0_1.json, schema/opsf_examples/scenario_1..4_*.json}` + `graqle/cli/commands/pct.py` |

---
## ⚠️ PLANNING-ONLY PR — TIDAK ADA KODE EKSEKUSI

PR ini hanya menambah 3 dokumen planning di `.kiro/specs/tracking-crash-and-export-upgrade/`. Belum ada perubahan kode. Tujuannya supaya rencana ter-track terlebih dahulu sebagai PR draft sebelum eksekusi — kalau context conversation antara user dan agent habis di tengah jalan, pelanjut bisa baca dokumen ini dan langsung pick up tanpa kehilangan keputusan-keputusan yang sudah dibuat.

## Yang dipecahkan

### Crash 1 — Battery permission

User tekan MULAI → dialog "izinkan di belakang layar" → tap Izinkan → app force-close.

### Crash 2 — Resume

User buka app pasca crash → popup "Lanjutkan tracking?" → tap Lanjutkan → app force-close lagi.

### Ekspor lebih lengkap

User mau file GPX yang berisi: nama nelayan, nama kapal, tanggal ekspor, info trip (nama, tanggal, total stats), info per tarikan (nomor + nama + warna jalur + jarak/durasi/kecepatan/arah/sapuan), penanda (nama + kategori + koordinat + catatan + tanggal). Plus filter (jalur saja / penanda saja / keduanya, ditambah filter rentang tanggal, per-trip, per kategori penanda).

## Lingkungan testing yang dilaporkan user

- HP: Redmi Note 10 Pro
- ROM: PixelOS (custom ROM, bukan stock MIUI)
- Android 14+ (PixelOS biasanya track ke AOSP terbaru)

Catatan: PixelOS = stock-Android-like, jadi bug bukan OEM-quirk Xiaomi. Akar masalah ada di kode kita atau interaksi `permission_handler` × `flutter_background_service` × Android 14+ foreground service rules. Lebih clean untuk debug.

## Isi dokumen

### `requirements.md`

6 Requirement, format EARS (Event-Action-Result-State), Bahasa Indonesia, dengan acceptance criteria + correctness properties:

- R1 — Tracking tidak crash saat permission battery dialog dijawab
- R2 — Crash recovery resume tidak crash
- R3 — Permission battery juga bisa diatur dari Settings
- R4 — GPX export memuat semua field yang user minta
- R5 — Filter ekspor lengkap (konten + tanggal + trip + kategori penanda)
- R6 — Per-trip share tetap ada (Opsi A)

### `design.md`

- Akar masalah crash diuraikan dari kode HEAD: permission battery dialog di hot path tracking, race dengan Android 14+ foreground service "5 seconds notification" rule, plus `detectRecoverableHaul` re-call `start()` saat service sebelumnya masih ada residue dari sesi crash.
- Solusi: pisahkan permission ke fire-and-forget background task **setelah** service stable, idempotent service start dengan `isRunning` guard, plus settings tile untuk re-grant manual.
- Struktur GPX baru lengkap dengan template XML output dan tabel mapping field user-request → lokasi di GPX (`<author>`, `<lsea:exporter>`, `<lsea:summary>`, `<lsea:trip>`, `<lsea:haul>`, `<lsea:marker>`).
- ExportFilter domain entity + ExportScreen UI revisi dengan 4 section filter (konten, rentang tanggal, trip subset, kategori penanda).

### `tasks.md`

9 phase, masing-masing dengan tugas-tugas yang punya definition-of-done konkret. Diatur supaya bisa dieksekusi sequential dari atas-ke-bawah, commit per phase untuk diff yang reviewable.

- Phase 1 — Crash Fix Tracking
- Phase 2 — Settings Tile untuk Battery
- Phase 3 — ExportFilter & DateRange domain
- Phase 4 — GpxExporter dukung filter & user profile
- Phase 5 — ExportService support filter
- Phase 6 — ExportScreen UI revisi
- Phase 7 — Per-trip share path
- Phase 8 — Wire-up final & polish
- Phase 9 — Push & PR

Ada section "Catatan untuk pelanjut konteks" di akhir `tasks.md` supaya kalau context window habis di tengah implementasi, pelanjut bisa pick up tanpa kehilangan rencana.

## Keputusan yang sudah final dengan user

- ✅ Format file: GPX saja (field tambahan masuk ke `<extensions>` namespace `lsea`)
- ✅ Permission battery: tetap auto-prompt + ditambah tile manual di Settings
- ✅ Field GPX yang masuk: nama nelayan, nama kapal, tanggal ekspor, info trip, info tarikan + warna, info marker + kategori
- ✅ Field GPX yang skip dulu: log book, tangkapan, lebar trawl per haul, status haul
- ✅ Filter ekspor: konten (jalur/penanda) + rentang tanggal + per-trip + kategori penanda
- ✅ Layar ekspor: Settings tetap (full filter), Trip detail share tetap (per-trip cepat)

## Cara review

Buka 3 file dalam urutan:

1. `requirements.md` — paham kenapa & apa yang user mau
2. `design.md` — paham bagaimana, terutama §2.1 (template output GPX) yang akan jadi kontrak
3. `tasks.md` — daftar pekerjaan langkah demi langkah

Kalau ada yang ingin diubah / ditambah sebelum eksekusi, comment di file yang relevan, lalu saya update commit.

## Dependencies

- Bergantung pada **PR #26** (`feat/integrate-pr23-pr24`) di-merge dulu ke `main`. PR #27 ini akan rebase ke main terbaru sebelum eksekusi.

## Estimasi

≈ 6-9 jam dev time, di-pecah jadi 9 phase yang bisa di-review terpisah.

body:
## 요약

React Native 릴리즈 번들에서 Metro와 달라진 평가 순서/링킹 의미론 때문에 실제 앱 부팅 중 순차적으로 드러난 런타임 오류들을 수정했습니다.

핵심은 `runBeforeMain`/`InitializeCore`를 Metro처럼 앱 엔트리와 user module 평가보다 먼저 실행하도록 되돌리고, 그 이후에 드러난 RN 릴리즈 전용 scope-hoist/CJS/worklet 경계 문제를 함께 막는 것입니다.

## 배경

Metro 릴리즈 번들은 대략 다음 순서를 유지합니다.

1. require 런타임 설치
2. 모듈 factory 등록
3. `runBeforeMainModule` 실행 (`InitializeCore` 등)
4. 앱 entry require
5. entry dependency 평가

여기서 2번의 factory 등록은 모듈 본문 실행이 아닙니다. 따라서 RN 전역 초기화(`queueMicrotask`, `performance`, `ErrorUtils` 등)는 앱/라이브러리 모듈 본문 평가보다 먼저 끝납니다.

반면 zntc 릴리즈 번들은 일부 ESM을 scope-hoist해서 module output에 본문을 직접 emit합니다. 기존 코드는 entry가 `__esm` 래핑된 경우 `runBeforeMain` 호출을 entry chain/body 쪽으로 미뤘고, 이 때문에 scope-hoisted user module이 `InitializeCore`보다 먼저 실행될 수 있었습니다.

## 수정 내용

### 1. runBeforeMain 실행 순서 보정

- single-file emitter와 chunk emitter 모두에서 entry가 `__esm` 래핑되어 있어도 `runBeforeMain`을 top-level module output 앞쪽에 emit하도록 변경했습니다.
- fallback 경로에서도 runBeforeMain이 이미 emit됐음을 기록해서 final entry chain에 중복으로 붙지 않도록 했습니다.
- `esm_wrap` 내부에서 entry body에 runBeforeMain을 끼워 넣던 경로를 제거했습니다.
- entry dependency chain은 기존처럼 entry factory 내부 nested require 의미론을 유지합니다. dependency를 top-level 개별 guard로 풀면, `ErrorUtils` 설치 후 throw가 swallow되어 entry 평가가 계속 진행될 수 있기 때문입니다.

이제 RN 릴리즈에서도 `InitializeCore`가 scope-hoisted user module보다 먼저 실행됩니다.

### 2. scope-hoisted named import rename 보존

실제 앱에서 다음 형태의 런타임 오류가 재현됐습니다.

```text
ReferenceError: Property 'isTestEnv$5' doesn't exist
```

원인은 `react-native-gesture-handler`의 `Pressable.tsx` 같은 consumer가 scope-hoisted되고, import target인 `utils`는 `__esm` wrap인 조합이었습니다.

- import binding은 먼저 canonical live binding 이름(`isTestEnv`)으로 rewrite됩니다.
- 이후 같은 모듈의 top-level canonical rename 루프가 import binding 심볼을 다시 `isTestEnv$N`으로 덮었습니다.
- 실제 emit에는 `var isTestEnv$N = ...`가 없으므로 런타임에서 undefined reference가 발생했습니다.

수정은 self top-level rename을 적용할 때 이미 import/live-binding rename이 존재하면 덮어쓰지 않도록 했습니다.

### 3. RN CJS named import tree-shaking 보정

RN platform에서 CJS named import가 사용된 경우에도 CJS export assignment statement가 제거될 수 있었습니다. 이 문제는 `react-native-is-edge-to-edge`류의 CJS wrapper에서 `exports.isEdgeToEdge = ...`가 사라지는 형태로 드러났습니다.

- opaque module seed 단계에서 target이 CJS이면 일반 import follow 로직과 같은 방식으로 처리합니다.
- namespace import는 전체 statement를 보존합니다.
- default import + used properties는 해당 CJS export를 seed합니다.
- named import는 해당 CJS export assignment를 seed합니다.

이로써 사용 중인 CJS named export의 할당문은 유지하고, 미사용 export는 계속 제거할 수 있습니다.

### 4. worklet closure global 목록 보정

`react-native-worklets`/Reanimated worklet 변환에서 RN/Hermes 런타임 전역이 closure로 캡처될 수 있었습니다. 릴리즈에서 이 값들이 RN 초기화 이전 또는 다른 runtime context 기준으로 캡처되면 `queueMicrotask`, `performance` 계열 오류로 이어질 수 있습니다.

- `performance`, `queueMicrotask`, `setImmediate`, `clearImmediate`, `HermesInternal`, `_WORKLET`, `_IS_FABRIC` 등을 closure capture 제외 목록에 추가했습니다.
- `react-native-worklets` Babel plugin의 기본 `notCapturedIdentifiers`에 맞춰 error constructors, BigInt/Atomics/WeakRef 등도 보강했습니다.

## 왜 개발 빌드에서는 괜찮았나

개발 번들은 HMR/디버깅을 위해 대부분의 모듈을 factory 형태로 lazy 평가합니다. 즉 Metro와 마찬가지로 “모듈 등록”과 “모듈 본문 실행”이 분리되어 있고, `InitializeCore`가 먼저 실행될 기회가 있습니다.

이번 문제들은 주로 zntc 릴리즈 최적화에서 발생했습니다.

- scope-hoist된 ESM 본문이 output 중 즉시 평가됨
- entry `__esm` 래핑 시 runBeforeMain 호출이 너무 늦게 배치됨
- 한 스코프로 합쳐진 이름 공간에서 import rename이 self canonical rename에 덮임
- CJS wrapper statement-level tree-shaking이 RN CJS named import를 충분히 seed하지 못함

따라서 dev에서 숨겨졌다기보다는, 릴리즈 최적화 경로가 Metro의 평가 순서와 일부 import/export 의미론을 보존하지 못한 것이 root cause입니다.

## 테스트

추가/수정한 회귀 테스트:

- `entry_error_guard #5b`
  - runBeforeMain이 final entry trigger 쪽에 남지 않고 module output 앞쪽에 분리되는지 확인합니다.
- `entry_error_guard #5c`
  - runBeforeMain 호출이 scope-hoisted user module body보다 먼저 emit되는지 확인합니다.
- `entry_error_guard #5d`
  - `__esm` wrapped target에서 named import를 받는 scope-hoisted consumer가 `isTestEnv$N` 같은 미정의 rename을 남기지 않는지 확인합니다.
- `TreeShaking CJS: react_native named import keeps used exports dot assignment`
  - RN platform CJS named import가 사용 export assignment는 보존하고 unused export는 제거하는지 확인합니다.
- `Worklet: react-native-worklets default globals are excluded from closure vars`
  - RN/worklets 기본 전역들이 worklet closure에 캡처되지 않는지 확인합니다.

실행한 검증:

```sh
zig build test -Dtest-filter="entry_error_guard #5d"
zig build test -Dtest-filter="entry_error_guard #5"
zig build test -Dtest-filter="Worklet:"
zig build test -Dtest-filter="TreeShaking CJS:"
zig build test
zig build napi
```

추가로 실제 대형 RN iOS simulator Release 앱에서 zntc 번들을 사용해 빌드/설치/실행까지 확인했습니다.

- `--mode Release --no-packager`
- Xcode RN bundle phase에서 zntc `bundleRn()` 사용
- 설치된 앱 `main.jsbundle`: Hermes bytecode
- Xcode 중간 JS bundle: `__zntc_guarded` 포함, `isTestEnv$...` 미정의 호출 없음
- 35초 console 로그에서 `runtime not ready`, `ReferenceError`, `TypeError`, AppRegistry 미등록 오류 없음

## 남은 메모

이번 PR은 RN 릴리즈 런타임 의미론 보존에 초점을 둡니다. 앱 내부 API 404, 외부 SDK 경고, simulator 접근성 bundle 중복 경고는 zntc 번들러 런타임 오류와 별개라 이 PR 범위에서 다루지 않았습니다.

body:
Running qsdev init and then devenv shell fails immediately due to three bugs in the generated devenv.yaml:

git-hooks input was generated with both url and follows set — devenv rejects this combination, they are mutually exclusive
follows was serialized as a nested YAML map instead of a plain scalar string — devenv expects follows: nixpkgs not follows:\n  nixpkgs: nixpkgs
Follows field typed as map[string]string in both DevenvYamlInput and ecosystem.DevenvInput — should be string

Fix

Changed Follows field type to string in both structs
Removed Follows from git-hooks input (URL only is correct)
Fixed addInputNode to serialize follows as a scalar string
Updated tests accordingly

Tested by
Running qsdev init on a real project and attempting devenv shell — confirmed these bugs block first-time users completely.

body: This PR fixes broken 3D, satellite, and map UX, adds location support, and restores favorites/watchlist flows by unifying them under the map-first theme and adding stable visual previews. **Frontend Pages (`frontend/app/`)** * **Map** (`/map`): Replace dark “Premium GIS” theme with map-first light palette; add geolocation button with nearby parcel checks; default to demo parcel features to prevent empty screen on load; replace `alert()` errors with status messages. * **Satellite** (`/satellite`): Add `NativeMapCanvas` visual preview alongside BBOX/date form; unify layout style with map-first shell. * **Simulation** (`/simulation`): Replace unstable Cesium lazy-loader with stable static `CesiumViewer` preview showing building mass and parcel context to prevent WebGL crashes; remove emojis from compliance results. * **Watchlist** (`/watchlist`): Wire `saveFavorite` and `getFavorites` APIs to UI; replace alerts with in-page status; add map canvas preview. **Components (`frontend/components/`)** * Add `NativeMapCanvas`: Reusable map visual with search pill, locate, tool stack, and info card. * **MapViewer**: Add `MapFallback` and `supportsWebGL` checks to handle browser limitations gracefully without empty screens; fix WMS layer initialization and palette. * **CesiumViewer**: Rewrite from lazy-loading dynamic 3D to a stable static preview component with `ParcelBlock` and metrics to fix “3D broken” complaints. * **SimulationPanel**: Remove emoji usage from compliance results to match design policy. --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Medium risk because it rewires key user flows (map rendering/WMS layering, geolocation, favorites/watchlist fetching) and replaces the Cesium runtime viewer with a non-WebGL preview, which could change expected behavior across multiple pages. > > **Overview** > Unifies `/map`, `/satellite`, `/simulation`, and `/watchlist` under a new *map-first* light UI shell and replaces disruptive `alert()` failures with persistent in-page status messaging so users don’t see empty/blocked screens. > > Improves map resilience and capability: `/map` now supports **browser geolocation** (including a `getNearby` check), defaults to **demo parcel GeoJSON** when no results are returned, and passes locate/status controls down to `MapViewer`; `MapViewer` adds **WebGL detection + fallback rendering**, and fixes WMS raster layer creation to be added/updated dynamically with default activation. > > Restores/extends data flows and previews: `/watchlist` now loads watchlist + favorites together and can **save favorites** via `saveFavorite`/`getFavorites`, while `/satellite` and `/simulation` add a reusable `NativeMapCanvas` visual preview; `CesiumViewer` is rewritten from lazy-loaded Cesium WebGL to a **static 3D preview** to avoid runtime WebGL/Cesium failures, and `SimulationPanel` updates result styling/text (including removing emoji status strings). > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit fc78118816c7ad4ac4b27b2adc136747f21dd976. body:
## Summary

Adds standards-based OpenID Connect authentication support to the template authentication module.

This implementation keeps OIDC provider setup isolated from `Program.cs`, binds provider settings from configuration, and keeps authentication disabled by default so the application continues to run normally unless explicitly enabled.

Closes #27

## Changes

- Added OpenID Connect authentication package reference.
- Added strongly typed OpenID Connect provider configuration.
- Updated authentication provider options to include OIDC-specific settings.
- Implemented OIDC registration through the existing authentication extension structure.
- Configured cookie authentication as the local sign-in scheme for OIDC.
- Added configurable OIDC values for:
  - Scheme
  - Display name
  - Authority
  - Client ID
  - Client secret
  - Callback path
  - Response type
  - Token saving
  - Scopes
- Updated `appsettings.json` with disabled-by-default OIDC configuration.
- Updated README documentation with OIDC enablement and configuration guidance.
- Preserved clean startup configuration by keeping provider-specific setup out of `Program.cs`.

## Validation

- Confirmed the application builds successfully.
- Confirmed the application starts with authentication disabled.
- Confirmed OIDC remains disabled by default.
- Confirmed no provider-specific values or secrets are hardcoded.
- Confirmed OIDC can be configured through application settings without code changes.

## Notes

This PR adds standards-based OIDC support only. Provider-specific convenience configuration for Microsoft Entra ID, Auth0, Okta, Keycloak, Google, or other providers can be handled in future issues if needed.

author: 1utkarsh1
body:
## Related issue

Related to #2509. A near-duplicate issue, #2510, was closed by #2517 when the first Jury implementation merged. #2509 is still open, so this PR is a focused follow-up rather than a full reimplementation of the original feature request.

## Summary

This PR updates `Jury` so direct calls can pass arguments the same way the wrapped provider method accepts them. Before this change, `Jury` exposed the provider method signature for Metric selector validation, but `Jury.__call__` only accepted keyword arguments internally. That worked for the Metric path, but made direct provider-style usage inconsistent with the advertised signature.

It also adds the LLM jury research references from #2509 to the docs page.

## What changed

- Forward both `*args` and `**kwargs` from `Jury.__call__` to each juror method.
- Copy keyword arguments per juror before dispatch so one juror cannot affect another by mutating its local kwargs.
- Keep the existing Metric keyword-argument path unchanged.
- Add regression tests for direct positional calls.
- Add regression tests for mixed positional and keyword arguments.
- Add regression coverage for independent kwargs across multiple jurors.
- Add the research references requested in the LLM jury docs checklist.
- Add a short docs note about provider instances and credentials.
- Apply notebook formatting produced by CI's all-file pre-commit hook.

## Checklist

- [x] Keeps `Jury` as a drop-in callable for `Metric`.
- [x] Preserves the current parallel juror execution flow.
- [x] Preserves existing aggregation behavior.
- [x] Covers direct positional calls in unit tests.
- [x] Covers mixed positional/keyword calls in unit tests.
- [x] Covers independent kwargs handling across multiple jurors.
- [x] Updates docs without changing the Jury example notebook.
- [x] Avoids new dependencies.

## Why

The `Jury` object sets `__signature__` from the wrapped provider method so callers and Metric validation see the expected parameter names, such as `prompt` and `response`. With the previous implementation, a direct call like this failed even though it matched the provider method shape:

```python
score, meta = jury("What is TruLens?", "An eval library.")
```

After this change, `Jury` forwards those arguments to each juror exactly as received. Metric-based usage still works because keyword arguments are forwarded the same way as before.

The latest update also gives every juror dispatch its own kwargs dict. That avoids accidental cross-juror interference if any dispatch path mutates top-level keyword arguments.

## Testing

- `uvx --with-editable src/core --with-editable src/feedback --from pytest pytest tests/unit/test_jury.py -q`
  - `33 passed`
- `uvx pre-commit run --files src/feedback/trulens/feedback/jury.py tests/unit/test_jury.py docs/component_guides/evaluation/llm_jury.md`
  - passed
- `uvx pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`
  - first run reproduced the Azure pre-commit notebook cleanup
  - second run passed

## Review and CI follow-up

- Addressed Copilot review feedback by copying kwargs per juror dispatch.
- Added a two-juror regression test where the dispatch path mutates kwargs and both jurors still see the expected original argument.
- Addressed the Azure `py311-static` pre-commit failure by committing the notebook cleanup produced by the full pre-commit run.

## Risk

Low. The runtime change broadens argument forwarding from keyword-only forwarding to normal Python call forwarding and isolates top-level keyword arguments per juror. Existing Metric calls continue to pass keyword arguments, and the new tests cover the direct-call and multi-juror kwargs cases.

## Notes

I used `Related to #2509` instead of a closing keyword because the main Jury feature was already merged in #2517 via #2510. This PR is a compatibility/docs follow-up for the still-open #2509 thread.

## Summary

Resolves all 12 open `practice_qa_flags` rows filed by a prior Opus QA pass on `statistics-aqa`'s `representing-data` and `numerical-measures` units. Each fix is a minimum surgical edit so the question stem, chart data, misconception text, and `solutions` all agree.

Supabase `lessons.practice_data` was PATCHed in lockstep with the JSON files, and each flag is already marked `status='fixed'` in `practice_qa_flags`.

## Flags fixed (12)

### HIGH (9)

| Flag | Lesson + path | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `c6738995` | rd-l2 bronze[3] | Added stem `"What is the difference in January sales...?"` (sol stays `[15]`) |
| `8b481094` | rd-l2 silver[2] | Added stem `"What percentage of Product B...in-store?"` (sol stays `[25]`) |
| `1e34f8cb` | rd-l2 silver[4] | Flipped direction Yr11 > Yr10; sol `[-4]` -> `[4]`; misconception text aligned |
| `3810b429` | rd-l2 gold[2] | Stem-and-leaf IQR sol `[18]` -> `[19]` (half method on n=9: Q1=45, Q3=64) |
| `b8e5423b` | rd-l2 gold[3] | Added stem `"What percentage of Group 1 is in Segment C?"` (sol stays `[31.25]`) |
| `1930caea` | rd-l3 gold[2] | MCQ correct option `[1]` -> `[0]` to match chart data (untrained peaks at 200ms, trained positively skewed) |
| `5b576f84` | rd-l5 silver[0] | Median sol `[36.7]` -> `[31.7]` (matches misconception's calc) |
| `f39fad96` | rd-l5 gold[1] | Q1 sol `[22.5, 37]` -> `[20, 37]` (Q1 sits exactly on plotted point x=20, cf=25) |
| `47ac5806` | nm-l7 gold[0] | Spearman sol `[11]` -> `[14]`; misconception text reworded (drops self-correcting "wait recheck" narrative) |

### MEDIUM (2)

| Flag | Lesson + path | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `9246b821` | rd-l5 bronze[2] | Boxplot min `20` -> `10` (was below Q1=15 — impossible geometry). IQR=20 answer preserved. |
| `25362ece` | rd-l5 gold[5] | Option [1] text `"lower fence of 22"` -> `"lower fence of 12"`. Solutions pointer unchanged. |

| Flag | Lesson + path | Change |

author: goccy
body:
Resolves the one remaining open code-scanning alert.

**Alert #86** — `go/incorrect-integer-conversion`, `internal/functions/spanner/mysql_helpers_extra.go:1133`:

> Incorrect conversion of an unsigned 32-bit integer from `strconv.ParseUint` to a lower bit size type `int32` without an upper bound check.

In the `\uXXXX` branch of the MySQL-style JSON string unescaper, `n` was parsed with `strconv.ParseUint(s[i+1:i+5], 16, 32)` and then converted to `rune` (int32). CodeQL flags this because a 32-bit unsigned value can exceed the `int32` range.

A `\uXXXX` escape is always exactly four hex digits — a 16-bit UTF-16 code unit — so the correct `bitSize` is `16`. That bounds `n` to `0xFFFF`, which fits in `rune` safely.

**No behavior change:** four hex digits never exceed `0xFFFF`, so `bitSize 16` rejects nothing that `bitSize 32` accepted. `go test ./internal/functions/spanner/` passes.

author: nhm7
body:
## Summary

When the Python script is invoked at the end of a pipe (`brew outdated | python3 ...`), Python defaults to block buffering on stdout. This means `print()` calls are held in a buffer and only flushed at exit — *after* `subprocess.run(["brew", "upgrade", ...])` has already written directly to the file descriptor. The result is garbled log output:

```
==> Upgraded 1 outdated package          ← brew output (unbuffered, appears immediately)
nhm7/aged-upgrade/aged-upgrade 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0
==> Upgrading nhm7/aged-upgrade/aged-upgrade 1.2.0 (5d old)   ← should have appeared first
```

**Fix:** `sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)` at the top of `run()` flushes each `print()` immediately, keeping log lines in the correct order. This also fixes log ordering in the launchd log file.

One line change.

author: alex-budanov
body:
## Summary
- **PR-C of the tiny dedup-rule engine** (Phase 0.5). Builds on #142 (capability interface) and #143 (schema + storage). Reopened from #145 to consolidate review history. No user-visible behaviour yet — admin UI lands in PR-D.
- New `src/services/rules/` module: pure evaluator, action dispatcher (routes `ticket.add_comment` / `ticket.transition` through the capability registry), atomic throttle-backed rate limiter, executor with full error containment.
- Outbox worker hook: right after `markSkipped('duplicate_of_set')`, fire the `outbox_about_to_skip` trigger.

## Hardening from prior review rounds (all already applied)

**Correctness / security:**
- Atomic `NotificationThrottleRepository.tryReserveSlot` — single `INSERT ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE WHERE count < $max RETURNING`; max-count contract holds under concurrent workers.
- Migration 023 drops the `notification_throttle.rule_id` FK so dedup-rule UUIDs are accepted; migration 024 restores CASCADE-on-delete via a trigger on `notification_rules` (prevents orphan rows).
- `loadReporterTier` filters `subscriptions.status IN ('active', 'trial')` so canceled / past_due / paused orgs fall through to null.
- `TicketsTableResolver` filters `br.deleted_at IS NULL` so soft-deleted canonicals can't receive engine actions.
- `RuleContextProvider` methods all scoped by `projectId`; `CanonicalTicketResolver` and `CapabilityServiceLookup` ditto — cross-tenant defense-in-depth at every boundary.
- `daysSinceClose` returns null unless canonical is `closed`/`resolved` — stale open tickets no longer match `closed_days_ago >= 7`.
- Multi-window cache key (`hits_in_window:<window>`) so two conditions on different windows don't alias.
- Per-rule try/catch around rate-limit + dispatch path; one bad rule can't abort the loop.
- Order: `markSkipped` FIRST, then fire — retries hit the terminal-state early-out, no double-fire.
- Rate-limit fallback chain: `canonical.id ?? duplicate_of ?? bugReport.id` (cluster-stable).
- `windowStringToMinutes` rounds up (Math.ceil) so sub-minute windows are strictly more conservative.
- `tryReserveSlot` fails closed on `maxNotifications < 1` or `windowMinutes < 1`.

**Throttle-budget protection:**
- New `ActionDispatcher.canDispatch(action)` probe; executor skips rules whose actions are all unwired (`notify.*` in PR-C) so the rate-limit slot isn't burned for zero work.

## Deliberately out of scope
- `duplicate_detected` trigger wiring — lands with PR-C2 alongside the email handler.
- `notify.email` / `notify.slack` / `notify.webhook` action dispatchers — recognised but `canDispatch` returns false.
- `cluster_growing` / `schedule` triggers — need an aggregator / cron worker respectively.
- Trigger on `dedup_rules` deletion → throttle cleanup — lands with the dedup-rule deletion path in PR-D.

## Test plan
- [x] 78 unit tests across 5 files (evaluator, executor, dispatcher, rate-limiter, outbox-worker hook)
- [x] Integration tests for `tryReserveSlot` (FK-drop, atomic TOCTOU, param validation, cascade trigger)

author: gr8gatsby
body:
## Root cause (confirmed via work-machine diagnostic)

Work-machine v1.3.5 diagnostic showed:
\`\`\`
session_stop=1, user_prompt=2, pre_tool_use=92, ...
\`\`\`
plus a wall of \`ConnectionResetError\` / \`JSONDecodeError\` in the daemon log. Half the Stop hooks were dropped before reaching the daemon — that's the "terminal responded, iPhone never saw it" bug.

Each socket handler was \`await\`-ing two MCP emits back to AskMac before returning, holding the connection open for the full RPC round-trip. Under load (~90 pre_tool_use events in seconds) the accept queue saturated, hook clients timed out, kernel RST'd, daemon read empty bytes on the eventual accept. Hooks exited silently.

## Fix

**Daemon side:** Hot socket handlers (pre_tool_use, tool_executed, user_prompt, session_stop, session_start) now \`_fire_a2a(...)\` the AskMac emits instead of awaiting them. Registry mutations still persist synchronously before returning — only the AskMac emits become background.

**Hook side:** Shared \`_ipc.py\` with \`send_to_daemon(payload, max_attempts, timeout)\`. Retries on ConnectionResetError / ConnectionRefused / FileNotFound / timeout up to 3 attempts with 100/250ms backoffs. \`permission_request\` keeps 1 attempt / 0.5s because it's user-blocking.

## Test plan
- [x] \`_ipc.py\` unit smoke: happy path delivers; retry path with late-binding server delivers in ~360ms (was: instant fail)
- [x] All 8 hooks parse-check + import _ipc
- [x] main.py parse-checks
- [ ] Reproduce previous workload on work machine: \`session_stop\` count should now equal \`user_prompt\` count

author: mellanon
body:
refs cortex#237

Wires `publishCapabilityRegistry` (shipped in PR-3, #284) into
`startCortex`'s boot sequence per
[`docs/design-capability-dispatch-review-consumer.md`][spec] §3.4
(boot loop) and §10.1 PR-7 (per-PR scope row).

[spec]: https://github.com/the-metafactory/cortex/blob/main/docs/design-capability-dispatch-review-consumer.md

## Summary

- New block in `src/cortex.ts:495-589` (after `mergedAgents` + `systemEventSource`, before `BusDispatchListener.start()`):
  - Projects `mergedAgents` → `CapabilityRegistryEntry[]` keeping only agents whose `runtime.capabilities[]` is non-empty.
  - When the list is non-empty: invokes `publishCapabilityRegistry` with the `systemEventSource` shape (identical to `CapabilityRegistrySource`) and a wrapped publisher that traps per-envelope errors via `process.stderr.write` and continues.
  - When the list is empty: logs `cortex: capability-registry skipped — 0 agents declare runtime.capabilities[]` and emits nothing.
- New test file `src/__tests__/cortex.capability-boot.test.ts` (5 cases): happy-path N publishes, per-envelope failure with stderr capture + sibling envelope still emits, zero-agents-with-capabilities, mixed roster, double-boot idempotency (re-emission with same `agent_id` per §3.3's bucket-overwrite contract).

## Wiring details

- **Where:** `src/cortex.ts:495` — immediately after `systemEventSource` is declared and before any other subsystem that consumes the runtime starts publishing/subscribing. Re-uses the same source struct (structural `{org, agent, instance, dataResidency?}` shape).
- **Error handling:** the publisher's own JSDoc states it does NOT catch publish errors; they propagate. The wiring wraps the injected `publish` so per-envelope failures log to stderr with the failing `agent_id` + message and continue the loop. Boot never aborts on a bus glitch.
- **Boot log:** `cortex: published N capability registration(s) for M agent(s)` (or the skip variant), matching the existing boot-log style.
- **Idempotency:** the publisher contract (per PR-3) is that re-invocation emits fresh envelopes but identical payload `agent_id` keys; the bucket consumer overwrites the slot. Double-boot test exercises this on the wire.

## Out of scope

- **Consumer / subscriber wiring** for the registry. The future consumer is the **operator-side dashboard** (deferred per §13.1 / §10.1's "future PR" note). This PR is publish-only.
- **Config-reload re-publish.** Capabilities live on `Agent.runtime.capabilities[]`, sourced from `inlineAgents` + the `agents.d/` fragments — NOT in `BotConfig`'s `SAFE_FIELDS` set. The BotConfig hot-reload callback at `cortex.ts:~1303` does not mutate the agent set. There is no agents.d/ fragment watcher running at the daemon level today; when one is wired, the re-publish belongs in that callback (documented inline at the call site).
- **KV bucket primitive.** §3.5 v1 is publish-only — the bucket reader ships when pilot Phase B.4 needs it.
- **PR-4's payload fields** (`sovereignty`, `max_concurrent`) — schema landed (#285), but PR-3's envelope builder doesn't yet carry them on the payload. That's a future small follow-up against `capability-registry.ts`, independent of this wiring.

## Acceptance gates

```
bunx tsc --noEmit         # clean
bun test src/             # 3183 pass / 0 fail (+5 new vs. main)
bun run lint              # 0 errors; 21 pre-existing warnings (unchanged)
```

- [x] Lint clean (0 new errors)
- [x] New tests pass: 5/5 in `cortex.capability-boot.test.ts`
- [x] Rebased on origin/main (merge-base `01a133b`)

body:
This PR establishes CopilotCurator as a wrapper over `github/awesome-copilot` by introducing a submodule-backed content layout and a scriptable flow to detect project context, plan module selection, and import modules into a target project’s `.github` directory.

- **Submodule-backed source of truth**
  - Added `awesome-copilot` as a git submodule.
  - Wrapper content now references modules directly from the submodule instead of duplicating sources.

- **Curated wrapper surfaces for core module types**
  - Added top-level wrappers for `instructions/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, and `hooks/`.
  - Each wrapper now includes:
    - `index.md` with representative links into `awesome-copilot`
    - `custom/` folder for user-authored `.md` content

- **CLI + planner/import engine**
  - Added `scripts/copilot-curator.sh` as the main entrypoint:
    - `context <project>`: analyzes project stack and writes `.github/copilot-curator-context.json`
    - `plan <project>`: prints selected awesome-copilot modules based on detected context
    - `import <project>`: copies selected modules into `.github/copilot-curator/modules`
  - Added `scripts/curator_modules.py` implementing:
    - language/framework/technology detection
    - module candidate discovery across core + plugin paths
    - keyword-based module scoring and selection with fallback defaults
    - import materialization preserving relative paths

- **Repository docs and hygiene updates**
  - Updated `README.md` with structure, setup, and command usage.
  - Added `.gitignore` entries for Python bytecode artifacts.

```bash
# Main workflow
scripts/copilot-curator.sh context /path/to/project
scripts/copilot-curator.sh plan /path/to/project
scripts/copilot-curator.sh import /path/to/project

# Direct Python invocation (optional)
python3 scripts/curator_modules.py plan --project /path/to/project
python3 scripts/curator_modules.py import --project /path/to/project
```

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> I want to create a repository that acts as a bit of a wrapper for the GitHub awesome-copilot repositories files. The structure will be the awesome-copilot repository used as a submodule. Then for the relevant directories like instructions, agents,skills,hooks,etc, there will be a directory with an index file to the relevant files within the submodule and a directory called custom where a user can add their own .md files for their uses. Lastly I want a scripts folder that will contain the brains of the app which is controlled through a main script that can later be configured as a function in a user's .bashrc or .zshrc. The scripts are where the users project will be examined for what programming languages are used, what frameworks, any addition technologies like azure, terraform, etc.  then the main script will create a context for the application that captures that information and writes it to the .GitHub directory if it exists in the project or creates it if it's missing. Then there is a python script that can be called to see what modules from the awesome-copilot repo will be pulled in and an import command to pull all of those files into the .GitHub directory

author: abfa41
body: ## Summary This PR migrates interview progress tracking from localStorage-only storage to a server-synced system. It enables cross-device and cross-browser persistence of user progress (completed questions, bookmarks, and last visited state), while safely migrating existing users without data loss. This fixes the core issue where user progress was previously device-bound and introduces a scalable foundation for analytics, resume functionality, and personalized learning features. --- ## Changes ### Backend - Added `UserInterviewProgress` model in Prisma schema to store per-user progress - Implemented `GET /api/interview-progress` endpoint to fetch user progress - Implemented `PATCH /api/interview-progress/:questionId` endpoint supporting: - complete / uncomplete - bookmark / unbookmark - visit tracking - Added upsert logic to initialize progress automatically for new users - Ensured all endpoints are auth-protected and user-scoped ### Frontend - Integrated `getServerProgress()` API call for initial hydration - Added `updateServerProgress()` for all progress mutations - Implemented optimistic UI updates with rollback on failure - Added debounced `visit` event tracking to prevent API spam during rapid navigation - Ensured UI state stays in sync with server response ### Migration - Added one-time localStorage migration for existing users - Safely merges: - completedIds (union) - bookmarkedIds (union) - lastVisitedId (server priority fallback) - Prevents duplicate migrations using `interview_progress_migrated_v1` flag - Ensures no loss of existing local or server data ### Reliability Improvements - Ensured no cross-account data leakage by isolating progress per user - Fixed rapid navigation issue by debouncing visit updates --- ## How to test ### 1. Fresh user (no data) - Clear localStorage + cookies - Login as new user - Open interview section - ✅ Expect empty progress state with no crashes ### 2. Existing localStorage user - Login with old user data in browser - Open interview section - ✅ Expect migration to run once - ✅ Expect data to appear on server - Refresh page - ✅ Migration should NOT run again ### 3. New device (server-only user) - Login on different browser/device - ✅ Expect server progress to load correctly - ✅ No loss of data ### 4. Mixed local + server data - Ensure both exist - Trigger migration - ✅ Expect union merge (no data loss) ### 5. Rapid navigation - Quickly navigate 5–10 questions - ✅ Only last visit event should be sent to server ### 6. Multi-user login - Login as user A, generate progress - Logout - Login as user B - ✅ No data leakage between accounts All test cases are passed ✔. --- ## Screenshots - No major UI changes in this PR - Get API request screenshot - - Patch API request screenshot ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Interview progress is now synced with the server so progress persists across devices. * Local progress is migrated to your account once after sign-in; visits and completions are recorded server-side and section completion milestones are tracked. * **Bug Fixes** * Signing out now clears interview progress stored on the device. author: bartelfe
body:
Zwei konkrete Bugs aus deinem Live-Test auf 2560×1440.

## 1) Aufriss-Section auf 2xl: zu viel leerer Space
Auf 1440px Höhe waren `min-h-[60vh]` (= 864px Header) und gleichzeitig die Carousel-Bühne mit `min(40vh, 380px)` capped — Header riesig, Foto verloren in der Mitte. Drei zusammengehörige 2xl-Tweaks:

| Element | Vorher | Nachher (2xl) |
|---|---|---|
| `Blatt03` Header `min-h` | 60vh | **42vh** |
| `AufrissCarousel` Bühne `h` | min(40vh, 380px) | **min(50vh, 580px)** |
| `AufrissCarousel` Bühne `max-w` | 1100px | **1280px** |
| `Blatt05` Detail-Header `min-h` | 70vh | **45vh** |

Unter 2xl (1536px) keine Verhaltensänderung — Polish auf Standard-Desktop/Mobile bleibt wie gehabt.

## 2) WebGL Context Loss in Brandschutz
> THREE.WebGLRenderer: A WebGL context could not be created. Reason: Web page caused context loss and was blocked

**Ursache:** GPU-Pressure. Auf 2560×1440 mit `dpr=2` ist das Framebuffer 5120×2880; kombiniert mit Bloom-Postprocessing + Shadow-Maps reicht das damit Chrome den Context proaktiv tötet und Folgeversuche blockt.

**Fix in `Scene.tsx`:**
- `dpr` cap reduziert von `[1, 2]` auf `[1, 1.5]`. Auf 2560×1440 ergibt das 3840×2160 statt 5120×2880 — immer noch retina-scharf, aber unter der Pressure-Schwelle.
- `gl.failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat: false` — wenn der Treiber den Context als "slow" flaggt, akzeptieren statt verweigern.
- `onCreated`-Hook installiert `webglcontextlost`/`-restored`-Listener. Ohne `preventDefault()` auf contextlost verweigert der Browser jede spätere Restore — der explizite Aufruf hält die Tür offen.

**Die Deprecation-Warning** `THREE.Clock deprecated, use THREE.Timer` bleibt absichtlich. Sie stammt aus three.js intern (drei 0.184 nutzt Clock noch), wird in der nächsten Three-Version automatisch wegmigriert. Nicht unser Code — und nur Warning, kein Error.

## Files
```
src/sections/Brandschutz/Scene.tsx                       (+33 / -2)
src/sections/Werkplan/blaetter/Blatt03Aufriss.tsx        (+1 / -1)
src/sections/Werkplan/blaetter/Blatt05Detail.tsx         (+1 / -1)
src/sections/Werkplan/components/AufrissCarousel.tsx     (+9 / -5)
```

## Test plan
- [ ] DevTools resize zu 2560×1440 (oder echter Monitor): Blatt 03 Aufriss Header nimmt nicht mehr 60% Viewport, Foto im Carousel deutlich größer
- [ ] Brandschutz-Section komplett durchscrollen mit DevTools-Performance-Tab offen: keine "context lost" Errors mehr in der Console
- [ ] Falls Context-Loss doch noch auftritt (z.B. nach Background-Tab-Wechsel): "WebGL context restored" Info-Log sichtbar
- [ ] Unter 1536px Breite (Standard-Desktop, Mobile): keine Verhaltensänderung im Aufriss-Layout
- [ ] Bloom + Shadow-Quality auf 2560×1440 noch akzeptabel mit dpr 1.5

author: mostafa-drz
body: ## Rationale End-of-month expense reporting is one of those tasks that doesn't feel hard until you're actually doing it: 10–20 receipt emails scattered across Gmail, each requiring you to open it, read the total, note the merchant, and copy it into a spreadsheet. The category guessing happens manually too — is this a travel expense or accommodation? Did that Amazon order count as equipment? The whole ritual takes 20–30 minutes and happens every month (or after every trip). It breaks not because any single step is hard but because the volume and context-switching make it tedious. This skill automates the hunting-and-extracting part: searches Gmail with multiple receipt-pattern queries, parses what it finds into structured line items, groups them by category, and hands the user a table that's ready to paste into a reimbursement form or save to Drive. The flag-personal step keeps it honest — it surfaces the Netflix renewal rather than silently dropping it, leaving the reimbursability decision to the user. --- ## Research sources | Source | Tier | What it informed | |--------|------|-----------------| | [Agent Skills overview — platform.claude.com](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview) | **Tier 1** (Anthropic official docs) | Confirmed Gmail and Drive MCP integrations are available in Desktop; varying network access constraint; frontmatter requirements (name ≤ 64 chars, description ≤ 1024 chars) | | [Meeting Preparation Checklist — Hyprnote](https://hyprnote.com/blog/meeting-preparation-checklist/) | **Tier 3** (practitioner blog, named authors) | Validated the pattern of multi-source context retrieval before a recurring ritual — informs the "Configuration" section structure and the "admit gaps" guideline | | [Google Calendar AI: The Ultimate Guide — GenFuse AI](https://genfuseai.com/blog/google-calendar-ai-the-ultimate-guide) | **Tier 3** (synthesis, named author) | Confirmed that automation tools for Gmail + Drive retrieval workflows are a validated category; no existing tool serves this use case natively within Claude Desktop | **Note on research pivot:** Phase B initially targeted `meeting-prep`, which had been built by the 2026-05-15 run and is open on PR #6. This skill was selected as a clean alternative — different data sources (Gmail receipts rather than Calendar/Drive docs), different output (structured expense table vs meeting brief), different trigger cadence (monthly vs per-meeting). **Rejected sources:** Expensify, Concur, and SAP marketing pages (Tier 4 vendor marketing); multiple "best expense app" listicles without author credentials (Tier 4 SEO content); AI-generated "ultimate guide to expense reporting" pages (Tier 4). --- ## Required integrations - **Gmail** — receipt/invoice search using multiple subject and sender patterns across a user-specified date range - **Google Drive** — optional: save the expense table as a Google Doc when the user confirms No MCP servers beyond Google Workspace are required. The skill degrades gracefully: if Gmail search returns nothing, it says so rather than fabricating entries. --- ## Icon preview ```xml ``` The receipt shape is universally recognizable. Three muted horizontal lines are the line items; the full-width line is the total separator. The green dot at the top-right anchors to the first line item — it means "verified/found", matching the skill's job of pulling confirmed charges from email. --- ## What I rejected - **`meeting-prep` (desktop, PR #6)** — already built by the 2026-05-15 run; selecting it again would be a duplicate PR on an open branch. - **`weekly-review` (desktop)** — overlaps with `workday-summary` (code skill) in spirit; the differentiation wasn't sharp enough to pass the "not a remix" bar. - A generic "Gmail search" wrapper — rejected for being a thin single-API call. author: reg2005
body:
Add first-class English/Russian internationalization across the web app and wire the selected language through the backend/ML pipeline.

This introduces an i18n layer with EN/RU resource bundles, a language preference setting, localized UI copy across the main product surfaces, and shared language typing so app routes, jobs, settings, and services can consistently resolve the active locale.

The ML/search pipeline is updated for multilingual workflows as well. Text embeddings now use the multilingual `Xenova/paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2` model, Russian search queries are normalized into canonical metadata filters without losing the original semantic query, suggestions can display localized text while preserving canonical backend values, and scene/vector descriptions can be generated in Russian from detected metadata. Transcription and reverse-geocoding also receive the selected language so language-specific results are produced closer to the source.

This also adds OpenAI-like API support for chat/model providers, including diagnostics that make provider configuration, routing, and compatibility issues easier to debug.

Reviewer notes:
- Existing text vector collections need to be rebuilt/reindexed after the text embedding model change.
- Canonical filter values remain English internally; Russian is used for UI display and query normalization.
- Russian scene descriptions are metadata-based rather than direct translations of BLIP captions, avoiding brittle caption translation while keeping generated descriptions localized.

author: its-me-prash
body:
## Summary

**Phase 2 PR #7/20** opener. Follow-on to PR #1 (consent-screen detection, merged) and ticket #183 (Auth Resilience für 2026).

Pre-v2.2.0 the IDK auth flow raised a generic \`TwoFactorRequiredError\` whether the IDP demanded an authenticator-app TOTP code or an email OTP. The Repairs UI then showed the same \"open the app and confirm the code\" copy in both cases, which left Email-OTP users staring at their authenticator-app trying to find a code that was actually sitting in their inbox.

## What's new

| Layer | Change |
|---|---|
| **`cariad/exceptions.py`** | New \`EmailTwoFactorRequiredError\` subclass of \`TwoFactorRequiredError\` — existing \`isinstance\` / \`except\` chains keep working |
| **`cariad/auth/idk.py` Auth0-path** | Detects \`/u/email-challenge\` URL fragment distinct from generic \`/u/mfa\` |
| **`cariad/auth/idk.py` Legacy-path** | Body markers \`email-otp\` / \`email-code\` / \`send-email-code\` checked BEFORE generic \`two-factor\` / \`2fa\` substring (both legacy POST sites updated) |
| **`coordinator.py`** | Catches email subclass FIRST (first-match handler order) → \`ValueError(\"email_two_factor_required\")\` |
| **`__init__.py`** | New \`_SETUP_ERRORS\` entry with \"Check your inbox\" copy |
| **`repairs.py`** | New \`_FIXABLE_REASONS\` + \`issue_map\` + \`clear_auth_issues\` entry |
| **8 lang files + strings.json** | New key in \`config.error\` (inline) AND \`issues\` (Repair card). DE/FR/ES/CS/NL/PL/SV native translations; EN canonical |

## Failsafe

- **Subclass relationship**: every existing \`except TwoFactorRequiredError\` handler throughout the codebase continues to catch this — no behavioural regression for unknown callers
- **Detection is purely additive**: if a body doesn't match the new email markers, fall-through to generic 2FA is unchanged
- **Translation fallback**: HA falls back to \`auth_failed\` template if a Repair card arrives with a key the current HA version doesn't recognise

## Test plan

- [x] 18 test cases in \`tests/test_v220_email_2fa_detection.py\`:
  - Exception-shape (subclass + isinstance chain + distinct message)
  - Legacy body-marker detection (3 markers + regression-shield for pure TOTP body)
  - Auth0 URL-marker detection (positive + 2 negatives)
  - Repairs registration (\`_FIXABLE_REASONS\` + \`_SETUP_ERRORS\` coverage)
  - **Translation coverage** parametrised over 8 langs × 2 sections + strings.json
  - **Exception-handler ORDER** source-level check that EmailTwoFactor handler precedes generic TwoFactor handler in coordinator.py
- [x] \`python -m py_compile\` clean on all 5 touched python files + test
- [x] All 9 JSON files parse cleanly
- [ ] CI green (7/7 checks)

## Restructure note

Plan re-baselined: 6 PRs done in Phase 1, 14 PRs remaining → total 20 PRs in v2.2.0. Numbering going forward is \`PR #N/20\`.

Marketing: *\"In the future, you should always check your e-mail first. And by 'in the future', I mean **starting now**.\"* — Marshall Eriksen

author: marcelo-rosas
body:
## Por quê

`cloudflared/config.yml` em main estava com **placeholders literais** (`<SEU_TUNNEL_ID>`), travando o tunnel container com `error parsing tunnel ID`. Mesmo se substituísse o UUID, o hostname `api.vectraclip.vectracargo.com.br` (2 níveis aninhados) não recebia cert SSL no plano Free do Cloudflare (Universal SSL cobre só `*.vectracargo.com.br`, 1 nível).

Esta PR consolida o que precisa pra o tunnel **funcionar end-to-end externo**.

## Mudanças

| Campo | Antes | Depois |
|---|---|---|
| `tunnel` | `<SEU_TUNNEL_ID>` | `7488faec-a04f-463c-a3fa-cb6cd0b0a205` (vectraclaw-api) |
| `credentials-file` | `/etc/cloudflared/<SEU_TUNNEL_ID>.json` | path real |
| `hostname` | `api.vectraclip.vectracargo.com.br` | `api-vectraclip.vectracargo.com.br` |

UUID em `config.yml` **não é secret** — só identifica o tunnel. O secret é o JSON em `cloudflared/<UUID>.json`, já gitignored (vide #127).

## Ações que aconteceram no painel Cloudflare (não no repo)

- DNS record `api.vectraclip.vectracargo.com.br` (CNAME→`b42b0634...cfargotunnel.com`, tunnel errado `ollama-tunnel`) → **deletado**
- DNS record novo `api-vectraclip.vectracargo.com.br` (CNAME→`7488faec...cfargotunnel.com`, proxied 🟠) → **criado**
- Tunnel `vectraclaw-api` (7488faec) public hostname **atualizado** pra `api-vectraclip.*`

## Validação end-to-end externo

```
GET  https://api-vectraclip.vectracargo.com.br/api/health → 200 (HTTP/2)
     body: {"status":"online","service":"VectraClaw Agent Engine"}
     server: cloudflare, cf-ray: 9fca5141995349ac-GRU
POST https://api-vectraclip.vectracargo.com.br/api/auth/login (creds inválidas) → 401
     body: {"detail":"E-mail ou senha incorretos"}
Cert: Let's Encrypt, CN=vectracargo.com.br, SAN inclui api-vectraclip.*
Tunnel local: 4 conexões registradas (GRU13, GRU13, GRU21, GRU17)
```

## ⚠️ Ação no frontend (fora do escopo desta PR)

O cliente em `app.vectraclip.vectracargo.com.br` precisa atualizar a base URL da API:
`https://api.vectraclip.vectracargo.com.br` → `https://api-vectraclip.vectracargo.com.br`

## Test plan
- [x] `docker compose up -d` sobe tunnel sem `error parsing tunnel ID`
- [x] Tunnel registra 4 conexões aos PoPs
- [x] `GET /api/health` externo retorna 200 com body
- [x] Cert TLS válido (Let's Encrypt via Cloudflare)
- [ ] Frontend atualizado para nova URL (PR separado)

author: tonichowbea
body:
**Stacked on #86. Targets `oddFEELING/openapi-typescript-axios` — please merge #86 first, then this PR re-bases against `main`.**

## Why

OpenAPI's `readOnly: true` and `writeOnly: true` annotations exist for a reason: server-controlled fields like `id` and `createdAt` shouldn't be in request bodies (the server ignores them anyway), and sensitive fields like `password` shouldn't be in response shapes (the server never sends them back).

Before this PR, chowbea-axios's generated helpers ignored both annotations. The type for a "create user" request body included `id`, and the type for "get user" responses included `password`. The type system was silently lying — letting consumers reference fields that either get ignored on the wire or never arrive.

This PR turns on openapi-typescript's `readWriteMarkers: true` option (which emits `$Read<T>` / `$Write<T>` markers inside generated types) and wraps the chowbea helpers in `Writable<...>` / `Readable<...>` resolvers from `openapi-typescript-helpers` to strip the markers in the right direction per usage.

## What changed

- `src/core/generator.ts:1159-1170` — `openapiTS()` call passes `readWriteMarkers: true`.
- `src/core/generator.ts` — helpers template imports `Readable` and `Writable` from `openapi-typescript-helpers`; wraps response helpers (`ApiResponseData`, `ServerResponseType`, `ServerSuccessResponse`) in `Readable<...>` and request helpers (`ApiRequestBody`, `ServerRequestBody`) in `Writable<...>`.
- `tests/types/fixtures/sample-api.types.ts` — adds an `Account` schema with inline `$Read<string>` / `$Write<string>` markers matching the upstream emission shape; adds `getAccount` / `updateAccount` operations exercising both stripping directions.
- `tests/types/api-helpers.test-d.ts` — 6 new `expectTypeOf` assertions verify `password` doesn't appear in account response types and `id` doesn't appear in account request types, for both path-keyed and operationId-keyed helpers.
- `tests/types/fixtures/sample-api.helpers.ts` — vendored fixture regenerated to match the new template.
- `tests/generator.test.snap` — helpers snapshot regenerated.

### Concrete consumer effect

Given a `User` schema with `id` readOnly and `password` writeOnly:

```ts
// Before — both types were just User, letting consumers misuse them
type UserResponse = ApiResponseData<"/users/{id}", "get">; // includes password
type UserCreate   = ApiRequestBody<"/users", "post">;        // includes id

// After — types match what the wire actually allows
type UserResponse = ApiResponseData<"/users/{id}", "get">; // password stripped
type UserCreate   = ApiRequestBody<"/users", "post">;        // id stripped
```

## Breaking changes

🚨 **This is a v3.0.0 cut.** Consumer code that relied on the old, overly-permissive shapes will fail to compile. Specifically code that:

- Sets `id` / `createdAt` / other `readOnly` fields in a request body
- Reads `password` / other `writeOnly` fields off a response

The fix is almost always to **remove** those reads or writes — the server was either ignoring them (readOnly → request) or never sending them (writeOnly → response). The "fix" is the type system finally telling you about a long-latent bug.

**Migration note:** Existing projects whose `api.helpers.ts` was generated under v2.x are *not* automatically updated — the helpers file is "generated once, never overwritten" by design. They keep their old types until they manually regenerate. A future migration helper (or a `--force-regenerate-helpers` CLI flag) would close that gap; not in this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 142 runtime tests pass (no change vs #86 — runtime behaviour identical)
- [x] `npm run test:types` — 36 type-level assertions pass (was 30 in #86; +6 read/write stripping tests)
- [x] `npm run test:types:strict` — vendored fixture compiles cleanly under strict mode
- [x] Pack-check confirms no new files leak into the published tarball

## Sources / related

- Stacked on #86 which adopted the upstream helpers vocabulary that this PR's wrappers depend on.
- `openapi-typescript-helpers`'s `$Read` / `$Write` / `Readable` / `Writable` types at the helpers source documented inline at line 113550-113595 of the reference bundle.
- Upstream config option: [`readWriteMarkers` in `OpenAPITSOptions`](https://openapi-ts.dev/cli#flags).

author: carlheinmostert
body:
## What changed

Two compounding re-use problems surfaced by the PR #376 + PR #377 review:

1. **`replaceFirst('_thumb.jpg', '_thumb_X.jpg')` scatter** — pattern was inlined at 9 call sites across `upload_service.dart`, `unified_preview_scheme_bridge.dart`, and `exercise_hero_resolver.dart`. Adding the 4th variant (`_thumb_bw.jpg`, PR #377) duplicated the pattern 7x; variant 5 would scale linearly.

2. **Fast-path / slow-path upload-block duplication** — `upload_service.dart` had near-identical ~50-line upload blocks for `_thumb_line.jpg` and `_thumb_bw.jpg` in both the fast-path (already-uploaded republish) and slow-path (fresh publish) branches. ~200 lines duplicated across four blocks.

This PR centralises both:

### New helper: `app/lib/services/thumb_paths.dart`

```dart
String thumbVariantPath(String thumbPath, String variant);
bool isVariantSwapValid(String thumbPath, String variantPath);
```

Single source of truth for variant-path derivation. All 9 inline swap call sites now go through these helpers. Mirrors the `web-player/hero_resolver.js` SSOT pattern (PR #364, `docs/HERO_RESOLVER.md`).

### New private helper: `UploadService._uploadThumbVariantToMedia(...)`

Collapses the four duplicated upload blocks into one. Handles:

* `thumbVariantPath` no-op guard (legacy pre-Bundle-2b photo rows)
* `File.exists()` on-disk check
* `existingFiles + thumbnailsDirty` override (2026-05-16 hero-thumb staleness fix)
* Success accounting: `uploadedPaths.add`, optional dirty-bookkeeping for fast-path, progress tick emit via injected `onSuccessTick` closure
* Failure recording: same `media_thumb_\${variant}_upload_failed` kind, same `debugPrint` line shape

Fast-path passes its `dirtyThumbUploadsByExercise` map for the early per-block dirty-clear pass; slow-path passes `null` (it clears dirty in a global post-upload pass).

### Call sites swept

* `upload_service.dart` lines 1310, 1362 (fast-path line, fast-path bw) — both now via `_uploadThumbVariantToMedia`
* `upload_service.dart` lines 1526, 1575 (slow-path line, slow-path bw) — both now via `_uploadThumbVariantToMedia`
* `upload_service.dart` line 2534 (raw-archive color) — via `thumbVariantPath`
* `unified_preview_scheme_bridge.dart` lines 211, 219, 233 (color, line, bw) — via `thumbVariantPath`
* `exercise_hero_resolver.dart` lines 288, 292 (line, color) — via `thumbVariantPath`

## Why

Carl cited this as compounding tech debt. PR #377 added the 4th thumb variant which duplicated the pattern 7x; the next variant (e.g. `_thumb_segmented.jpg`) would scale linearly. Same fragility class as the pre-PR-#364 hero-crop scatter — a typo in `_thumb.jpg` silently no-ops via the existing `if (path != original)` guard. Breaking the loop now keeps the next variant a 1-line change.

## No behaviour change verified by

* `dart analyze` — clean on all 4 modified files (zero errors, zero warnings)
* `flutter analyze` — clean across the whole app
* `flutter test` — all 24 tests pass, including:
  - `idempotent_migration_test`
  - `publish_dirty_state_test`
  - `studio_delete_rollback_test`
  - `capture_defaults_test`
* `grep -rn "replaceFirst.*_thumb" app/lib/` — only the helper definition + historical doc comments remain (0 inline swap sites)
* Same upload payloads, same failure-kind strings, same progress emit ordering, same debugPrint lines

## Net line change

`app/lib/services/upload_service.dart`: 2817 → 2801 lines (-16). The collapsed duplication frees ~100 lines; the new 90-line helper method costs ~90; net `-16` inside upload_service.dart plus the new 59-line `thumb_paths.dart` file. Adding variant 5 will now be a one-line `_uploadThumbVariantToMedia(variant: 'segmented', ...)` call rather than another ~50-line block per call site.

## Out of scope / follow-up

* `web-player/exercise_hero.js` — no analogous JS-side scatter discovered.
* `app/lib/services/conversion_service.dart` lines 1767-1770 — uses `p.join(thumbDir, '\${id}_thumb_X.jpg')` to construct paths from scratch, NOT `replaceFirst` from a canonical path. Different pattern; could be unified under a `thumbVariantInDir(dir, id, variant)` helper as a follow-up if a 5th variant lands.
* `get_plan_full` CASE-arm boilerplate in the SQL migrations — harder to abstract cleanly in PL/pgSQL; flagged in the original brief as separate.
