author: panda260
body:
This pull request enhances the reporting of ZFS pool storage metrics by distinguishing between logical and raw storage usage, and updates both the backend and frontend to support and display these new metrics. The backend now fetches the actual "used" bytes for each pool, while the frontend computes and displays both logical and raw storage statistics for improved accuracy and clarity.

**Backend improvements to pool metrics:**

* The backend (`rust-backend/src/routes/pools.rs`) now fetches the true used bytes for each ZFS pool using `zfs get used`, and includes this as `used_bytes` in the API response. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-978857a631ef37e15fd6a9559f0c0f7b3e1c016045be150550533603f20f9b03R199-R217) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-978857a631ef37e15fd6a9559f0c0f7b3e1c016045be150550533603f20f9b03R229)

**Frontend enhancements to storage reporting:**

* The frontend (`web/src/App.tsx`) updates pool mapping to use the new `used_bytes` value, and separately computes logical (actual used/available) and raw (reported by ZFS) capacity and usage. These are now tracked in state and passed to the dashboard. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2e5aec0d80c33c218d97cb48edb61724a5e25bfc33478de5907916a90a92accfL241-R256) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2e5aec0d80c33c218d97cb48edb61724a5e25bfc33478de5907916a90a92accfR143-R144) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2e5aec0d80c33c218d97cb48edb61724a5e25bfc33478de5907916a90a92accfR428)
* The dashboard component (`web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx`) is updated to accept and display both logical and raw storage metrics, and the main storage widget now shows both values and their percentages for better insight. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c89ce46baa4e05febf915fa586b16eccd3ad684563218c51acfdd4cff5118a9cR22-R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c89ce46baa4e05febf915fa586b16eccd3ad684563218c51acfdd4cff5118a9cL541-R543) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c89ce46baa4e05febf915fa586b16eccd3ad684563218c51acfdd4cff5118a9cR649-R655)

author: f-trycua
body:
## Summary

Ports Swift `PermissionsGate` to cua-driver-rs as a **terminal-driven** first-launch flow. Closes #1527.

When `cua-driver serve` starts on macOS and TCC grants for Accessibility or Screen Recording are missing, the gate now:

- prints a banner listing exactly which grant is missing and why cua-driver needs it
- raises the system TCC prompts (no-op when already granted)
- auto-opens the matching `System Settings → Privacy & Security` pane(s) via `x-apple.systempreferences:` URLs (the same URLs Swift's `PermissionsGate` uses)
- polls TCC state every 1s, prints "still waiting on X" every 5s
- auto-continues startup the moment everything flips green

Already-granted users see **no change** — the gate is a transparent no-op when both grants are active.

### Why CLI and not SwiftUI

- Rust port already drives an AppKit run loop on the main thread for the cursor overlay; grafting another window onto it invites main-thread deadlocks.
- Primary deployment shape is `cua-driver serve` from a shell (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) — terminal is already attached.
- Headless / CI needs an opt-out anyway; a terminal-driven flow with `--no-permissions-gate` is the straight-line approach.

A native `NSAlert` via objc2 is tracked as a possible follow-up. CLI is the MVP.

### Opt-out

| Signal                                          | Effect       |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| `cua-driver serve --no-permissions-gate`        | gate skipped |
| `CUA_DRIVER_RS_PERMISSIONS_GATE=0` env-var      | gate skipped |
| (any other env-var value, including unset)      | gate active  |

### Commits

1. `feat(platform-macos): permissions gate (CLI flow)` — new `permissions/{mod,status,gate}.rs`, 7 unit tests, `check_permissions` tool refactored to share the new `status` module.
2. `feat(cli): wire permissions gate into serve startup` — `--no-permissions-gate` flag + `Serve` arm call.
3. `docs: permissions gate (PARITY.md + installation + CLI reference)` — PARITY.md gets a new section under `check_permissions`; `installation.mdx` and `cli-reference.mdx` get the CI / headless opt-out recipe.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --release` clean (warnings unchanged from baseline).
- [x] `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib permissions::` — all 7 unit tests pass (opt-out logic, env-var parsing, missing-permission ordering, settings URLs match Swift verbatim).
- [ ] Manual: `cua-driver serve` on a fresh macOS box with grants revoked → banner appears, Settings opens, gate auto-continues on grant.
- [ ] Manual: `cua-driver serve` with both grants already active → no banner, no delay, normal startup.
- [ ] Manual: `cua-driver serve --no-permissions-gate` on a fresh box → no banner, daemon starts, tool calls fail with normal TCC errors.
- [ ] Manual: `CUA_DRIVER_RS_PERMISSIONS_GATE=0 cua-driver serve` → same behaviour as the flag.

author: markmichaelis
body:
Fixes #85.

## Root cause

Anthropic's winget manifest (`Anthropic.Claude` 1.7196.1) ships **two** installer flavors:

| # | Type | Scope | Notes |
|---|------|-------|-------|
| 1 | **MSIX** (x64/arm64) | machine-context (implicit) | Declares `RestrictedCapabilities: runFullTrust, unvirtualizedResources, localSystemServices, packagedServices`. Honored only on interactive desktop Windows with sideloading enabled. |
| 2 | **EXE** (x64/arm64) | `Scope: user` (explicit) | Squirrel installer dropping the app into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AnthropicClaude\`. |

There is **no machine-scope EXE/MSI** offered by Anthropic. With our previous `--scope machine` invocation winget picked the MSIX, which fails on GitHub-hosted Windows Server runners with `APPINSTALLER_CLI_ERROR_INSTALL_SYSTEM_NOT_SUPPORTED` (-1978334957) after hash verification — the runner can't satisfy `runFullTrust`.

## Fix

Set `Scope = 'user'` on the Claude Desktop `[Package]` entry in `bucket/AIAgents.ps1`. Both the module's `Install-WingetPackage` and `.github/scripts/Test-Installs.ps1`'s wrapper already plumb `--scope user` when `Scope='user'`, so winget will now select the per-user EXE installer — which is also Anthropic's actual deployment model (Electron + Squirrel auto-update writes to `%LOCALAPPDATA%`).

Removed `Anthropic.Claude` from `$script:CISkipPackages` in `.github/scripts/Test-Installs.ps1` so the Heavy validate-installs workflow exercises the real install path on the next push to `main`.

## Changes

- `bucket/AIAgents.ps1` — `[Package]` Claude Desktop gains `Scope = 'user'` with an explanatory comment.
- `.github/scripts/Test-Installs.ps1` — drop `Anthropic.Claude` from `CISkipPackages`.
- `.github/scripts/Test-Installs.Tests.ps1` — update one comment that mentioned the now-removed skip.
- `bucket/AIAgents.json` — version 1.16.001 → 1.17.000 (AIAgents.ps1 modified).

## Tradeoffs

- A user running `Install-Package 'Claude Desktop'` now installs into their own profile rather than machine-wide. This matches Anthropic's intent: Claude Desktop is a per-user Electron app whose auto-updater writes to `%LOCALAPPDATA%`. A machine-wide MSIX install couldn't roam to other user profiles either, so no real capability is lost.
- An admin running for someone else's profile would need to run as that user, same as for Slack/Discord/Teams/Cursor.

## Verification

- `Invoke-Pester bucket\Bundles.Tests.ps1` — 752 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped.
- `Invoke-Pester .github\scripts\Test-Installs.Tests.ps1` — same 17 pre-existing local failures as `main` (local env can't run `Get-Package` discovery; CI Light path is unaffected).
- Heavy `validate-installs.yml` runs on push to `main` only, so the true Claude Desktop install gets validated post-merge. If the user-scope EXE also rejects the runner, the workflow will auto-refile the issue with the new exit code/output.

author: amamparo
body:
## What this is

Two changes, one PR:

### 1. New kata 10: `assignments`

A linear instruction-list interpreter. Given a vector of `[:set sym v]`, `[:add a b dest]`, `[:mul a b dest]` instructions, return the final environment as a map.

```clojure
(interpret [[:set 'x 5]
            [:set 'y 3]
            [:add 'x 'y 'sum]])
;; => '{x 5, y 3, sum 8}
```

Synthesis kata — pulls together `reduce` (§7), maps (§9), and `ex-info` (§18). All prerequisites are taught by §18, so it sits between kata 9 and §19 (no new SENSEI section needed; a one-paragraph bridge in SENSEI signals it's coming).

The pedagogical role: exercises the env-as-map muscle that kata 14 (tree-walking interpreter) will generalise to recursion over trees. The student should land in kata 14 having already felt "I am threading an environment through a sequence of operations" — kata 14 then becomes "...but the operations are nested instead of flat."

### 2. Renumber 10→11, 11→12, 12→13, 13→14

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `kata-10-rpn` | `kata-11-rpn` |
| `kata-11-shapes` | `kata-12-shapes` |
| `kata-12-when-let-star` | `kata-13-when-let-star` |
| `kata-13-interpreter` | `kata-14-interpreter` |

Source files, test files, namespaces, headers, and SENSEI checkpoints all updated. The single intra-test full-namespace reference (`katas.kata-12-when-let-star/when-let*` inside a macroexpand assertion) was updated to the new name.

### 3. Square added to shapes (kata 12)

A fourth shape on both axes — `defrecord Square [s]` + `defmethod describe :square` — so the workload contrast between protocol-extension and multimethod-extension is visible while solving. The reflection paragraph in the kata gets a one-line nudge to compare what it took on each axis, without telling the student which one was easier.

## ⚠️ Cleanup needed before merge

The GitHub MCP's `delete_file` tool was timing out consistently from my side, so I couldn't remove the old paths. **Both old and new files currently live on the branch.** Before merging, please run locally:

```bash
git checkout kata/insert-assignments-and-extend-shapes
git rm src/katas/kata_10_rpn.clj \
       src/katas/kata_11_shapes.clj \
       src/katas/kata_12_when_let_star.clj \
       src/katas/kata_13_interpreter.clj \
       test/katas/kata_10_rpn_test.clj \
       test/katas/kata_11_shapes_test.clj \
       test/katas/kata_12_when_let_star_test.clj \
       test/katas/kata_13_interpreter_test.clj
git commit -m "remove pre-rename kata paths"
git push
```

Then the diff is clean. Alternative: GitHub web UI's file delete on each of the 8 paths.

## Why no test renumbering as a separate concern

Tests live one-to-one with their kata sources. The test file renames are mechanical (namespace + `:require` updated to point at the new source ns), no test logic touched. The shapes test gets four added Square assertions; everything else just moves.

body:

The final PR (9 of 9) of the cortex#237 cluster per

§10.1 (PR-9 row) + §11.1 Layer 2 (test layer contracts).

## What this closes

PRs already merged in the cortex#237 cluster (8 of 9):

- PR-2: `createReviewVerdictEvent` + `createReviewTaskFailedEvent` builders.

(`docs/design-capability-dispatch-review-consumer.md` §11.4 — ≥5
consecutive real review cycles across ≥2 PRs over ≥48 hours) can begin
once this merges.

## Test surface

Adds `src/__tests__/cortex.review-consumer.e2e.test.ts` driving the
spec §11.1 Layer 2 round-trip via:

- Real `ReviewConsumer` constructed against an in-process bus runtime
  that implements `MyelinRuntime.subscribePull` + `publish` with a
  subject-matching fan-out (matches the existing pattern from
  `iaw-phase-d-integration.test.ts` and `iaw-phase-b-integration.test.ts`).

  test seam) returning a fixed verdict envelope built via the real

  spec §11.2.
- Stubbed `JsMsg` with `ack`/`nak`/`term` mocks; the bus applies the
  consumer's returned `AckDecision` to the msg using the same
  `applyAckDecision` semantics as production `subscriber.ts`.

**Happy path (`tasks.code-review.typescript`):**
- handler invoked exactly once on the matching subscription
- `AckDecision = { kind: \"ack\" }` returned

**Failure path (`tasks.code-review.python` with no matching capability):**

author: connorburns19
body:
Mutating link.href on a <link rel="stylesheet"> doesn't reliably invalidate the CSSOM in WebKit when the new sheet is cached — the rule sheet swaps but style recalc is skipped, so CSS variables don't propagate to repaint. Tapping the same theme a second time nudges WebKit into the recalc, which is why iOS needed two taps.

applyPreset now creates a fresh <link> element per switch and removes the old one once the new sheet has loaded. New nodes force a full restyle on all engines, bypassing the WebKit cached-stylesheet quirk while still avoiding FOUC during the swap.

## Summary

## Problem

**Severity**: `High` | **File**: `tinker-android/tinker-android-lib/src/main/java/com/tencent/tinker/lib/patch/BsDiffPatchInternal.java`

This sibling class extracts native library entries from the same patch zip. It is subject to the same Zip Slip vector if it uses `ZipEntry.getName()` to construct destination paths under the patch lib directory.

## Solution

Refactor the entry-name validator into a shared utility (see suggested `PatchEntryUtils` below) and call it for every `ZipEntry` consumed in `patchFastExtractDiffInternals` / similar methods. Also perform the canonical-path containment check before writing each extracted file.

author: nc1107
body:
## Summary

This PR carries **four scope-aligned fixes** that came in via the iOS forensics loop.

### 1. iOS voice lounge crash — actual root cause (REGRESSION FROM EARLIER TODAY)
My own commit \`38e1e0a6\` ("pre-activate audio session and request mic permission before livekit") regressed iOS. The \`try session.setActive(true)\` in \`didFinishLaunchingWithOptions\` synchronously blocks the main thread waiting for the TCC mic-permission prompt — which can't be presented yet (no UIScene up). iOS watchdog SIGKILLs at 20-30s. Symptoms match the production report exactly: orange dot, zero Dart breadcrumbs, zero \`/api/voice/token\` requests on server. 

**Fix**: remove the launch-time \`setActive\` call. Set the category only. LiveKit's \`LocalAudioTrack.create\` activates the session itself at the right moment (after a UI scene exists + after explicit mic permission via \`permission_handler\` in joinChannel). Also dropped \`.mixWithOthers\` from the option set — it fought with \`.voiceProcessingIO\` that LiveKit installs.

### 2. Synchronous log flush (precondition for diagnosing future iOS hard-crashes)
- New \`DebugLogService.forceFlushSync()\` uses \`File.writeAsStringSync\` — POSIX blocking write, ~1-3ms on iOS NAND for the 5000-entry buffer.
- Voice-tap handler in \`channel_bar.dart\` now uses sync flush — breadcrumb is guaranteed on disk before the next line of code runs.
- Global error handlers (\`FlutterError.onError\`, \`PlatformDispatcher.onError\`, \`runZonedGuarded\`) all upgraded to sync flush.

### 3. Window starts off-screen
\`WindowStateService.save()\` was persisting the 300×300 splash geometry, putting the window's top-left at the screen center on the next launch. Guarded \`save()\` to refuse to write geometry smaller than the minimum restore thresholds (720×480).

### 4. Joining feels hung — no feedback during the ~2s connect
Chip in the channel bar now shows a \`CircularProgressIndicator\` (sized to the icon slot for the current density) while the join chain is in flight, cleared in \`finally\` so failures don't leave a stuck spinner. Existing dock-side \`_buildJoiningIndicator()\` already covered post-connect; this adds the pre-connect bridge.

## Test plan
- [x] \`flutter test\` — 1565 tests pass including new sync-write timing test + chip-spinner widget test
- [x] \`flutter analyze --fatal-infos\` clean
- [ ] CI green on dev
- [ ] Merge to main; iOS rebuild
- [ ] iOS beta tester:
  - Launch should no longer hang at 30s watchdog
  - If a crash STILL happens, the new sync-flushed breadcrumbs will pinpoint the exact failure step
  - Desktop window should now open at the previously-saved position OR centered, not off-screen

body: ## Summary After PR [#388](https://github.com/verity-org/verity/pull/388) switched the gitea chart to single-node `postgresql` + `valkey` subcharts (avoiding the HA-subchart DNS-convergence timeout), the install still failed because Bitnami migrated their gitea image to the `bitnamilegacy` namespace. `docker.io/bitnami/gitea` now returns an empty manifest; only `docker.io/bitnamilegacy/gitea:1` is published. ## Diagnosis chart-integration run [25972171694](https://github.com/verity-org/verity/actions/runs/25972171694) (gitea shard) diagnostic dump: ``` gitea-f7d8d8cf8-l4vnz [Pending] init-directories: waiting/ImagePullBackOff: Back-off pulling image "docker.io/bitnami/gitea:1": ErrImagePull: rpc error: code = NotFound desc = failed to pull and unpack image "docker.io/bitnami/gitea:1": failed to resolve reference "docker.io/bitnami/gitea:1": not found gitea-postgresql-0 [Running] OK gitea-valkey-primary-0 [Running] OK ``` Confirmed via `crane`: - `crane ls docker.io/bitnami/gitea` → empty (404) - `crane ls docker.io/bitnamilegacy/gitea` → lists `1`, `1-debian-11`, `1-debian-12`, `1.17.3`, ... - `crane manifest docker.io/bitnamilegacy/gitea:1` → valid amd64/arm64 manifest list The postgresql + valkey subcharts were already correctly pointing at `bitnamilegacy/*` via their own chart defaults — they install successfully per the dump. Only the gitea top-level image needed the namespace fix. ## Changes - `verity.yaml`: - gitea chartValues: `image.repository: bitnamilegacy/gitea` (was `bitnami/gitea`) - `unpatchableImages`: `bitnamilegacy/gitea` (was `bitnami/gitea`) - `test/chart-integration/values/gitea.allowlist.txt`: `docker.io/bitnamilegacy/gitea:` + `@` (was `docker.io/bitnami/gitea:` + `@`) - Updated header comments in both files documenting the Bitnami migration ## Test Plan - Verified via `crane` that `bitnamilegacy/gitea:1` is published and resolves to a valid amd64/arm64 manifest. - `helm template gitea --set image.repository=bitnamilegacy/gitea ...` locally renders the 4 expected images: `bitnamilegacy/gitea:1`, `busybox:latest`, `bitnamilegacy/postgresql:17.6.0-debian-12-r4`, `bitnamilegacy/valkey:8.1.3-debian-12-r3`. - Unit tests: `go test ./internal/chartgen/...` + `go test -tags integration ./test/chart-integration/... -run TestLoadAllowlist|TestIsAccepted` all green. - `golangci-lint run ./internal/chartgen/` → 0 issues. ## Followups Pre-existing failures still tracked under SCR-2026-05-14-001 chart-integration recovery: - `argo-cd`: redis-secret-init Job - `opensearch`: JVM gc.log path - `opensearch-dashboards`: crash-class - `mimir-distributed`: crash-class - `airflow`: migration timeout - `crossplane`: settle-window restart / CRD ordering --- ## Summary by cubic Switch Gitea to the `bitnamilegacy` image namespace to match Bitnami’s migration. This fixes ImagePullBackOff errors and unblocks the Gitea install. - **Bug Fixes** - Set `chartValues.gitea.image.repository` to `bitnamilegacy/gitea` and updated `unpatchableImages` in `verity.yaml`. - Updated test allowlist to accept `docker.io/bitnamilegacy/gitea:` and `docker.io/bitnamilegacy/gitea@`. - No changes to subcharts; `postgresql` and `valkey` already use `bitnamilegacy/*`. Written for commit bcf6805a20910ca10ee412aebb5cd1d48de655d1. Summary will update on new commits. Review in cubic

author: netique
body:
## Summary

- **New auth UX**: `node dist/index.js login` opens a dedicated Chrome profile pointed at Overleaf, lets the user authenticate normally (captcha / Google OAuth / ORCID / institutional SSO / 2FA all work because it's a real browser), reads the session cookie via Chrome DevTools Protocol once the dashboard loads, and persists it to `<configDir>/overleaf-mcp/cookie.json` (mode 0600). Re-runs against the same profile are near-silent. Auto-triggers when a tool call finds no cookie or a stale one.
- **Auto-recovery on expiry**: `withAuthRetry` (HTTP) and `withReconnectingSocket` (Socket.IO) evict the stored cookie, relaunch Chrome, and retry the original call exactly once. `applyOtUpdate` re-joins the doc before retrying so mid-edit cookie expiries are transparent.
- **Fix latent GCLB session-affinity bug**: the WS upgrade was sending the original cookie unchanged, but Overleaf's GCP LB sets `Set-Cookie: GCLB=...` on the handshake response for backend pinning. Without echoing that on the upgrade, the upgrade landed on a different backend → intermittent 502s. Was masked when users supplied `OL_COOKIE` env vars copied from long-running Chromes that already had GCLB. Now `mergeSetCookies` appends fresh values from the handshake response to the upgrade's Cookie header.
- **Drop `OL_COOKIE` / `OL_NO_INTERACTIVE` / the stdin paste path entirely.** One auth source per host: the cookie file. Updated `README`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `tests/manual/*.mjs` usage docstrings to match.

New env vars: `OL_BROWSER` (override Chromium binary path), `OL_INSECURE` (`--ignore-certificate-errors` for self-hosted CE with self-signed certs). `OL_CSRF` / `OL_BASE_URL` / `OL_MCP_LOG_LEVEL` unchanged.

No new runtime dependencies — CDP is hand-rolled on the existing `ws@8` client (mirroring how `src/api/socket.ts` hand-rolls Socket.IO 0.9). Chrome / Brave / Edge / Arc / Chromium auto-detected on macOS, Linux, Windows.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [x] `node dist/index.js login` opens Chrome (dedicated profile), captures cookie after manual login, saves to file mode 0600
- [x] `node dist/index.js status` reports file path, host, age, validates by hitting `/project`
- [x] `node dist/index.js logout --confirm` clears the entry
- [x] `tests/manual/smoke.mjs list_projects` works with no `OL_COOKIE` env (uses file)
- [x] `tests/manual/sequence.mjs <project_id>` opens project, joins doc, reads content end-to-end (verifies GCLB merge fix unblocks the WS upgrade)
- [x] Poisoned-cookie test: `withAuthRetry` evicts and re-discovers cleanly on stale cookie
- [ ] Manual: wait for natural 5-day cookie expiry and observe transparent re-auth on next tool call
- [ ] Self-hosted CE smoke (would need test instance)

author: mmkal
body:
## Summary

Adds clickable relation browsing to the studio table grid. Cells backed by a single-column foreign key show relation actions for the referenced parent row, and referenced key cells show reverse actions for every matching child relation.

Relation actions now open as collapsed options first, so a parent key with several inbound relations shows each possible follow-up query before running one. Each option can also navigate into a URL-backed sub view, where the generated SQL is shown above the read-only result table.

The schema endpoint returns relation metadata for both directions:

```ts
relation.foreignKeys // child table -> parent table
relation.referencedBy // parent table -> child tables
```

SQLite and Postgres both implement the dialect hook. The UI intentionally limits this click-through pass to single-column relationships, while the metadata shape can carry composite keys for a later UI pass.

## Media

Forward relation preview from `order_details.product_id` to the referenced `products` row:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2105fef-0ffb-44b8-9132-e267fb2465bd

Reverse relation preview from `products.product_id` to matching `order_details` rows:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/745a4d6e-dd48-441b-a3cd-e8a4ac8d0791

Relation click-through walkthrough video:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c4d7367-d635-440c-9abc-857c8329a2e9

## Before / After

Before, an `order_details.product_id` cell was just a scalar value. The user had to manually know and type the follow-up query.

After, hovering the cell exposes a relation action. Clicking it opens collapsed relation options; expanding one previews the generated filtered query and matching rows:

```sql
select * from "products" where "product_id" = ? limit 100
```

Reverse relations work the same way from the parent row. For example, `employees.employee_id = 1` shows separate options for `employee_territories.employee_id`, `employees.reports_to`, and `orders.employee_id`.

The `Open in sub view` link navigates to a read-only table route with the concrete query shown above the grid, for example:

```sql
select * from "orders" where "employee_id" = 1 limit 100
```

- `pnpm --filter @sqlfu/ui exec playwright test test/demo.spec.ts`

> **Overview**
> Adds **foreign-key–aware navigation** in the sqlfu studio: the dialect layer gains `getRelationForeignKeys` (SQLite via `PRAGMA foreign_key_list` with implicit PK resolution; Postgres via `pg_constraint`), and `schema.get` now returns each relation’s **`foreignKeys`** and **`referencedBy`** edges.

author: mvanhorn
body:
## Summary The eval pipeline uses JSONPath to extract values from traces. When users wrote patterns containing constructs we don't support (filter expressions `[?(...)]`, script expressions, recursive descent inside arrays) the error surfaced as an opaque parser internal exception. Adds a pre-validation pass that names the unsupported construct in the error message and points at the supported subset in the docs. ## Why this matters #13586 reported repeatedly hitting the same "Internal Server Error" while iterating on an eval template; the only path forward was to bisect the pattern by hand. Naming the bad construct turns a 20-minute debug into a 30-second fix. ## Changes - `packages/shared/src/features/evals/utilities.ts` - pre-validate JSONPath patterns and emit a typed `UnsupportedJsonPathError` naming the construct. - `packages/shared/src/features/evals/__tests__/extractValueFromObject.test.ts` - tests covering filter expressions, script expressions, and recursive descent. ## Testing New tests + existing extractor tests pass locally. Fixes #13586

Greptile Summary

 This PR adds a pre-validation pass inside `parseJsonDefault` that catches the most common unsupported JSONPath pattern — negative indexing like `$[-1]` — before the expression reaches the JSONPath engine, replacing an opaque internal exception with a clear, actionable error message. The change is narrow and self-contained. - `packages/shared/src/features/evals/utilities.ts`: introduces `stripJsonPathStringLiterals` (prevents false-positives from object-key string literals) and `validateJsonPath`, which throws a descriptive `Error` when a `[-N]` subscript is detected. Slice forms like `$[-1:]` correctly pass through. - `worker/src/features/evaluation/__tests__/extractValueFromObject.test.ts`: adds positive coverage for `$[-1:]` and negative coverage for `$[-1]` / `$.messages[-1]`, verifying both the error message text and the raw-value fallback.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 Safe to merge — the change is additive, touches only the validation layer before the existing JSONPath call, and all error paths fall back to the pre-existing raw-value behaviour. The regex correctly distinguishes blocked [-N] subscripts from valid slice forms, and the string-literal stripper prevents false positives on keys like $['[-1]']. The only gap is that the implementation throws a plain Error rather than the named UnsupportedJsonPathError class the PR description promises, which means callers cannot programmatically distinguish this validation error from unexpected JSONPath runtime errors. packages/shared/src/features/evals/utilities.ts — the typed error class is missing.

Flowchart

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A["extractValueFromObject(obj, colId, selector)"] --> B{selector present?} B -- No --> Z["return raw column value"] B -- Yes --> C["parseMultiEncodedJson(selectedColumn)"] C --> D["parseJsonDefault(parsed, selector)"] D --> E["validateJsonPath(selector)"] E --> F["stripJsonPathStringLiterals(selector)"] F --> G{"/\[-\\d+\]/ match?"} G -- Yes --> H["throw Error(UNSUPPORTED...)"] H --> I["catch → error returned, fallback to raw value"] G -- No --> J{selectedColumn is primitive?} J -- Yes --> K["return primitive as-is"] J -- No --> L["JSONPath({path, json, eval:false})"] L --> M{result length?} M -- 0 --> N["return undefined → empty string"] M -- 1 --> O["return unwrapped result[0]"] M -- ">1" --> P["return full array"] ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 packages/shared/src/features/evals/utilities.ts:3-4 The PR description says this adds a typed `UnsupportedJsonPathError`, but the implementation throws a plain `Error`. A typed subclass lets callers (e.g. the eval pipeline's error handler) distinguish this user-visible validation failure from unexpected JSONPath runtime errors, so they can format the message differently or re-throw with more context. ```suggestion export class UnsupportedJsonPathError extends Error { constructor(message: string) { super(message); this.name = "UnsupportedJsonPathError"; } } const UNSUPPORTED_JSONPATH_NEGATIVE_INDEX_ERROR_MESSAGE = "JSONPath negative indexing like [-1] is not supported by jsonpath-plus. Use slice syntax instead (e.g. [-1:] for the last element)."; ``` ### Issue 2 of 2 packages/shared/src/features/evals/utilities.ts:99-103 The throw site should use the typed class to match the PR description's intent. If `UnsupportedJsonPathError` is introduced above, this line should reference it. ```suggestion function validateJsonPath(selector: string) { if (/\[\s*-\d+\s*\]/.test(stripJsonPathStringLiterals(selector))) { throw new UnsupportedJsonPathError(UNSUPPORTED_JSONPATH_NEGATIVE_INDEX_ERROR_MESSAGE); } } ``` `````

author: andrew-bierman
body:
## Summary

The MCP server and CLI are now thin Eden Treaty wrappers around the PackRat API — the API stays the source of truth, edge apps stay lean. The branch landed in two phases:

**Phase 1 (commits `bc5baa5` – `2d70fab`)** — migration: built the Treaty clients, ported every existing MCP tool and added 30+ new ones, added the CLI's API command tree, consolidated narrowing helpers in `@packrat/guards` under `to*` naming.

**Phase 2 (commits `1cb8d84` – `31a0a69`)** — API thickening: cleaned up Treaty-hostile schema patterns, added five lean endpoints that collapse multi-step / client-side-compute flows into single Treaty calls, made `id` optional on create endpoints (offline-first preserved), and added a body-credential admin login so MCP/CLI no longer bypass Treaty for admin auth.

## What landed

### Phase 1 — MCP + CLI on Eden Treaty
- **MCP**: two typed clients (`api.user`, `api.admin`). 60+ tools — packs, pack-templates, catalog, trips, weather, trail-conditions, trails, feed, season-suggestions, wildlife, alltrails, upload, guides, ai, plus admin (stats / users / packs / catalog / trails / analytics / ETL). Admin tools hidden until `admin_login` mints a JWT; `registerFlaggedTool(flag, …)` does the same for `MCP_FEATURE_FLAGS` toggles. ACL-aware `call()` maps 401/403/404/409/422/429 to friendly tool errors.
- **CLI**: `auth/admin/packs/trips/catalog/trails/weather/feed/templates/seasons/user/ai` command trees alongside DuckDB analytics. Token store in `~/.packrat/config.json` (0600, atomic write); base URL override via `PACKRAT_API_URL`. 401 → refresh → retry via `createApiClient`'s AuthHooks.
- **`@packrat/guards`**: `toString` / `toNumber` / `toBoolean` / `toDate` (strict narrow) + `toArray` / `toRecord` / `toRecordArray` / `toStringRecord` (coercive). Legacy `as*` kept as `@deprecated` aliases.

### Phase 2 — API thickening (10 proposals, all in)
- **`1cb8d84` Schemas T1+T2+T3** — Dropped redundant `.optional().default(N)` from every query schema where handlers already applied defaults (catalog, guides, ai, admin analytics platform/catalog, admin trails, admin packs/users lists, feed, packs `includePublic`, trail-conditions). Treaty now types these as truly optional. Wire up `includeDeleted` on admin packs-list (was schema-declared but unread), drop dead `includeDeleted` from admin users-list (Better Auth doesn't support user soft-delete), switch remaining `includeDeleted` to `z.coerce.boolean()`, coerce `duration` in gap-analysis to number.
- **`5d8ab30` Edge cleanup T4** — CLI/MCP drop the workarounds the schema changes obsoleted.
- **`ffc929e` T5 `GET /weather/by-name?q=…`** — Combined search + forecast in one call.
- **`4e79c18` T6 `GET /packs/:packId/weight-breakdown`** — Server-computed total/base/worn/consumable grams + per-category aggregation.
- **`2fcc4c4` T7 `POST /catalog/compare`** — `{ ids: number[] }` → comparison rows + lightestId/cheapestId/highestRatedId leaders, single SQL query.
- **`089af14` T8 `POST /packs/:packId/items/from-catalog`** — Server hydrates name/weight/category/image/embedding from the catalog row; caller supplies catalogItemId + per-pack metadata.
- **`df0cfac` T9 Server-side ID minting** — Every create endpoint accepts an optional `id`; server mints with `mintId(prefix)` when absent. Offline-first stores (mobile, Legend State) keep supplying client-side IDs for sync. (Tradeoff noted below.)
- **`31a0a69` T10 `POST /admin/login`** — Body-credential variant of `/admin/token`. MCP/CLI no longer bypass Treaty for admin auth; both go through the typed Treaty client.

## On T9 (offline-first + ID ownership)
T9 ships the pragmatic interim: one `id` field, client- or server-supplied. Mobile/Legend State stores keep working unchanged. The cleaner long-term design splits ownership — server-owned `id` (real PK, auto-generated) + client-owned `clientUuid` (idempotency + sync key). That's a bigger lift (schema migration, sync-plugin rewiring across mobile/web) and deserves its own brainstorm + plan. Tracked as a follow-up.

## Bugs caught while migrating
- MCP `update_trip` was PATCHing but the API expects PUT (silent 404).
- MCP `get_weather` indexed `searchResults.id`/`.results[0].id`; the API returns a flat array → should be `[0].id`. (Now obsolete — `get_weather` calls the new combined endpoint.)
- MCP `get_season_suggestions` posted `{ destination }`; API requires `{ location, date }`.
- MCP feed-comment had `parent_comment_id: string`; API body is `z.number().int()`.
- MCP catalog search used `'sort[field]'`/`'sort[order]'` bracket notation; the catalog schema preprocesses `sort` from a JSON object. The bracket form was silently ignored.
- Admin packs-list/users-list declared `includeDeleted` in the schema but the handler never read it. Now wired up correctly on packs-list (admins can see soft-deleted packs); dropped from users-list where Better Auth doesn't support user soft-delete.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun check:casts:strict` — no unsafe casts
- [x] biome clean on all touched files in packages/api, packages/mcp, packages/cli, packages/guards
- [x] All pre-push lints green (typeof, regex, env, circular, dup-deps, dup-guards, unauth-routes, sorted package.json, casts:strict)
- [x] `packages/cli` typechecks
- [x] CLI smoke: `packrat --help`, `packrat <group> --help`, unauthed `packrat packs list` → friendly auth hint, unauthed `packrat admin stats` → admin hint
- [ ] `packages/api` typecheck — running locally hung; needs CI
- [ ] End-to-end against staging API: login, weather/by-name, weight-breakdown, catalog/compare, items/from-catalog, admin/login, create-without-id
- [ ] Admin login → admin tools become visible in MCP `tools/list`

## Follow-ups (out of scope for this PR)
- **`clientUuid` split** — proper server-owned `id` + client-owned `clientUuid` (the cleaner T9). Schema migration + Legend State plugin rewire.
- **Body-schema defaults** — same `.optional().default(N)` cleanup for POST bodies (packs.consumable/worn, packTemplates.quantity, etc.). T1 handled query schemas; bodies have a slightly different cost/benefit and deserve their own pass.
- **`shortId` helpers in CLI/MCP** — exported but no internal callers now. Safe to remove if nothing external uses them.

author: jamestexas
body:
## Summary

During post-OSS-launch dogfood on macOS, `task serve:local`'s `sudo mkdir -p /data/do` fails with `mkdir: /data: Read-only file system` — Apple's signed system volume (SIP, macOS 10.15+) disallows writes outside specific firmlinks. The repo's docs assumed Linux-style filesystem semantics and gave no guidance to macOS readers, who hit this on first try.

Two doc updates, no code changes.

### What changed

1. **`README.md`** + **`GETTING-STARTED.md`** — explicit macOS callout with three escalating workarounds for Path B (`task serve:local`):
   - **(a)** use Path A (`task dev`) — same substrate, no `/data` involvement.
   - **(b)** `task image && docker run cloister:0.1.0` — `/data/do` is writable inside the container's own filesystem.
   - **(c)** synthetic firmlink via `/etc/synthetic.conf` + reboot — last resort, called out as such.

2. **Encryption-at-rest disclaimer.** Both docs now note that DO SQLite databases are unencrypted on disk in every path (Path A, B, C). The vault ciphertexts *inside* those SQLite files ARE AES-GCM-encrypted per ADR-0013/0014; the bead/trust/blob tables are plaintext. Operators shouldn't drop production-sensitive data into a dev install.

3. **`.wrangler/state/` gitignore note.** README explicitly mentions that Path A's local DO state is already covered by `.gitignore` so it can't accidentally be committed.

### Deferred (separate ADR thread)

Making `/data/do` configurable on the host. The path is hardcoded in `apko.yaml:50` and `config.capnp:71`; a future path-resolution module + env-var contract (or full XDG migration) would let macOS hosts run Path B directly without firmlinks. That's tracked separately behind the network-identity / capnp-substrate ADR conversation; out of scope for this doc patch.

### Test plan

- [x] No code changes; `task lint` not affected.
- [x] Path A (`task dev`) validated locally: `/health` ok, 14 tools, 3 registry servers.
- [x] Path B validated on Linux conceptually (the docs describe the existing pre-PR behavior).
- [ ] macOS reviewer can verify the new doc warnings render correctly + workaround (a) actually works for them.

body:
Se necesitaba habilitar GitHub Pages para servir la documentación ya generada por Doxygen (`documentation/html`) sin depender de una rama estática. Esta propuesta automatiza la generación y despliegue desde Actions en cada cambio a `main` y por ejecución manual.

- **Alcance del problema**
  - Se incorpora un flujo de publicación continua para la documentación técnica del repositorio.
  - Se expone un enlace único en el README para consumo directo de la documentación publicada.

- **Workflow de despliegue de documentación**
  - Nuevo archivo: `.github/workflows/github-pages-docs.yml`.

body:
### Motivation
- Reduce false-positive alias/duplicate suggestions by requiring only strong, verifiable signals before surfacing alias/merge guards. 
- Prevent DefiLlama resolver from promoting unrelated protocols as high-confidence matches, preferring “no reliable match” over misleading recommendations. 
- Keep the source engine conservative and admin-only for uncertain matches while preserving Managed Vault, provider discovery and public runtime safety.

### Description
- Tightened duplicate detection in `lib/admin/logoDb.ts` to only surface candidates with strong signals such as exact CoinGecko ID, exact CoinMarketCap numeric ID, exact approved_logo_url, exact source/image URL, explicit alias/name/slug matches, and normalized-name equality. 
- Hardened provider scoring in `lib/admin/providerScoring.ts` to penalize derivative/bridged/wrapped/LP/IOU/stable candidates unless the target itself contains those terms, and to require a strong exact/alias reason for `high` confidence. 
- Reworked DefiLlama resolver in `lib/admin/defillamaResolver.ts` to require strict matches (exact normalized name/slug/known alias + category compatibility), filter derivative mismatches, verify an actual icon exists, and only mark a candidate `recommended` when it meets a minimum high-confidence threshold; otherwise return a compact "No reliable DefiLlama source found." message. 
- UI and action changes: the admin detail page (`app/admin/logos/[slug]/page.tsx`) now only renders the Alias / merge guard when high-confidence duplicates exist and shows explicit match reason + confidence, and the DefiLlama helper shows only a recommended high-confidence result (with `Use + Fetch`) while other low/medium matches are collapsed under "Other possible matches"; server-side `addDefiLlamaAction` was restricted to accept only the recommended high-confidence candidate. 
- No DB/schema changes were introduced and Admin DB Setup is not required for this PR.

### Testing
- Ran type-check: `npx tsc --noEmit` and it completed successfully. 
- Built the app: `npm run build` and the production build completed successfully.

author: williamthorsen
body:
## What

Sharpens `respond-to-review` so the agent no longer accepts reviewer recommendations that move, promote, or restructure code or guidance without verifying that the destination's stated doctrine actually accommodates it. For such recommendations, pushback is the default posture; acceptance requires affirmative evidence: The destination's doctrine must clearly accommodate the change, and the move must resolve a real duplication or location problem.

Hedging language in a recommendation is now treated as a signal that the premise needs independent verification rather than as license to accept on the reviewer's word.

## Why

The previous anti-sycophancy guidance verified reviewer claims at the syntactic level (does the proposed change make the code correct?) but did not address doctrinal compatibility, recommendation type (move/promote/restructure), or hedging language as a premise-verification trigger. In the #555 review response, the agent accepted a recommendation that promoted a commit-specific rule into a destination whose stated voice was incompatible — purely on a "plausibly generalizes" framing. The user had to surface the doctrinal conflict and reject the change manually after seeing the result. This change closes that failure class.

## Details

### 🎉 Features

- A doctrinal-compatibility check applies to recommendations that move, promote, or restructure code or guidance. The destination's stated scope, conventions, and invariants must be read in full; syntactic fit is not sufficient.
- Hedging language is named explicitly as a verification trigger: the recommendation's premise is treated as unverified until independently checked.
- A doctrine-warranted ACCEPT path is available for structural recommendations: when the destination's stated doctrine clearly accommodates the change and the move resolves a duplication or location problem, the rule supports acceptance rather than reflexive rejection.

Closes #572

author: pdlug
body:
Comprehensive code-quality pass over the surface that churned across the three stacked transaction PRs (#136 TableContribution, #138 durable fulltext, #139 cross-store transactions).


## What changed

**Structural**
- **Cut the speculative `source` abstraction.** `TableContributionSource`, `source`, `isDrizzleContribution`, `StrategyDrizzleModel`/`drizzleModel`, and `resolveStrategyContribution` had zero production consumers (only re-exports + tests). `StrategyTableContribution` is now a `TableContribution` alias. Removed both `eslint-disable no-explicit-any` escapes; `isPgTable`/`isSqliteTable` now use Drizzle's real `is()` brand check instead of "any non-string object".
- **Deleted the fully-dead `ensureContribution` API** across all four layers (materializer, `GraphBackend`, both backends) + `findStrategyContribution` that only served it. Never called anywhere.
- **Collapsed the 3-way-duplicated fulltext gate** (`gateFulltext` + both backends' hand-coded non-tx wrappers) into one shared `gateFulltextMethods` — the gating contract now lives once.
- **Removed the tx-adoption type-safety escapes.** New `InternalOperationBackend` intersection lets the factories return their true shape — all three `as unknown as CommonOperationBackend` double-casts gone. Shared `assertAdoptedDialect` guard fails a wrong-dialect handle loudly at the boundary and eliminated the last `as Any*Database` casts (zero adoption casts remain).
- **Shared `coerceNumericScore`** so SQLite enforces the same `FulltextSearchResult.score: number` contract as Postgres.

**Readability**
- `withTransaction` `@throws {StoreNotInitializedError}` documented; `manager.ts` ensure-path; `materializeOne` shares the one state classifier with `assertInitialized`; `StoreNotInitializedError` constructor-shape rationale; comment-bloat trim.

**Docs/changesets**
- The pending (unreleased) changesets for #136/#138 and the fulltext-search doc updated to describe the final trimmed API. No new changeset — every changed API was added by those three unreleased PRs, so editing their changesets is correct (a new one would double-count).

## Deliberately *not* done (flagged, not forced)

- **Marker-store plumbing extraction:** the sibling subsystems (`index-materializations.ts`, `kind-removals.ts`) deliberately share only value-builders/adapters and keep thin per-backend Drizzle plumbing. Extracting only contribution markers would make them *inconsistent* with three siblings.
- **sqlite "sql"-branch / `bindTransactionBackend` unification:** the divergence is legitimate (manual BEGIN/COMMIT on the outer connection vs a distinct `tx` handle). Documented the deliberate divergence rather than risk an unverifiable transaction regression.

author: razinkele
body:
## Summary

User-reported: the workflow stepper at the top of the dashboard displayed raw i18n keys (e.g., \`modules.workflow_stepper.step_get_started\`) instead of translated labels.

Verified visually via Playwright:

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| \`modules.workflow_stepper.step_get_started\` | **Get Started** |
| \`modules.workflow_stepper.step_create_ses\` | **Create SES** |
| \`modules.workflow_stepper.step_visualize\` | **Visualize** |
| \`modules.workflow_stepper.step_analyze\` | **Analyze** |
| \`modules.workflow_stepper.step_report\` | **Report** |

## Root cause

\`modules/workflow_stepper_module.R:279\` constructs the lookup key dynamically:

\`\`\`r
label <- i18n\$t(paste0("modules.workflow_stepper.", step\$key))
\`\`\`

The 5 step keys (defined inline in the module at lines 22-27) were never added to \`translations/modules/workflow_stepper.json\`. shiny.i18n's missing-key fallback returns the key string verbatim, which is what the user saw on screen.

## Changes (4 files, +62/-2)

- \`translations/modules/workflow_stepper.json\` — added 5 keys × 9 languages = 45 entries.
- \`VERSION\` + \`DESCRIPTION\` bumped 1.13.0 → 1.13.1 (patch — strings only).
- \`CHANGELOG.md\` — 1.13.1 entry.

## Test plan

- [x] JSON parses
- [x] \`test-i18n-enforcement.R\` → 37/37
- [x] Playwright visual check — screenshot confirms all 5 stepper labels translated

author: bageus
body:
### Motivation
- Players must be able to voluntarily abort a mission attempt and return to the Box to change modules before retrying, which is required for the flow prior to Mission 4. 
- This action must be distinct from `Restart Mission` and `Mission Complete` and must preserve progression and installed/digital module state.

### Description
- Added a new `returned_to_box` signal and `return_to_box()` in `BipobController` which sets `mission_finished = true`, clears `last_diagnostic_result`, transfers any carried physical modules (`held_module`, `stored_physical_module`) into `box_storage`, emits the hint "Returned to box. Mission attempt aborted.", emits `status_changed` and `returned_to_box`, and intentionally avoids calling `complete_mission()` or advancing mission state. 
- Added a programmatically-created `Return to Box` button to the in-field `CommandPanel` in `GameUI`, wired `_on_return_to_box_button_pressed()` to call `bipob.return_to_box()`, show the `BoxScreen` if it is not already visible, and update status/box/diagnostic UI; also connected `bipob.returned_to_box` to `show_box_screen()` and guarded against double-showing. 
- Files modified: `scripts/bipob/bipob_controller.gd`, `scripts/ui/game_ui.gd` (no `.tscn` changes). 
- Short Godot test checklist: Start a mission and pick up/store physical module(s) then press `Return to Box` to confirm BoxScreen opens, hand/storage become empty and box storage lists returned items; confirm the hint appears, `current_mission_index` is unchanged, installed modules/digital storage remain intact, and `Restart Mission` / `Mission Complete` behaviors remain unaffected.

### Testing
- Ran `git status --short && git diff -- scripts/bipob/bipob_controller.gd scripts/ui/game_ui.gd` to inspect the diff and it completed successfully. 
- Inspected file contents with `nl -ba scripts/bipob/bipob_controller.gd | sed -n '1,40p'` and `nl -ba scripts/ui/game_ui.gd | sed -n '20,210p'` to verify new symbols and handlers were inserted, and those inspections completed successfully.

body:
## Summary

Ships the foundation for fleet integration: Zitadel PKCE sign-in, env-profile selector, capability surface, and the OSS-first design contract.

- **fleet-auth-foundation** (WP01–WP07): `core/fleet/` package skeleton, `KENAZ_HARNESS_ENV={dev,stage,prod,local}` profile selector (defaults to prod), PKCE + loopback OAuth against Zitadel `kameas-native` app (RFC 8252, no client secret), `Identity` populated from `POST /api/v1/enroll`, OS-keychain token persistence, refresh-on-401 retry, `Settings → Account` panel (signed-out / signed-in / kill-switched states with env badge), fork-recipe docs.
- **fleet-capability-surface** (WP08–WP14): 25-key capability enum + `Has`/`Require` accessors, 5min polling goroutine with single-flight refresh and backoff (5/15/60min), disk cache at `<DataDir>/fleet/capabilities.json`, frontend `capability(key)` composable, `core/llm/fleet_hosted/` LLM adapter registered only when `hosted_inference` capability is on, codegen parity check (Go enum ↔ `frontend/src/lib/capability-keys.ts`).
- **OSS-first contract** (binding for all future fleet missions): `HARNESS_FLEET_DISABLED=1` kill switch; non-fleet packages cannot import `core/fleet/` (enforced by `scripts/ci/check-no-fleet-imports.sh`); fleet UI surfaces use `v-if="signedIn && capability('<key>')"` — never disabled buttons; fork recipe verified.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./core/... -race -count=1 -short` green (4674 tests)
- [x] `vitest run` green (1532 tests + 6 skipped)
- [x] `bash scripts/ci/check-codegen.sh` — capability-keys.ts parity intact

author: isjunrod
body:
## Resumen

Iteración UX sobre el mapa tras los PRs #1 y #2. 3 commits semánticos:

### 1. \`checkpoint: cinematic flyTo working\`
Backup del estado pre-orbital antes de los cambios mayores.

### 2. \`fix(map): killer flyTo, multi-layer highlight, scroll-spy by zoom\`
Fixes acumulados que arreglaron el bug "el flyTo no movía el mapa":
- \`setPadding\` global removido (interfería con \`flyTo\` zoom alcanzable).
- flyTo: \`map.stop()\` + \`duration:2000\` explícito + fallback \`setCenter/setZoom\` a +2.4s para garantizar aterrizaje.
- \`detectLocation\` usa \`map.getZoom()\` directo en vez de \`bounds.width\` (el pitch inflaba bounds y devolvía dept/región equivocada).
- \`mapReadyRef\` reemplaza \`map.isStyleLoaded()\` (este último retorna falso transitoriamente post-\`setProjection\` y dejaba effects pegados en \`once load\`).
- Highlight 4 layers: outer pulse (3s) + inner pulse (1.5s) + glow blur + núcleo blanco r=12. Filter syncado en las 4.
- AuthorityHud: removido \`motion.span absolute inset-0\` que capturaba pointer events y bloqueaba interacción del map.

### 3. \`feat(map): scroll-spy bidireccional + marker padding + null-geom guard\`
- ObrasListPanel auto-scrollea al item seleccionado cuando el origen es el click en marker (scroll-spy bidireccional).
- flyTo del marker usa \`padding\` inline (no \`offset\` — más predecible con pitch 55°) → halo aterriza en franja libre entre panel detalle y sidebar.
- Guard \`if (!geometry) return false;\` en \`featureContains\` y \`computeBbox\` — el GeoJSON del INEI tiene features con geometry null que tiraban \`TypeError\` y hacían que el label cayera al fallback "Perú".
- Force emit del label post-flyTo (\`setTimeout 2400ms\`) con los valores TARGET conocidos — no depende del \`idle\` event ni de \`getZoom()\` actual.

## Test plan

- [ ] Click obra del sidebar → flyTo cinematográfico arranca de inmediato (sin esperar 2do click)
- [ ] El halo verde aterriza centrado entre el panel detalle y el sidebar
- [ ] Sidebar auto-scrollea para poner la obra seleccionada en el top
- [ ] Label junto al wordmark cambia a \`Perú · Lima · Miraflores\` (o lo que toque)
- [ ] Click distintas ciudades (Pucallpa, Cusco, Iquitos) → label correcto en cada una
- [ ] Zoom out al máximo → \`Vista global\`
- [ ] Pan a Chile/Bolivia → label cambia al país (sin polígonos finos, fallback bbox)

## Riesgos

- Performance del 4-layer highlight: RAF a 60fps, \`setPaintProperty\` × 5 por frame. Validado en pantalla 13" sin lag.
- El padding del flyTo puede limitar el zoom alcanzable en viewports <1024px; el fallback \`setCenter+setZoom\` a +2.4s lo cubre.

body:
Append the three drift findings surfaced during the INV-07 / INV-09 / INV-15 audit loops in cluster #2 (commit aad0c464 on test/lifecycle-invariants-cluster-2). The findings were captured in the test file's class docstrings and the cluster-2 commit message; promoting them to §1.3.1 makes them visible at the matrix's top-level audit point. Findings added: - INV-07 schema permissiveness — InquiryStateUpdate uses Pydantic's default extra='ignore'. LLM emissions of evidence_to_add on INQUIRY responses are silently dropped, not rejected. Invariant still holds (no Evidence row created — engine has no creation branch either), but LLM training drift is invisible. Hardening to extra='forbid' is an open design question. - INV-09 terminology drift — matrix calls require_case_not_terminal() "middleware" but it's a plain helper used at one site; other write endpoints inline the case.is_terminal check. Matrix wording should be updated; consolidation via FastAPI dependency injection is a future possibility. - INV-15 scan scope — the matrix's "light vocabulary check" refers to _completion_phrases at milestone_engine.py:2602, which only catches transition-completion claims. The prompt's _ADVISOR_ROLE_CONSTRAINT bans a broader set ("Let me check", "I will run", etc.) that the runtime scan doesn't cover. Broadening the scan is an open design question. None of these are invariant violations — every invariant holds. The drifts are between matrix descriptions and code surfaces. Implementation actions (cleanup PRs, design decisions) are tracked separately, not here. Note: the INV-06 entry above ("design-text overstatement") is expected to be revised when the same-turn KB-resolution collapse code change lands (per the Option B decision in the cluster-2 audit follow-up discussion). The obu order rule for the non-vcl obus is checked at the end of aom_decode_frame_from_obus() 
1. configuration record obus, (qm and fgm obus) order
2. frame unit rule : no obus are allowed in between two tile groups that have the same order hint and the same mlayer_id
3. multi layer rule : unique order hint in each mlayer_id and increasing order or mlayer_id for each order hint.

This MR contains an encoder change to comply the obu rules, consecutive CLKs need to have different order hint, to differentiate temporal units. 

This MR contains the later half of 1.3 related to picture units in CWG-F436.
In this MR `check_obu_order` is temporarily disabled and it will be re-enabled when rest of F436 is integrated in separate MR.

author: aaronpeterson-franconnect
body:
## Summary

Closes the last gap in the eval/smoke gating story: the existing `Live Smoke` workflow asserts `/api/search/hybrid` returns **503** with the documented detail when no LLM is configured (catches silent-degradation regressions). This PR adds the opposite assertion — `/api/search/hybrid` returns **200** with a `hits[]` envelope when a working LLM provider IS configured.

To get a working LLM without Azure OpenAI keys or LLM cost on every PR, ships a deterministic in-network mock that responds to `POST /openai/deployments/{deployment}/embeddings` with a hash-seeded 1536-dim vector. Same input → same vector, which is what makes the gate reproducible.

## What's in the PR

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/AiLibrarian.LlmMock/` | ASP.NET Core minimal API. ~150 lines. SHA256-seeded RNG walks a 1536-dim float vector. Azure OpenAI v1 response shape (object/list/data/usage). |
| `src/AiLibrarian.LlmMock/Dockerfile` | Same multi-stage shape as the three workload Dockerfiles. |
| `docker-compose.llm-mock.yml` | Compose override that adds `llm-mock` to the network + injects 6 `LlmGateway` env vars onto the api service. Activate with `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.llm-mock.yml up`. |
| `scripts/live-smoke-llm.sh` | Same shape as `scripts/live-smoke.sh`. Seeds a department + user + source + 1536-dim chunk, then asserts `/api/search/hybrid` returns 200 with the expected envelope. |
| `.github/workflows/live-smoke-llm.yml` | New CI workflow. Runs in parallel with the existing 4. |
| `AiLibrarian.sln` | New project added to the solution. |
| `docs/dev/local.md` | Phase 2B section rewritten as usage docs for the shipped thing. |

## What this is NOT

Documented in `src/AiLibrarian.LlmMock/Program.cs` at length:

- **Vectors are random.** Two unrelated strings produce uncorrelated vectors; two *related* strings ALSO produce uncorrelated vectors. Random hashes don't preserve meaning. The mock is for "plumbing works" gating, NOT for "retrieval finds the right chunks" quality evaluation.
- **Only embeddings.** No chat completions endpoint, so `/api/ask` still 503s. Extending to chat is a follow-up.
- **Real retrieval quality testing** still needs Azure OpenAI keys + `HttpEvalBackend` against a deployed API. The mock and the real-Azure path are complementary, not substitutes.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build AiLibrarian.sln -c Release` — 0 warnings 0 errors
- [x] `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.llm-mock.yml config` — merges cleanly; env-vars on api, `llm-mock` joined to network, `depends_on` union'd
- [x] Standalone LlmMock returns expected JSON shape + determinism verified (three calls with same input → identical first 6 floats)
- [ ] **CI: 5 workflows green** (CI, Quality Gate, Release Images, Live Smoke, Live Smoke (LLM mock))

The new `live-smoke-llm` job is the canonical proof — it boots the merged compose, exercises the path end-to-end, and dumps llm-mock logs on failure.

## Summary

Rebuilds `<Aside>` chrome per [visual-polish-target.md §"Aside dissolution"](docs/website/vision/design/visual-polish-target.md): drops card chrome (border, shadow, radius, background), renders a 3px gray left rule + 18px indent + italic body in Plex Sans at `--sophie-text-body` (17px) / `--sophie-leading-prose` (1.65). Variant signal lives in the small-caps kind label (or bolded definition term) — never in accent color.

Aside is the only Tier-3 component in the three-tier visual model; this is the *only* dissolution-tier sweep in step-G.

## Visual contract

- **Uniform muted left rule** across all 5 variants (was: per-kind accent `border-left-color`). Variant differentiation moves to the marker text alone.
- **Small-caps kind label** via `font-variant: all-small-caps` — typographically correct over `text-transform: uppercase`, matches visual-polish-target's "designed-label not banner-shouting" directive.
- **Em-dash separator** after marker via CSS `::after` (presentation-only, kept out of the accessibility tree).
- **`definition` variant drops the marker entirely** — the bolded defined term IS the variant label (Wikipedia / academic-textbook convention). Schema's `title`-required refinement is unchanged.
- **Body italic** with `--sophie-text-body` (17px) + `--sophie-leading-prose` (1.65) — matches surrounding prose rhythm.

## Structural shape — Path A

Preserves `<details>` / `<summary>` semantics so `@sophie/astro`'s `[data-sophie-aside]` margin-docking chrome continues to work unmodified. Dissolved chrome shows in inline-fallback mode; docked-mode body renders in the right margin column. Path B (drop `<details>`) was considered and deferred — would have killed margin-docking mid-stream, no ADR authorizes that.

Also serves as a controlled experiment for the known Callout VR bug (memory `project_ws3_pr5_callout_vr_bug.md`): if PR-6's CI baselines render correctly, the prior bug is Callout-specific (title-bar/icon machinery). author: timothyfroehlich
body:
## Summary

Long feature branch names produced project_ids that, combined with Supabase's `supabase_<service>_<project_id>` container naming, exceeded Docker's 63-char container name limit and got truncated mid-token (often leaving a trailing hyphen). Result: hostname resolution failed in those worktrees and Supabase wouldn't start. Bit a Wave 0b teammate on 2026-05-15 with branch `feat/e2e-cleanup-admin-discord-downgrade-PP-t8o`.

## Fix

- Cap sanitized project_id at **40 chars** (was 50). Longest active Supabase prefix is `supabase_inbucket_` (18); `supabase_edge_runtime_` (22) is a future risk — 40 keeps us safe against either against Docker's 63-char limit.
- For branches whose sanitized form would exceed 40 chars: append an 8-char sha256 hash of the original branch name to keep the readable prefix while guaranteeing uniqueness across worktrees on different long branches that share a common prefix.
- `rstrip("-")` at the truncation boundary prevents trailing-hyphen container names even when the cut lands on a token boundary.

## Migration

- Short branches (≤31 readable chars): unchanged behavior, no migration.
- Long branches: project_id changes from a possibly-broken truncated form to a deterministic readable+hash form. These worktrees were already broken (Supabase wouldn't start), so there's nothing to lose; the next config regeneration produces a working container name.

## Test plan

- [x] 6 new pytest cases: hash-suffix for long branches, deterministic hashing, distinct IDs for common-prefix long branches, no trailing hyphens after truncation, exact 40/41-char boundary
- [x] Existing `<= 50` assertion tightened to `<= 40`
- [x] All 47 `test_worktree_setup.py` tests pass
- [x] `pnpm run check` clean (ruff included)

body:
### Motivation
- Make seller offers inside the buyer request view clear and buyer-friendly so buyers can instantly see who responded, what is offered, price, availability, and how to contact the seller. 
- Provide a safe, minimal buyer-side selection flow that marks a chosen seller and exposes contact info without adding payments, orders, websockets, or CRM changes. 
- Keep compatibility with existing flows and avoid DB migrations or wide-scope rewrites. 

### Description
- Updated buyer request display and offer card formatting in `bot/handlers/buyer/start.py` to prioritize seller name, price, city, availability (friendly labels), short comment, and a visible selected marker (`⭐ Обрано`).
- Added small helpers: `_format_availability`, `_format_seller_contacts`, and `_get_own_offer` to present compact availability and seller contact blocks and to ensure offers belong to the requesting buyer before showing contacts.
- Implemented offer action handlers that reuse existing accept logic: `_send_offer_contacts`, `_select_offer`, and new callback handlers under the safe `buyer_offer` namespace (`buyer_offer:contact:{id}`, `buyer_offer:select:{id}`, `buyer_offer:back`). These handlers call `accept_buyer_offer(...)` and refresh request details without adding order/payment logic.
- Modified inline keyboard `bot/keyboards/buyer_requests_inline.py` to use `buyer_offer` namespace for offer actions and present buttons as `[Написати] [Обрати]` or `[Написати] [✅ Обрано]` for already-selected offers; added legacy wrappers so existing `buyer_requests:contact:*` and `buyer_requests:select:*` callbacks remain supported.
- Kept all database interactions unchanged and reused existing `accept_buyer_offer`/`list_buyer_offer_cards` logic; no migrations or CRM changes were introduced.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall bot` with no syntax errors reported. 
- Ran `git diff --check` and no whitespace or diff issues were found. 
- Note: full manual Telegram button/polling checks require a running bot session and were not executed in this automated run.

author: drewjocham
body:
## Summary
PR-3 of the [lufis audit plan](../blob/main/docs/lufis-terminal-audit-plan.md). \`kube/backend/internal/terminal/terminal.go\` and \`lufis-terminal/internal/pty/pty.go\` used to maintain near-identical PTY lifecycles — ~340 lines of production code in two copies, slowly drifting (different error wrapping, restart semantics, read-buffer sizes). **The duplication is gone.**

## Layout
\`\`\`
pkg/pty/                       — new shared module
  go.mod                       — module github.com/argues/argus-pty
  pty.go                       — PTY type + Options config + lifecycle
  pty_test.go                  — black-box coverage
go.work                        — workspace listing all 7 in-repo modules
.gitignore                     — un-ignore go.work / go.work.sum

kube/backend/internal/terminal/terminal.go     — now 85-line adapter
lufis-terminal/internal/pty/pty.go             — now 60-line adapter
lufis-terminal/internal/pty/pty_test.go        — slimmed to adapter contract;
                                                 deep coverage moved up
\`\`\`

## Design decisions where the two old copies disagreed
| Concern | argus had | lufis had | merged shared core |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Restart semantics | Start re-enters | Close blocks subsequent Start | argus flavor |
| Error wrapping | bare | \"pty start:\" prefixes | lufis flavor |
| Read-buffer size | 64KiB | 8KiB | 64KiB |
| Close error aggregation | drop | errors.Join | lufis flavor |

## API preserved
Existing callers (\`terminal_handler.go\`, lufis render loop, all the tests) compile **without source changes**. \`kube/backend\`'s \`StartWithEnv\` works via the new \`Options.ExtraEnv\`.

## Cross-module wiring
\`go.work\` makes \`argus-pty\` resolvable without publishing. Both consumers also carry a \`replace …/argus-pty => ../path/to/pkg/pty\` so non-workspace tooling (CI without GOWORK, sub-module \`go test\`) still works.

## Test coverage
- \`pkg/pty/pty_test.go\` — 10 top-level: constructor, pre-start safety (5 rows), started lifecycle (7 rows), \$SHELL fallback chain, ExtraEnv end-to-end via printf round-trip, OnOutput, concurrency
- \`lufis-terminal/internal/pty/pty_test.go\` — adapter-only (4 top-level, 13 subtests): forwarding, OnOutput field wiring, nil-callback safety, concurrent public calls
- \`kube/backend/internal/terminal/terminal_test.go\` — **unchanged from PR-2**; still green (Terminal API preserved)

## Test plan
- [x] \`go build ./...\` in all three modules
- [x] \`go test -race -short\` in \`pkg/pty/\`, \`kube/backend/internal/terminal/\`, \`lufis-terminal/internal/pty/\`
- [ ] Stack atop PR #91, PR #93, PR #94 in CI order (each independently mergeable)

## Refs
- \`docs/lufis-terminal-audit-plan.md\` PR-3
- \`AGENTS.md\` (handler pattern)

author: micherra
body:
## Summary

`generateSlug` had no length cap. Verbose task descriptions produced slugs that pushed the resulting directory path past macOS's 255-byte `NAME_MAX` limit, causing `ENAMETOOLONG` failures at workspace creation. The companion function `sanitizeBranch` already truncated to 80 chars — `generateSlug` was the gap. This fix adds word-boundary-aware truncation at 72 characters to close it.

## Changes

- **`workspace.ts`**: Added `MAX_LENGTH = 72` constant and word-boundary truncation to `generateSlug`. Backs up to the last hyphen within the limit; falls back to hard truncation when no hyphen exists. Strips any trailing hyphen after truncation. JSDoc updated to document the 72-char cap and word-boundary behavior.
- **`workspace.test.ts`**: Replaced the "preserves long names" assertion (which encoded the pre-fix behavior) with 4 targeted tests covering: length cap, word-boundary cut, trailing-hyphen removal, and hard-truncation fallback.

## Testing

- Tests written: 4 (net new; 1 prior assertion replaced)
- Integration tests: N/A
- Coverage gaps filled: 4 truncation cases previously untested
- Review verdict: **CLEAN**

All gates passed: `npm run build` (tsc clean), `npm run lint` (biome, 403 files, no issues), `npm test` (3437 tests, 19/19 workspace tests pass).

🎯 **What:** Replaced the bloated `__init__` inside the `Achievement` class by converting it into a `@dataclass`. Converted `SteamManager.sync_all` caching fallback instantiation to use keyword arguments.

💡 **Why:** Using `@dataclass` greatly improves code readability, enforces type hints natively onto class attributes, and resolves the issue "Too Many Parameters in Achievement.__init__". Refactoring to use keywords during cached object instantiation prevents accidental bugs with positional arguments during object rebuild.

author: nocktoshi
body:
# Adapt to nockvm `NounSpace` API (nockchain master)

## Summary

Updates vesl-core for nockchain master’s **NounSpace** refactor: noun accessors are now space-aware. Without this, the tree fails to compile and slab-allocated nouns panic at runtime when jammed or inspected with the wrong arena.

## Motivation

Recent nockvm changes:

| Before | After |
|--------|--------|
| `indirect.normalize_as_atom()` | `normalize_as_atom(&NounSpace)` or `normalize_as_atom_stack()` for stack-pointer atoms |
| `atom.as_ne_bytes()` / `as_u64()` | `atom.in_space(&space)` → `AtomHandle` |
| `cell.head()` / `tail()` | `NounHandle` / `CellHandle` with `&NounSpace` |
| `T::from_noun(noun)` | `T::from_noun(noun, &space)` |
| `slab.copy_into(noun)` | `slab.copy_into(noun, &space)` |

`new_raw_bytes_ref` produces **stack-pointer** atoms → use `normalize_as_atom_stack()`, not `normalize_as_atom(&slab.noun_space())` (panics on slab).

Jamming must use the noun’s **own** arena: `jam_to_bytes(noun, &slab.noun_space())`, not a throwaway `NockStack`.

## Breaking change

```rust
// Before
jam_to_bytes(&mut stack, noun)

// After
jam_to_bytes(noun, &stack.noun_space())   // stack nouns
jam_to_bytes(noun, &slab.noun_space())    // slab nouns
```

Implementation uses `NockJammer::jam` (same encoding as `NounSlab::jam()`).

## Summary

body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD041 -->
## Summary

Closes #3630. The `[1/8] Preflight checks` step ran `docker run --rm --pull=missing busybox:latest nslookup registry.npmjs.org` and treated `Name: registry.npmjs.org` + `Address: <ip>` as proof that container DNS works. On a host where outbound UDP/TCP port 53 was blocked at the iptables `OUTPUT` chain, that probe still passed because Docker's embedded DNS resolver (and the upstream resolver before it) had cached the `registry.npmjs.org` answer from earlier successful lookups. Onboarding then continued past preflight and only hit the real DNS failure deeper in the sandbox build, where the error is much less actionable.

Replace the probe target with a random subdomain of the RFC 6761 reserved `.invalid` TLD, e.g., `nemoclaw-dns-probe-9c4f02a8b1d3e6f7.invalid`. Three properties make this resilient to the cache hit that masked #3630:

- The random suffix is never cached anywhere — Docker's embedded resolver, the host's stub resolver, and any upstream caching layer see a brand-new name on every probe and have to forward the query.
- Every compliant resolver returns NXDOMAIN immediately for any `.invalid` name (RFC 6761 §6.4), so the probe succeeds quickly when DNS works without depending on any specific A record being reachable from the container.
- NXDOMAIN is genuine round-trip evidence: the resolver received the query, decided it does not exist, and answered. If host egress is blocked, busybox prints `;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached` (the existing `servers_unreachable` signature) and the probe fails fast.

The success regex is widened to accept both shapes busybox emits:

1. `Server: ... / Name: <name> / Address: <ip>` for a real A-record resolution. Kept for back-compat with callers that pass a custom probe name resolving to a real IP.
2. `Server: ... / ** server can't find <name>: NXDOMAIN` for the `.invalid` probe sent by default.

The resolver-identification block (`Server: <ip> / Address: <ip>:53`) appears at the top of every busybox response, including malformed ones, so the new regex requires either a real `Name:` line OR an NXDOMAIN response body before declaring success. A regression test pins the malformed case (`;; reply from unexpected source: ...`) so this guard cannot quietly weaken.

## Related Issue

Closes #3630

## Changes

- `src/lib/onboard/preflight.ts`:
  - New `dnsProbeName()` helper returns a random `nemoclaw-dns-probe-<16-hex>.invalid` name (exported for the test seam; production callers never override).
  - `ProbeContainerDnsOpts` gains an optional `probeName?: string` to support pinned-name assertions in tests.
  - Probe command is now templated as `docker run --rm --pull=missing busybox:latest nslookup ${probeName} 2>&1`.
  - Success-path regex requires `^Server:` AND either `Name:`+`Address:` or `server can't find ... NXDOMAIN`.
- `src/lib/onboard/preflight.test.ts`:
  - The previous "NXDOMAIN → resolution_failed" assertion is replaced by "NXDOMAIN → ok" (the new contract).
  - New regression test for the malformed-response failure case (`;; reply from unexpected source: ...`).
  - New test for the random `.invalid` probe-name property (every call returns a distinct name matching the `nemoclaw-dns-probe-<16-hex>.invalid` shape).
  - New test for the `probeName` override seam.
  - Existing tests for the spawned command updated to assert the new `nslookup nemoclaw-dns-probe-<...>.invalid` prefix.

## Type of Change

- [x] Code change (feature, bug fix, or refactor)
- [ ] Code change with doc updates
- [ ] Doc only (prose changes, no code sample modifications)
- [ ] Doc only (includes code sample changes)

## Verification

- [x] `npx vitest run src/lib/onboard/preflight.test.ts -t "probeContainerDns"` — 18/18 pass
  - Existing success + servers_unreachable + image_pull_failed + no_output/error paths unchanged
  - New: NXDOMAIN-on-default-probe (the #3630 case) returns `ok: true`
  - New: malformed `;; reply from unexpected source` returns `resolution_failed`
  - New: `dnsProbeName()` returns distinct random `.invalid` names per call
  - New: `probeName` override is wired into the spawned script
- [x] Verified busybox output shapes on a working host:
  - DNS works + `.invalid` name: `Server: 192.168.65.7 / Address: 192.168.65.7:53 / ** server can't find <name>: NXDOMAIN`
  - DNS broken (via `--dns 240.0.0.0` to simulate the iptables DROP path): `;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached`
- [x] No regression in existing `Name: registry.npmjs.org` probe-output tests — the broader success regex still accepts the old shape for back-compat with custom probe names.

body:
Closes the long-standing CI failure on
`test_stage2_rederivation_noise_respects_global_seed`.

## Root cause

Not an RNG or NumPy issue. The realism layer caches its resolved
data source in module-level globals. Several tests in
`test_realism_fixture_fallback.py` legitimately set `_SOURCE = "none"`
via a monkeypatched fixture path; `monkeypatch` restores the path
attribute on teardown but doesn't clear the realism cache. The
seeding test then inherits `_SOURCE = "none"` and `adjust()` returns
its input unchanged — both seeds produce identical DataFrames, which
the test correctly reports as a seed-threading failure.

CI fails where the Windows dev env passes because
`test_realism_query_target.py`'s `realism_db` fixture teardown
incidentally calls `clear_cache()`, masking the leak locally. That
file is skipped on CI: it starts with
`pytest.importorskip("sqlalchemy")` and sqlalchemy lives in the
`[realism]` extra, not `[dev]` (which is what CI installs).
